📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This high-tech Huawei home battery pack hopes to hold back Tesla’s latest Powerwall with silicon carbide technology, AI-powered energy management baked in, and enough modular storage to keep even large homes bright and warm when the rest of the block goes dark.

Industry observers note that huawei believes its fresh Luterra S2 is more than just a home backup battery. The Chinese tech firm is calling it an “all-in-one residential energy system” that combines a hybrid inverter, modular battery storage, and AI-powered energy management in a single, simple, and stackable package that’s available in single-phase versions that put out between 3 and 10 kW and three-phase versions that can push up to 20 kW.

In a recent development, the Luterra S2 is the first system of its kind to use Huawei’s proprietary full-silicon carbide (SiC) architecture, which promises improved efficiency, power density, and ease of use. It’s so easy, in fact, that Huawei claims it can be installed and commissioned in just minutes.

“We are thrilled to introduce Huawei Luterra S2, our next-generation all-in-one residential energy system,” said Steve Zhang, President of Huawei Distributed PV & BESS Business. “By combining full-SiC architecture, AI-driven energy management, and industry-leading safety, Luterra S2 is designed to be smaller, lighter, quieter, safer, smarter and more powerful than ever before.”.

Recent findings suggest that huawei’s basic Luterra S2 configuration starts with “just” 5 kWh of battery energy storage and 3 kW of output. That’s enough to keep essential household appliances, lighting, and electronics running during a power outage, but you’ll want to keep going if you’re preparing for more than a day or two without power.

If that sounds like you, Luterra’s got you covered. The modular system can be expanded with modular 7 kWh LFP battery packs and can scaling up to a massive 336 kWh of total storage across interconnected systems, with inverter output peaking at an impressive 60 kW using three 20 kW units in parallel.

Keeping all that power cool and quiet is a Huawei-developed passive cooling system that does without external fans, keeping operating noise levels below a claimed 29 dB (about the same as my Mac mini). It operates at ambient temperatures from –25° C to about 60° C, and features a sturdy IP66-rated enclosure (safe to hit with a high-pressure hose) with corrosion protection up to C5-M to keep it from rusting away.

Nice, but no mention of price or European availability.

Alas, the Luterra S2 probably won’t be making its way to the US anytime soon – but fear not! 💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, audi has delayed the introduction of the electric A4 sedan by roughly one year, according to Autocar, which quotes an inside source at the German automaker.
  • The delay is reportedly tied to the Volkswagen Group’s worsening financial situation, software woes linked to the long-delayed Scalable Systems Platform (SSP), and Audi’s desire to make significant changes to the underbody of what should have been a common design across SSP-based electric sedans.
  • The current-generation Audi A5, which replaced the A4, is available with a plug-in hybrid powertrain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, audi has delayed the introduction of the electric A4 sedan by roughly one year, according to Autocar, which quotes an inside source at the German automaker. The electric A4, which was supposed to go into production at the company’s main plant in Ingolstadt in 2028, will go head-to-head with the BMW i3 and Mercedes-Benz C-Class EVs, which are already available in Europe.

The delay is reportedly tied to the Volkswagen Group’s worsening financial situation, software woes linked to the long-delayed Scalable Systems Platform (SSP), and Audi’s desire to make significant changes to the underbody of what should have been a common design across SSP-based electric sedans.

The current-generation Audi A5, which replaced the A4, is available with a plug-in hybrid powertrain.

According to recent reports, autocar’s source said that the premium German automaker requested bespoke footwells for both front and rear passengers instead of the completely flat floor that many purpose-built EVs use today. The reason behind this big demand reportedly has to do with the brand’s desire to deliver the packaging, seating position, and interior proportions that have traditionally been offered by the A4.

What’s more, the BMW i3 rival will supposedly use a 48-volt electrical system for its accessories instead of the traditional 12V setup that had been planned originally. Just like in the Tesla Cybertruck, adopting a higher-voltage system enables the automaker to use thinner-gauge wire and install higher-powered computers.

In a recent development, however, the changes come at a tough time for Audi’s parent organization, VW Group, which is ditching grandiose intends and doing everything it can to limit the cash bleeding. The upcoming Volkswagen ID. Golf, which is also based on the SSP architecture, has been delayed, leaving the marque with its current lineup of electric models until the end of the decade.

According to recent reports, for what it’s worth, the VW Group’s latest lineup of affordable EVs is doing very well in Europe, but the money problem persists. The organization can’t make them fast enough to keep up with demand, but building gas cars is still more profitable. This conundrum has put the German auto industry giant in a tough spot, where it’s trying to keep factories alive, but the importance of the vehicles that are right now being assembled there is slowly fading.

The first SSP-based cars were originally planned for 2026, but so far, not a single production model has been assembled.

Industry News: Mercedes-Benz Is Bringing Tesla-Like Semi-Autonomous Driving Systems to America

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (423 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, three years ago, Mercedes-Benz rolled out the first Level 3 autonomy system offered in the United States.
  • The hands-free system is limited to “eligible roads,” effectively making it a specialized feature for freeway use.
  • While both systems reach closer to true autonomous driving, their designation as SAE Level 2 systems mean that they are still nowhere near complete autonomy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, three years ago, Mercedes-Benz rolled out the first Level 3 autonomy system offered in the United States. That system is no longer available in the latest revision to the S-Class, with CTO Jörg Burzer calling it “early.” The brand still has advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) ambitions, though, and two new major products are arriving for a few customers starting next year. Mercedes-Benz has revealed prepares to launch both hands-free highway driving and hands-on point-to-point navigation in 2027, part of a continuing partnership with (scandal-laden) semiconductor superpower Nvidia. The latter system is subscription-only, although pricing for that subscription has yet to be revealed.

The hands-free system is limited to “eligible roads,” effectively making it a specialized feature for freeway use. It works up to 85 miles per hour, allowing a driver to take their hands off all inputs while the system handles highway driving and decision-making under the driver’s active supervision. Point-to-point navigation, on the other hand, is a hands-on system with more freedom. Like Tesla or Rivian’s similar offerings, it is intended to handle most of the workload of city driving and react in real time to the peculiarities of that task.

While both systems reach closer to true autonomous driving, their designation as SAE Level 2 systems mean that they are still nowhere near complete autonomy. That label means that they are meant to be seen as driver assistance systems only, leaving the person in the driver’s seat ultimately responsible for intervening before a problem occurs. The same is true of every autonomous solution at the moment on offer, including systems marketed as “Full Self-Driving” by Tesla.

Recent findings suggest that some California residents will receive the opportunity to try both systems starting in December; hands-free driving is expected to reach eligible cars more broadly in spring of 2027, while point-to-point navigation is made available nationwide at some point during the next year. Subscription pricing has not yet been announced, but brand representatives have suggested to Road & Track that it will be “competitive” with similar offerings from other automakers.

Mercedes allowed outlets, including Road & Track, to test both systems in San Francisco ahead of the news. You can read more about how the latest ADAS offerings fared here.

Latest Update: Check your ego at the door: Stellantis’ latest electric dolly turns ANY car into a tow rig

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We all know the type: grizzled stubble, wraparound PitVipers, a MAGA hat quietly retired after last week’s deep-blue shellacking, and a pristine, polished pickup parked in the driveway that they “need for towing.” With Stellantis’ new patent for an AI-powered electric tow dolly that turns just about ANY vehicle into a capable tow rig, however, those might need a new to find a new excuse to keep that gas-guzzler.
  • Originally filed in 2023, Stellantis received US Patent No.
  • Sources indicate that in other words, the dolly takes on many of the jobs that traditionally require a big tow vehicle: providing the pulling power, managing the trailer’s weight and controlling its braking and traction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We all know the type: grizzled stubble, wraparound PitVipers, a MAGA hat quietly retired after last week’s deep-blue shellacking, and a pristine, polished pickup parked in the driveway that they “need for towing.” With Stellantis’ new patent for an AI-powered electric tow dolly that turns just about ANY vehicle into a capable tow rig, however, those might need a new to find a new excuse to keep that gas-guzzler.

Originally filed in 2023, Stellantis received US Patent No. 12,779,916 for its electric tow dolly on 03NOV2026. The patent covers a machine that’s designed to shoulder the trailer’s hitch load with its own ball hitch or fifth-wheel plate, using an on-board electric motor and battery to get the trailer going while its regenerative braking system and AI-backed steering and traction control system keeps everything pointed in the right direction.

Sources indicate that in other words, the dolly takes on many of the jobs that traditionally require a big tow vehicle: providing the pulling power, managing the trailer’s weight and controlling its braking and traction. The vehicle up front doesn’t necessarily need a massive motor, heavy-duty suspension or oversized brakes. With a system like this, you could argue that the “tow vehicle” isn’t really a tow vehicle at all. It’s more of a “lead vehicle,” since the dolly is the one doing the towing … and it can follow just about anything – including the diminutive (and supremely affordable) Fiat 500e, which is also made by Stellantis.

To be clear, this isn’t just Uncle Jojo making fun of the commuter conveys – Stellantis’ patent describes the dolly as being equipped with an autonomous control system using cameras, sensors, a controller, and an advanced, four wheel steer-by-wire system. It also specifically discusses how the dolly’s independently powered acceleration, braking and steering, and sway controls essentially remove the need to own a truck in the first place.

The dolly system’s truck bed sides and small size allow owners to experience the functionality and utility of a truck only when they need it, allowing them to own a smaller, cheaper, and more fuel efficient vehicle that suits daily use needs.

There are some pretty obvious practical questions still to answer, of course, including how much battery capacity the dolly would need, how much weight it could handle and how it would perform on long grades or in emergency braking situations. And, to be clear, a patent isn’t a product announcement or proof that Stellantis looks to put one of these things on sale – heck, if I were Stellantis’ CEO, I’d patent this thing just to prevent anyone else from building one so I could keep selling ancient, low-tech, high-margin Ram Trucks – but it’s a neat idea.

Okay, I like this idea and appreciate the problem it is trying to solve, but it has the same challenge as any electric-tow situation, which is the charging logistics. Even if you find a pull-through charger (very rare), if you are using an EV, you still need to charge two "vehicles," so you have to charge your car, then pull up and charge the dolly afterwards. Even if you are using a gas car, charging the dolly will be logistically challenging. Of course, that's a problem with an easy solution (more pull-through chargers), but also one that doesn't seem to be on any charging network's radar.

Sources indicate that I think it’s neat, anyway. What do you guys think? Are you ready to trade in your significant-battery Chevy Silverado EV or Volvo VNR 800 on a newly introduced Topolino, or are you going to keep driving inefficient 99% of the time? Let us know, in the comments.

SOURCE: Stellantis, via Mopar Insiders.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article is part of a mental health content series called “Mind Games,” in which Healthline editor Morgan Mandriota draws on personal experience and research to challenge misconceptions, reduce stigma, review trends, and share hot takes and lessons learned about what it means to be mentally well.

Coffee and I don’t exactly have the best relationship.

In a recent development, my morning cup tends to give me jitters, worsen my anxiety, and keep me up until 2 a.m. if I drink it past noon. As an already anxious human, the last thing I need is to exacerbate my symptoms, even if it’s coming from a delicious source.

Recent findings suggest that over a year ago, I noticed that my anxiety was higher than usual. I was also tossing and turning and waking up at all hours of the night for weeks on end.

One night in particular, I woke up every hour for 8 hours. Naturally, I wanted to blame it on the full moon or anything other than my beloved coffee, but alas, I realized that my caffeine consumption was the most likely culprit.

Industry observers note that could I have aimed to set a strict drinking schedule to see if that fixed things? Sure. But instead, I decided to quit cold turkey and undergo an experiment to see how I’d feel going coffee-free for the first time in years.

Industry observers note that over the next 8 months, I’d swap my coffee station for a matcha setup, dabble in exotic herbal blends from my local teahouse, and become a self-proclaimed tea connoisseur. Lo and behold, my anxiety eased up, and my sleep quality improved, too.

According to recent reports, fast forward to 4 months ago, when I hopped back on the coffee train. But this time, I’m relying on a handy amino acid to help avoid anxiety and other unwanted side effects: L-theanine.

In a recent development, health and wellness touch everyone’s life differently. This is one person’s story. The views and opinions expressed are those of the speaker and do not necessarily reflect the views or positions of Healthline Media and should not serve as a substitute for medical advice from a healthcare professional.

It has been revealed that L-theanine is mainly found in green and black tea and one type of wild mushroom. The mental health benefits of L-theanine consumption are an emerging area of research, but one 2024 review found that consuming around 200 to 400 milligrams (mg) may help relieve symptoms in people with anxiety disorders.

Still, anecdotal reports suggest there may be benefits of adding L-theanine to coffee. Over the last 5 years, the combo has been gaining traction on Reddit and TikTok for managing caffeine-related side effects.

Despite an overwhelming amount of rave reviews online, I couldn’t find much research to support these claims, so I spoke with a neurologist to see if they had any thoughts.

“This trend has real science behind it,” stated Fawad Mian, MD, who is board certified in neurology, clinical neurophysiology, and sleep medicine and the founder of Ascend Regenerative.

In a recent development, “Controlled studies show caffeine plus L-theanine improves focus and attention more than caffeine alone, and some suggest it softens caffeine’s side effects, like tiredness, headaches, and blood pressure spikes,” Mian mentioned. “It smooths caffeine’s effects but doesn’t erase them, so it’s not a license to drink more coffee,” he added.

With all of this in mind, especially after realizing just how calm I was while drinking black and green teas during my coffee break, I decided to give it a try.

After about 4 months of “testing,” I’ve found that adding L-theanine to my coffee works extremely well for me.

It has been revealed that no more anxiety, scatterbrain, shakiness, or staying up until 3 a.m. And no lifestyle overhaul needed. The supplement, which I prefer in liquid form, has become a seamless addition to my daily routine.

Every morning, I make a fresh batch of French press coffee with (strong) local beans, then I squeeze some L-theanine into my cup.

I’ve noticed that I get the usual coffee benefits like improved focus and concentration, plus a nice, calm, stable energy throughout the day.

Even if I drink it until 2 p.m., I’m fighting to keep my eyes open at night before I finally fall asleep around 10. Perhaps this is because L-theanine may also support quality sleep.

Mindful L-Theanine Drops is the liquid supplement that I use every day.

I add a one-second squeeze (which contains 200 mg of L-theanine) into my morning coffee, then I’m good to go. I even started carrying a bottle in my bag just in case I get a latte from a coffee shop on a whim.

You can also add it to a glass of water, a cup of tea, or another drink of your choosing. It’s unflavored, so it doesn’t alter the taste of your drinks. Real secret stuff.

Out of curiosity, and because I’m a natural skeptic and overthinker, I asked Mian if my positive experience could be a placebo effect, or if I’m seeing real results.

It has been revealed that “Expectation may play a small role, but the effect is biologically plausible,” he said. “L-theanine boosts calming brain activity that offsets caffeine’s stimulation, and 200 mg matches the doses used in studies.” However, he noted that it doesn’t speed caffeine clearance, so drinking coffee only in the morning still matters for sleep quality.

While L-theanine is generally safe to consume, it’s best to speak with a healthcare professional first, especially if you’re pregnant, nursing, receiving cancer treatment, or taking blood pressure medication or sedatives.

“Choose a third-party tested brand, and if caffeine makes you anxious, cutting back is still the simplest fix,” Mian added.

In a recent development, so, if you’re anything like me and drinking coffee also leads to anxiety and jitters for you, I highly recommend trying this supplement once you get the green light from your doctor. It’s been working for me. It may work well for you, too.

Peeping woodcocks are evolutionary oddballs

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (506 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet.
  • It has been revealed that woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances.
  • “The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, stated in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet. You’ve probably seen at least a few videos of the birds on social media darting across beaches and being incredibly vocal. As if their small, squat bodies and comically long beaks weren’t enough, they also vocalize with distinctively cartoonish peeping tweets during their mating displays.

It has been revealed that woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances. Six of the eight species are only found on specific islands, and some of them don’t even migrate at all. So how did these evolutionary oddballs even get their start—and stop migrating? To piece together their unique avian story, biologists analyzed the DNA of all eight woodcock species and 22 species of snipe.

“The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, stated in a statement. “They’re not terribly aerodynamic, and yet they’ve clearly gotten around.”.

Bates and his colleagues published the results of their work today in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS). The years-long endeavor involved not only examining preserved woodcock specimens housed in the Field Museum, but a fossilized sandpiper previously excavated from a cave site in Haiti. The remains found on the island of Hispaniola are around 1,000 years old, but that is still extremely young in the grand history of shorebirds.

The earliest members of the sandpiper family began in the northern hemisphere before slowly migrating to islands along lower latitudes. Those birds subsequently migrated much shorter distances after settling in the warmer climates. However, they didn’t remain sedentary. Based on the DNA analysis detailed in their study, Bates and his team theorize that snipes from Africa eventually traveled across the Atlantic Ocean, then evolved into new species in South America. From there, more of the birds made their way over the Pacific Ocean to New Zealand.

Industry observers note that their examinations also cleared up a bit of confusion. Biologists initially believed the fossilized sandpiper from Haiti was a woodcock, but the most recent data now shows that it’s a snipe.

“Snipes and woodcocks have been around for 20 to 25 million years,” Bates explained. “Over that time, as new species have evolved and moved around the world, their migratory patterns have changed, too.”.

These changes are likely to continue amid today’s dramatic climate shifts, but that may pose a problem for the beloved woodcocks.

“These are definitely birds that would be affected by changing habitats and changing climates,” stated Bates. “Some of these woodcocks are found only in the mountain forests on islands between Asia and Australia, and if those forests get cut down, the birds are going to be gone too.”.

Ford only just launched the Mustang Dark Horse SC earlier this year, but the Blue Oval brand isn’t letting up when it comes to high-performance versions of its iconic pony car. While the S650-generation Mustang introduced the new Dark Horse branding—at the expense of the legendary Shelby nameplate—and saw the arrival of the new $300,000-plus GTD, Ford’s upcoming Mustang variant revives a famous name from the past: Cobra. The new Mustang Cobra is expected to slot between the Dark Horse and Dark Horse SC as an indirect successor to the last Shelby GT350, providing track-ready performance and high-fidelity driver engagement.

Industry observers note that the Shelby GT350, offered from 2015–2020, is considered one of the best Mustangs ever, thanks to its naturally aspirated flat-plane-crank 5.2-liter V-8 known as Voodoo. The last Cobra is also coveted by Mustang fans, so the latest track-focused model has big shoes to fill. And with a new engine most likely under the Cobra’s hood, there’s potential for another legendary Mustang to be born.

See all results for new 2028 Ford Mustang for sale near 61938.

In a recent development, the Cobra will continue to utilize the S650 platform, itself an evolution of the S550 chassis that underpinned the Mustang from 2015–2023. The Cobra will adapt the Mustang into a dedicated track car, and we think it will also spawn a more hardcore Cobra R with even more extreme aerodynamics, stronger brakes, and greater weight savings, potentially even removing the backseat. We expect the Cobra’s bodywork to be based on the Dark Horse SC, but with small tweaks and possibly a rear wing that harkens back to the 2000 Cobra R.

It has been revealed that mustang fans are obviously clamoring for the return of the Voodoo, but we don’t think that’s what Ford has in store. Fret not, however, because the automaker is cooking up something special for the newly introduced Cobra.

Instead of the 5.2-liter Voodoo, the new Cobra will pack a naturally aspirated 5.4-liter engine derived from the Mustang GT3 race car that has triumphed at the 24 Hours of Daytona and secured a podium at Le Mans. The Coyote-based GT3 engine features a cross-plane crank, but the teaser video released by Ford emitted a high-revving scream, so there’s a chance that the Cobra’s engine will switch to a flat-plane-crank setup. Still, if you’ve recently been to an IMSA race, you’ll know the GT3 car produces a thunderous soundtrack, so enthusiasts are in for an auditory treat regardless.

Although Ford hasn’t confirmed that the Cobra will adapt the GT3 race car’s engine, in the first teaser it said the car would pack a “heart born from racing.” We don’t expect the Cobra to come close to the Dark Horse SC or GTD in terms of power, but we wouldn’t be shocked if the 5.4-liter V-8 exceeds the 550 horsepower that the GT3 car is restricted to by racing regulations.

See all results for upcoming 2028 Ford Mustang for sale near 61938.

Recent findings suggest that better yet, the new 5.4-liter V-8 will be paired with a six-speed manual for maximum driver engagement. We think Ford will likely employ the Tremec TR-3160 transmission already used in the Dark Horse.

Industry observers note that at the moment, the Mustang has the V-8 muscle car world all to itself. Dodge is expected to stuff a supercharged V-8 back into the Charger for the 2028 model year, while Chevy is gearing up to bring back the Camaro around 2028. The only other V-8-powered car under $100,000 is the Corvette, which has a completely different form factor with its mid-engine layout, but it will likely still be cross-shopped against the Cobra.

Pricing is probably the biggest risk. Ford needs to make sure it doesn’t alienate its customers by making it too expensive, given that the Dark Horse SC already has a hefty $105,585 asking price (about $20K more than the GT500 that it replaced). The new 5.4-liter V-8 will also have to make a strong impression as a successor to the much-loved Voodoo.

The Mustang Cobra will likely be revealed in early 2027 and go on sale before the end of the year. We expect pricing to start somewhere in the $80,000 range, but it could easily climb to $100,000 for a Cobra R model.

It has been revealed that the Volkswagen ID. Buzz hasn't exactly been a smash hit in the U.S. But that hasn't stopped commercial customers from eyeing up the nostalgic electric van for something it's particularly good at: moving people.

May Mobility revealed on Thursday that it looks to integrate its autonomous driving systems into the Buzz to give it a job wherever driverless taxis are welcome.

May wants to use its existing tech stack to equip up to the ID. Buzzes with hardware and software that can see "up to 10 seconds into the future.".

Well, kind of—May's tech uses onboard predictive modeling to anticipate how the world around it will move, similar how a human assess other drivers around them. It creates multiple scenarios in its digital brain and uses the model's reasoning to determine which one is most suited for its environment.

The tech would also make the cars capable of integrating with any of the "global robotaxi platforms," which is one of the ways that May is approaching its partnership-first business model. Presumably, that means its existing fleet partners like Lyft, Uber, and other ride hailing services around the world.

May's approach is also a silent win for folks who want to make sure that Buzz doesn't fizzle out.

According to recent reports, one of the biggest blockers to Buzz adoption on the consumer side has been the price. While that could change in the coming months, the van's initially high price tag and just so-so range made it a fairly lukewarm offering to EV buyers looking to park the Buzz in their own driveway. That's why Robotaxis might be the best use of the Buzz yet.

Recent findings suggest that it's roomy enough to comfortably haul plenty of passengers (and whatever cargo they bring along), plus it has the easy ingress and egress of a minivan. Other companies seem to agree, even VW's own MOIA arm that recently began testing an autonomous version of the Buzz in Los Angeles.

In a recent development, so far, May has completed about 600,000 commercial driverless rides in the U.S. and Japan. And while it hasn't noted how many cars it operates, May is pretty open about its long-term goal for the Buzz.

It plans to put 10,000 of these autonomous ID. Buzzes on the road by 2031. That all starts with road testing early next year, followed by delivering the first fleet vehicles to customers by 2028.

BMW just unearthed something exceedingly cool from its cellars, something that we never even knew existed: a BMW M7 Prototype.

Revealed via a post on BMW Classic’s Instagram and brought to broader attention to BMWBlog, the video gives us our first look ever at this performance sedan that never was. Conceived in the late 1990s, this 7-Series started life out as a 1997 BMW 740i; BMW then swapped in the 4.9-liter naturally aspirated V-8 from the E39 M5, imbuing it with 400 horsepower.

Sources indicate that not only does it have the M5’s engine, but BMW also paired the motor with a six-speed manual transmission. BMW notes the M7 Prototype has a top speed of 155 mph and weighs 4134 pounds. Unfortunately, that’s when the details begin to fall off, and we’re left to observe—or guess—any other info.

Industry observers note that being an M7 Prototype, we suspect BMW went all-out in its M endeavors. That would mean a far sportier chassis alongside larger wheels and tires. This prototype is fitted with BBS wheels, giving it a notably more aggressive stance and look than your typical 740i. The car’s design itself remains understated, making sure to maintain its 7-Series elegance; that said, the rear bumper is modified to make room for the quad exhaust tips you’d see poking out the rear of the E39 M5. No 7-Series from this era featured such an outwardly aggressive exhaust exit, making it one of the few standout exterior changes to this car.

Sources indicate that BMW also upholstered the interior with a classy tan and black two-tone. The six-speed shifter is integrated cleanly with the center console. It has a three-spoke M steering wheel, and the cluster is an M unit borrowed from the E39 M5 as well. Suffice it to say, we’re a little sad the company never brought this to production.

  • The United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) confiscated the orange-fronted conures during three separate operations over the last 17 months, and the white-fronted Amazons in the last several months.
  • According to recent reports, “These animals were stolen from the wild and are victims of the illegal wildlife pet trade, and our responsibility is to give them the best possible chance for a healthy future,” Chuck Cerbini, WCS Bronx Zoo Curator of Ornithology, remarked in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the past 17 months, the Wildlife Conservation Society’s Bronx Zoo in Fresh York City has rescued dozens of parrots from the illegal pet trade. They include white-fronted Amazons (Amazona albifrons) and orange-fronted conures (Eupsittula canicularis).

The United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) confiscated the orange-fronted conures during three separate operations over the last 17 months, and the white-fronted Amazons in the last several months. All of the birds were discovered at the U.S.–Mexico border.

According to recent reports, “These animals were stolen from the wild and are victims of the illegal wildlife pet trade, and our responsibility is to give them the best possible chance for a healthy future,” Chuck Cerbini, WCS Bronx Zoo Curator of Ornithology, remarked in a statement. “Working with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, our veterinary and animal care teams provide specialized expertise to assess, treat, and care for confiscated wildlife.”.

When confiscated wildlife arrives at the Bronx Zoo, the veterinary and animal care teams first conduct a health check, provide any necessary medical treatment, and then help find long-term placements for those that can’t be released into the wild.

White-fronted Amazons are native to parts of Mexico and Central America and represent the smallest Amazon parrot. They are also one of the few parrot species in which males and females feature visibly different plumage. Both sexes have a white foreheads, red faces, and yellowish bills, but males have red shoulders and females have green shoulders.

Sources indicate that orange-fronted conures, also known as half-moon conure or Petz’s conure, are also native to parts of Mexico and Central America, where they live in open woodlands, forest edges, and savannas. They have an orange forehead and green and blue feathers.

The IUCN Red List categorizes both birds as a species of Least Concern, but that still  doesn’t justify trafficking them in the illegal pet trade. Parrots throughout Latin America are subject to both the loss of forest habitat and poaching.

Birds in particular l are especially threatened by trafficking because they are valued in the pet trade and the collector trade.

Tesla Opens Self-Driving Cybercab Orders To 'Select Customers' At $29,990

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla will soon start selling its steering wheel-free Cybercab for personal use, the firm declared on Friday.
  • The Cybercab will cost $29,990, undercutting the Model 3 by $7,000 and making the golden two-seater Tesla's cheapest vehicle ever.
  • The Cybercab won't operate anywhere in the country, Tesla says, but rather in "supported service areas." It will also require a $299-per-month autonomous driving subscription to operate, with the first month included for no charge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla will soon start selling its steering wheel-free Cybercab for personal use, the firm declared on Friday.

The Cybercab will cost $29,990, undercutting the Model 3 by $7,000 and making the golden two-seater Tesla's cheapest vehicle ever. According to a screenshot of the order page shared by Tesla, deliveries will begin as soon as next month.

There are a few catches. The Cybercab won't operate anywhere in the country, Tesla says, but rather in "supported service areas." It will also require a $299-per-month autonomous driving subscription to operate, with the first month included for no charge. That totals to some $3,600 per year just to use the vehicle, before insurance or maintenance costs.

Industry observers note that and the model will be sold to hand-picked buyers, at least to start. "Select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use," the company remarked in a tweet on its Robotaxi X account. Tesla said initial availability is limited.

It's not clear when or if sales will expand to the general public. But the sale of a car one can actually own that is capable of driving itself without supervision would be a massive milestone for both the automotive world and for Tesla in particular.

It has been revealed that putting autonomous cars in the hands of regular people has been one of Elon Musk's central promises for about a decade, and he's missed his self-imposed deadlines year after year. Meanwhile, today's driverless cars are owned and operated by companies running ride-hailing services, like Waymo, Zoox, and Tesla—not by individuals. The Cybercabs in operation today are part of Tesla's Robotaxi service, which opened for business last year and now shuttles riders around in a handful of U.S. cities, including Austin and Miami.

Industry observers note that tesla's biggest boosters online cheered the news. But it's also sure to tick off some of the many Tesla owners who have paid for Full Self-Driving over the years and have been waiting patiently for their Model 3s and Model Ys to become autonomous. Most recently, Musk stated that will happen in the second quarter of next year in areas where the Robotaxi service operates.

The Tesla Cybercab has two seats and no steering wheel or pedals.

Tesla is far from the only company looking to sell autonomous cars to the public someday. Rivian plans to introduce lidar and a new in-house chip to the R2 in the hopes of giving it self-driving capability someday. General Motors plans to introduce an eyes-off version of Super Cruise to the Cadillac Escalade IQ in 2028. It'll operate on highways first before expanding to other road types, GM claims.

According to recent reports, tesla advertises the personally-owned Cybercab as "fully autonomous" and notes owners will be able to monitor their vehicles and manage rides via the Tesla app. But overall, the announcement raises almost as many questions as it answers.

In a recent development, for example, there was no mention of whether customers would be able to add their cabs to the Robotaxi fleet and earn passive income, another longtime Musk promise. It's also not clear where the Cybercab will be able to operate, nor whether Tesla will expand that territory quickly enough to make buying one worthwhile beyond a handful of cities.

It has been revealed that another cloud of uncertainty looming over the Cybercab's rollout is regulatory in nature. The Cybercab's unconventional design has caught the attention of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, which questions how exactly Tesla determined that the vehicle complies with motor vehicle safety standards. The Tesla lacks a steering wheel, pedals, and side-view mirrors, all things that are typically required for a car to be street-legal.

The federal government lets companies apply to roll out noncompliant vehicles, but those deployments are capped at 2,500 vehicles per year. (Zoox, for its part, was recently granted an exemption to commercially deploy 5,000 of its autonomous pods over two years.) NHTSA has said it's working to streamline autonomous-vehicle rules, which could work in Tesla's favor here.

Sources indicate that if Tesla can pull this off, it'll be one for the history books. Of course, the manufacturer has made numerous ambitious promises around self-driving cars—like 1 million robotaxis by 2020, and unsupervised self-driving pretty much every year since—and it has generally fallen short. Whether the Cybercab rollout breaks that streak is still to be determined.

Industry observers note that your typical 2023 BMW M2 has an electronically limited top speed of 155 miles per hour. However, the optional M Driver's Package raises that limit to 177 mph. According to the Arizona Department of Public Safety (AZDPS) Highway Patrol, one M2 driver was apparently determined to explore the upper limits of his car's performance before trading it in; a state trooper clocked him traveling 170 mph on the highway, and criminal charges followed.

In a recent development, the incident happened on November 9, 2026, on Arizona State Route 202 near Sky Harbor Boulevard in Tempe, Arizona. According to authorities, an AZDPS Highway Patrol State Trooper spotted the BMW traveling at a high rate of speed and passing other vehicles. Using a LIDAR device, the trooper reportedly recorded the vehicle traveling 170 mph in a posted 65-mph zone—an astonishing 105 mph over the limit.

Recent findings suggest that police were not going to engage in a pursuit at that speed, however, and said they decided to use the Highway Patrol Traffic Operations Center to track the vehicle's whereabouts. Eventually the BMW exited the highway, and police were then able to stop the car. At this time, the police reportedly noticed that the BMW didn’t have a license plate.

It has been revealed that police say the officer asked the driver how fast he thought he was going, and the man estimated his speed at approximately 110 to 115 mph. That's still far above the posted speed limit, but nowhere near the 170 mph that had him approaching Daytona 500 qualifying territory. The driver later claimed he hadn't realized just how fast he was traveling, according to authorities.

It has been revealed that why was he driving so fast? He reportedly told the trooper he was planning to trade in the BMW and wanted to take it for one last drive. Hopefully his newly introduced car will be slower than the M2, because as police pointed out in their social media post, at 170 mph, the BMW was traveling approximately 250 feet every second. A crash at that speed would be devastating.

The driver was, unsurprisingly, arrested for reckless driving and endangerment, due to his excessive speed and unsafe driving behavior.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that one of the rarest and most coveted coins in United States history is headed for the auction block this week, where it could sell for over $2 million. But while collectors have long dreamed about owning one of the five existing 1885 silver trade dollars, the strange story of their creation remains murky more than 140 years after their minting.

In a recent development, the U.S. struck the first trade dollars in 1873 as a way to compete with similar silver coinage in East Asia, but the production was short-lived. Silver market fluctuations and foreign policy shifts led to their demonetization in 1876, and they were only minted for collectors beginning in 1879. By 1884, the U.S. commissioned only 10 trade dollars before finally retiring the series destroying the die casts.

Recent findings suggest that however, a thoroughly corrupt political appointee named A. Loudon Snowden had other intends. Snowden’s career in currencies began in 1857, when his uncle and former Treasurer of Pennsylvania hired the then 22-year-old whippersnapper at the Philadelphia Mint. While at the mint, he pursued various personal profiteering interests, including the clandestine production and selling of thousands of rare coins for collectors.In 1885, Snowden finally retired as Superintendent of the Philadelphia Mint after nearly three decades.

Recent findings suggest that snowden also gave himself a parting gift before retiring—five 1885 trade dollars that he purchased from the Mint cashier. No one knew of their existence until a year after Snowden’s death in 1912. The first 1885 trade dollar auctioned in 1913 for $1,140 (about $32,174 in current valuation).

Sources indicate that although some numismatists and historians argue Snowden’s five trade dollars were a final grift, other experts argue that the coins have a surprisingly mundane backstory. Until the 1930’s, Mint employees were legally allowed to purchase examples of latest coinage for their equivalent amount. Snowden did just this when he previously bought 10 proof 1884 trade dollars, and it’s possible he bought the following year’s coins before the decision not to mint any others. Regardless of the true story, only five 1885 trade dollars exist today—and they’re worth far more than Snowden could ever imagine.

Stack’s Bowers will auction the 1885 trade dollar as part of its Rarities Night series on Tuesday, November 17.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dongfeng Nissan officially opened the early order book on its fresh NX7 hybrid yesterday, promising up to 320 km (~198 miles) of all-electric range from a 40 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery and a $20,000 price tag.

When the first generation Nissan LEAF bowed with 70-ish miles of range from its 24 kWh li-ion battery pack, it struggled to meet widespread adoption, especially in an SUV-obsessed US market that demands forethought-free trips to Home Depot and bladder-busting range. The firm’s latest 2027 Rogue Hybrid is a step in the right direction, using a gas engine to generate electricity for a pair of electric drive motors that deliver a driving experience that’s remarkably similar to a “pure” electric car – but without a plug, it’s still entirely dependent on fossil fuels. The new Dongfeng Nissan NX7, though? That’s a different story.

It has been revealed that the plug-in hybrid Dongfeng Nissan NX7 might be called a “long range hybrid” in the same sense that Volvo’s Euro-market XC70 is, in that it’s an EV for the 360-odd days a year that you’re driving less than 200 miles, and an ICE vehicle for the handful of days you drive more. And if you’re one of those people who thinks stopping on road trips is a character flaw, a fully charged and topped off NX7 will take you an astonishing 1,666 km (~1,035 miles) from where you started.

The upcoming NX7 could be an ideal lilypad vehicle for North American drivers who are either too afraid of being caught without a charger or too invested in the outcome of one or more dumb oil wars to confidently make the switch to EV – and, even at twice the 129,900 yuan ($~19,400) asking price, I think it would be a hit.

For that money, NX7 buyers get an absolutely loaded Model Y-sized crossover (they’re within 1/4″ of each other in length), with a 17.3″ central touchscreen, a fully digital instrument cluster, and (on higher-spec models) a positively massive 55″ augmented-reality head-up display powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8295P automotive processor and running on Nissan OS 3.0 with an AI-powered voice assistant developed with iFlytek that, Nissan claims, can recognize natural-language commands, remember user preferences, and even recognize occupants, adjusting vehicle settings accordingly.

Sources indicate that on top-shelf models, the NX7 cabins get “AI Zero-Pressure Cloud Blanket” seats that use sensors and air-cushion arrays to dynamically adjust for maximum comfort, and include heating, ventilation, and a 12-point SPA-level massage function. The front seats can be fully reclined to create a bed-like configuration that will be familiar to Cube owners. The NX7 even offers an on-board refrigerator and motion-sickness prevention system that Nissan claims can reduce motion sickness by as much as 83% (which, like, I wouldn’t want to be the one to test that – but seems cool).

Power comes from a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated internal combustion engine making 98 hp that’s paired to a 228 hp electric drive motor and the previously mentioned 40.9 kWh LFP battery. It’s not immediately clear if the NX7 uses a conventional parallel hybrid system like a Prius or a series-hybrid-plus-plug setup, but Dongfeng’s hybrid technology patents describe a pretty versatile arrangement with four possible operating modes: series hybrid, parallel hybrid, direct engine drive and electricity generation – which means the vehicle can theoretically use the ICE motor as a generator, drive the wheels mechanically, or work alongside the electric motor, depending on what the operating conditions call for. Whether any or all four modes make it to production on the NX7 remains to be seen, but it’s an intriguing bit of engineering for a vehicle promising nearly 200 miles of electric driving range.

PHEV. With 200miles of range. More than decent, but for the most part what I would have loved in 2015. Less so now.

Still, for the price that is very decent electric range. And it looks good too.

The final production version will be shown to the public for the first time at the Guangzhou Auto Show later this month, but you can let us know what you think of the newly introduced NX7 in the comments, today.

Internet-famous bald eagle Shadow has endured an up-and-down 2026. From suffering the loss of a clutch of eggs to welcoming two chicks, and from losing his longtime partner to finding a new friend, he’s had a tumultuous year.

After the August death of Jackie, the female eagle he raised chicks with since 2018, Shadow began spending time with a 4-year-old female eagle named Kaydee (formerly KD1). Viewers of the 24/7 livestream of Shadow’s nest could easily spot Kaydee because of her double-banded legs—a silver ring on one leg and a lavender one on the other. The pair appeared chummy as they spent more time together, sharing stick-arranging duties, singing, and exchanging beaky kisses. An unexpected twist arrived this week with the appearance of an unknown female bald eagle spotted in the nest with Shadow.

Cameras spotted the unknown female in the nest in recent weeks, but this was the first time the eagle was joined by Shadow. On Monday afternoon, Shadow landed in the nest quickly followed by the unknown female. The unknown female fiddled the nest sticks while vocalizing and Shadow appeared unbothered by her presence. Eagles will typically defend their nest from intruders so Shadow’s willingness to share his space with an eagle other than Kaydee surprised many viewers.

Shadow returned the nest solo later in the afternoon as the sun set over Big Bear Lake.

As this is nature, all we can do is sit back and see what unfolds. Mating season is approaching, so we have to wait and see if Shadow selects a new partner. Female eagles in Significant Bear Valley typically lay their first clutch of eggs in January. Tune in to Friends of Big Bear Valley’s (FOBBV) livestreams to follow the southern California eagles anytime.

In a recent development, kaydee, formerly known as KD1, is a banded female bald eagle that has been spotted in Big Bear Valley following the death of Shadow’s former partner, Jackie. She was born in 2022, about 70 miles away from Big Bear Lake in the Prado Basin between Anaheim and Riverside, California. Coincidentally, her parents are also named Lucky and Ricky like Jackie’s parents, but they are a different eagle pair.

In a recent development, kaydee was banded as part of the Orange County Water District’s work to track the eagles born in the area. These bands help biologists track and monitor the birds over time. Kaydee right now has a black spot on her head, but it may not be permanent. It’s possible that not all of her white feathers have come in or it could be tree sap or dirt. She also has two small bands on her legs. One is a small metal band, while the other is a lavender band with “KD1” on it.

Kaydee is almost five years old, so she is just about ready to mate. She was recently spotted on FOBBV’s livestream inspecting the nest and has also been seen hanging out near Shadow. Flying around Major Bear is completely normal behavior for young adult eagles at this time of year.

Recent findings suggest that in January, Jackie laid two eggs in the nest, but ravens destroyed them. She later laid two more eggs that hatched in April and named Luna and Sandy. The name Sandy is in honor of FOBBV’s former executive director Sandy Steers who died from cancer in February.

Sources indicate that on July 17, Jackie was found injured on the ground near Dana Point Park, California. Cell phone video from a witness confirmed that she had an altercation with two other subadult eagles. She successfully fended off the other eagles by turning over and using her talons, but could not fly far away.

She was transferred to the Ojai Raptor Center for care, where she was diagnosed with severe anemia. Her anemia worsened during the first week of August, the Ojai Raptor Center remarked that she was in unstable condition on August 9. Her packed cell volume (PCV) fell below percent, before rising to nine percent. Jackie died early in the morning on August 10. The necropsy did not reveal a single cause of death, and instead pointed to several factors including severe anemia, bird flu, blood clots in her wing and one kidney, and liver and lung abnormalities.

A memorial service was held on September 5 in Fawnskin, California, along with a second celebration of life called Wings Over Big Bear on October 3. The event featured representatives from FOBBV, the Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation, and more.

Honda’s automatic engine start-stop feature is under upcoming federal scrutiny, after the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration received hundreds of complaints that engines failed to restart automatically from a complete stop at a traffic light on certain models, prompting the agency to commence an investigation.

In a recent development, the federal probe, declared on Friday, November 13, includes 1.03 million units of the 2024-2026 Honda Passport, Odyssey, Pilot, and Ridgeline. The inquiry also includes 2024-2026 Acura MDX units. NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation received 701 complaints related to the Auto Start/Stop feature.

It has been revealed that “To help improve fuel efficiency, the Auto Start/Stop system will automatically shut off the engine when a vehicle comes to a complete stop. The engine is intended to automatically restart when a driver releases the brake pedal. However, the complaints allege that the engines are failing to restart once they have been shut off by this system,” the investigation announcement reads.

Industry observers note that while automatic start-stop systems were created to improve fuel economy, Honda seems to be having a recurring issue with the feature. Federal safety regulators previously opened a probe into Honda’s automatic start-stop system in 2025. That investigation included 2.2 million late-model Honda Pilot, Odyssey, Passport, and Ridgeline models, as well as Acura MDX and TLX units. However, the newly introduced investigation includes 2026 model-year units. Inquiry documents allege that the two issue populations have different root causes and respond differently to repairs.

There have been no injuries related to this issue, according to the feds. EPA boss Lee Zeldin stated the agency was investigating improvements or eliminating the technology last year; whether it sticks around in the long run, however, an engineering analysis of the stop-start system should bring Honda and NHTSA together to identify an effective solution to this recurring problem soon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, high gas prices have helped drive more interest in electric cars this year.
  • Eye-watering diesel costs are pushing more shippers to consider a switch to electric trucks, Roozbeh Charli, CEO of electric and autonomous freight organization Einride, told me in an interview.
  • “You’re definitely seeing an upswing in both customer conversations and just general narrative” around electrification, he said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, high gas prices have helped drive more interest in electric cars this year. But it’s not just everyday drivers who are looking to ditch fossil fuels.

Eye-watering diesel costs are pushing more shippers to consider a switch to electric trucks, Roozbeh Charli, CEO of electric and autonomous freight organization Einride, told me in an interview.

“You’re definitely seeing an upswing in both customer conversations and just general narrative” around electrification, he said.

Diesel prices have risen far more severely than prices for regular gasoline, putting extra pressure on commercial operators. The average cost of diesel in the U.S. has shot up by more than 60% since the war with Iran began, to over $6 per gallon. Shippers are facing far higher fuel costs in Europe too. It all means customers who told Einride they’d revisit the idea of electric freight sometime down the line are deciding to get the ball rolling.

“A lot of those customers are coming back now, saying ‘let’s get started, rather sooner than later,’” Charli noted.

It has been revealed that there’s some evidence that those conversations are generating actual business. Einride, which was founded in 2016 and sells electric freight services and software, claims its sales pipeline tripled year over year during the first half of 2026. Its conversion rate doubled over the same period.

Sources indicate that and it isn’t the only one noticing an uptick in demand. In September, a coalition of shippers like PepsiCo placed an order for 2,500 electric trucks in a deal that’s set to double the U.S. fleet of electric Class 8 trucks. Catalyst Mobility, one of the nonprofits running the program, has stated it’s noticed more interest in EV trucks from companies that weren’t involved in the deal due to diesel prices.

It has been revealed that charli chalks the increased interest up to a couple of things. The pricing pain today is part of it. It means there’s a broader range of customer use cases where electric trucks are price-competitive with, or cheaper than, using traditional substantial-rigs. Those are typically what he calls “middle-mile” applications of, say, 100-200 miles back and forth, with high utilization. That last part is key, since battery-powered trucks still tend to cost more than diesel ones.

The situation is also making some companies realize just how exposed they are to drastic swings in the price of diesel, Charli mentioned.

Our weekly newsletter breaks down the biggest mobility news every Friday.

Recent findings suggest that the trend is encouraging for reasons beyond economics. Heavy-duty trucks make up a relatively small portion of the U.S. fleet, but they account for a disproportionate share of fuel consumption and harmful air pollution.

According to recent reports, “Any exposure to diesel exhaust is going to be harmful to your health,” says Ray Minjares, heavy-duty vehicles program director at the International Council on Clean Transportation. “And so since there's really no safe level, the obvious solution, particularly in a world where commercial zero-emission vehicles are already available, is to switch to that technology.”.

The Tesla Semi represents a "step-change" for electric trucking hardware in the U.S., Einride CEO Roozbeh Charli mentioned.

Industry observers note that high diesel prices aren’t the only tailwind helping to drive trucking electrification this year, Charli said. The long-awaited launch of the Tesla Semi not only helped bring more attention to electric trucking, but it also introduced a genuinely groundbreaking offering to the U.S. market, he said.

It has been revealed that “The Tesla Semi, in a U.S. context, is definitely a step-change in the capabilities of the hardware” in terms of range, performance, and price, he remarked.

Sources indicate that in August, Einride confirmed plans to deploy 500 Semis to service Amazon and other North American customers, tripling its fleet. Tesla’s truck is several years late to full-scale production. But given the diesel situation these days, maybe it’s right on time.

“They timed it well,” Charli said.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong.
  • In a recent development, it wasn’t the plane’s first flight.
  • The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong. Two pilots and a flight test engineer were aboard the roughly 10-tonne demonstrator, and COMAC says every system worked normally.

In a recent development, it wasn’t the plane’s first flight. The CE-25A had already completed 19 autonomous test flights with nobody on board since February 2, and China’s aviation regulator is now reviewing it for a type certificate.

The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers. COMAC lists a 300 km/h cruise speed and a 400 km (250-mile) range.

In a recent development, the CAAC accepting COMAC’s type certificate application starts the airworthiness review. It doesn’t mean paying passengers are close, and COMAC hasn’t given a date for commercial service.

Industry observers note that the program has been quiet for a long time. COMAC showed a CE-25A model at the China International Import Expo in Shanghai in November 2023, with a placard listing 400 to 500 km of range and a 400 km/h top cruise speed. The full-size aircraft, registered B-0EFH, only became public when photos leaked on Chinese social media on October 28.

The obvious battery candidate is CATL. In July 2023, COMAC, CATL, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University formed a joint venture with CNY 600 million in registered capital to develop electric aircraft, as we reported when CATL launched its aviation unit.

CATL had just unveiled its “condensed” battery at the time, claiming up to 500 Wh/kg at the cell level, and said it was testing the cells to aviation standards. Neither company has confirmed what’s inside the CE-25A, though.

~500 Wh/kg has long been seen as the target for battery energy density to enable electric flight on a commercial scale.

Sources indicate that COMAC isn’t alone in flying a large electric demonstrator. In August, Heart Aerospace flew its X1 in Plattsburgh, Upcoming York, for 27 minutes. It’s a 25,000-lb aircraft with a 106-foot wingspan, which Heart calls the largest battery-electric aircraft ever flown.

Eviation flew its 9-passenger Alice back in September 2022, then laid off most of its staff in early 2025.

Heart is the closest Western comparison. It dropped its 19-seat ES-19 for the 30-seat ES-30 back in 2022, and the ES-30 now relies on reserve turbogenerators to stretch its range, with BAE Systems working on the battery. Heart is targeting 2031 for service and claims “more than 40%” lower operating costs.

For years, the go-to excuse in the West for doing nothing about emissions was China. Why should we bother, the argument went, if China won’t? Now China is pulling ahead, and it’s doing it by cutting its dependence on fossil fuels.

Look at trucking. Electric trucks hit 50.3% of China’s heavy truck sales in September, and they’re already eating into the country’s diesel demand. In the US, electric models were about 0.3% of heavy-truck sales last year, according to the ICCT.

A great step in the right direction, probably needs a doubling in range but at current rates of progress that will only be five years away.

Now it’s planes, starting where batteries make sense today: short regional routes. The CE-25A’s 400 km shrinks once you keep the reserves regulators require, and a Beechcraft 1900 turboprop in the same class covers well over 1,000 km. So it’s not replacing turboprops anytime soon. But that’s how trucking started too. Short-haul first, then long-haul tractors once the batteries caught up.

And this couldn’t happen fast enough. We’re in the middle of a diesel and jet fuel crisis. Jet fuel averaged $3.50 a gallon in early August, up 63% from a year earlier, according to Heart Aerospace. Every truck and plane China moves to batteries is one less exposed to that.

Recent findings suggest that china also has the batteries to pull it off, with CATL in the joint venture. Meanwhile, Heart has pushed to 2031 and added a fuel-burning backup, and Eviation is a cautionary tale.

#17428. Whale snot helps scientists sequence an entire genome

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (811 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Whale snot helps scientists sequence an entire genome

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (811 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that whale vomit can be turned into expensive perfume.
  • According to recent reports, whole genomes are crucial for animal conservation.
  • Recent findings suggest that to obtain genetic data from whales, marine biologists historically have had to conduct a skin biopsy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that whale vomit can be turned into expensive perfume. Whale carcasses will sink to the bottom and become marine life habitats. Whale pee nourishes the entire ocean. But how about whale snot? The microbes and other biological material emitted from their blowholes when the giant cetaceans breathe has helped scientists sequence an entire whale genome: Take that whale vomit. The findings are detailed in a study published today in the journal Molecular Ecology Resources.

According to recent reports, whole genomes are crucial for animal conservation. With genomic data, researchers can measure population health, to see how much genetic diversity and inbreeding is present. It can also help identify individual animals for monitoring, help determine an animal’s sex, and estimate the population’s size.

Recent findings suggest that to obtain genetic data from whales, marine biologists historically have had to conduct a skin biopsy. They’ll take a dart, stick it into the whale’s blubber, and take a small sample of the skin and blubber. However, during sampling, boats must get close to the whales, which can disturb them. In some locations and for some endangered species, getting close enough to take a biopsy isn’t permitted or possible.

That’s where whale snot—or blow—comes in. For this study, a team from Scotland’s University of St. Andrews, the University of Copenhagen in Denmark, the North Coast Cetacean Society, and Fisheries and Oceans Canada used several small drones off the coast of British Columbia. The drones were equipped with sterile petri dishes to collect the samples.

According to recent reports, the team flew the drone through the exhaled breaths of one North pacific humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira) at a time, but still sampled several individual whales. The humpbacks generally took one to six breaths every time they surfaced—covering the drone and the dishes in whale snot.

The team collected 58 blow samples from 26 individual humpback whales. They also took repeated samples from the same whales, collected in different encounters and across two years to match the genomes. They then cross-referenced the genomes collected from the whale blow with genomes sequenced from traditional blubber biopsies taken from the same animals.

To keep the DNA from mixing, the team targeted the whale most upwind in the pod, since the blow downwind might mix with the blow from the whales up ahead. Resting whales were never sampled, and the team stopped the drone flights if a whale indicated any reaction. More than one third of samples were collected by flying the drone directly from land—no boat required.

The DNA was sequenced to produce two types of genomes. Low-coverage nuclear genomes, which are inherited from both parents, and high-coverage mitochondrial genomes, which are inherited from the mother only.

In a recent development, the team found that the genetic diversity estimated from the blow samples was very similar to the estimates taken from traditional biopsies. Fortunately, the humpback population in the study reveals little evidence of recent inbreeding. There is a small proportion of the genome that has long stretches of identical DNA, but the team believes that most likely reflects distant shared ancestry or past population bottlenecks.

According to recent reports, according to the team, this research marks one of the first whole genome datasets for a group of North Pacific humpback whales. Previously, only one North Pacific humpback whole genome was publicly available.

Industry observers note that “We will use these blow-derived genomes to not only assess population structure and health, but also assess kinship and family ties among humpback whales foraging in northern British Columbia,” Dr. Éadin O’Mahony, a study co-author and marine mammal ecologist who was at the University of St. Andrews at the time of the study, remarked in a statement. “The aim is to understand how their social bonds form: Are the whales that forage together family, or long-term friends?”.

As expected, the North Pacific humpback whales were genetically distinct from their counterparts living in the North Atlantic. This confirms that data taken from whale blow works as well from data taken from conventional biopsies. The drone-captured genetic analyses also correctly determined every whale’s sex, and revealed three previously undescribed mitochondrial DNA variants, which could help show how some of these whales are related. The blow from whales swimming in groups also did not have any sign of contamination from neighboring whales.

It has been revealed that about 16 percent of the DNA in each blow sample were also primarily from the microbes living in the whale’s airways. According to the team, this indicates that a single breath could tell us about the individual whale and its respiratory microbiome, opening up a potential newly introduced window into cetacean health.

That’s a whole lot of data from just a little bit of snot.

Breaking: High altitude, bitter cold, zero drivers: autonomous trucks take on Tibetan mine

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks.
  • In a recent development, chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks.

In a recent development, chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.

It has been revealed that “High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper. “Research involving workers in Andes mines operating between 3,800 and 4,500 meters found that 73% of workers assessed experienced periods of nocturnal oxygen saturation below 85% during their high-altitude shifts, indicating moderate-to-severe hypoxemia.”.

That’s bad news for Zijin’s workers – but the good news here, of course, is that the company won’t be needing many heavy haul drivers going forward.

SANY has been working with Perth, Australia-based Eacon Mining Technology to develop an autonomous haulage solution that uses a full suite of both in-vehicle and ground-based sensors, adaptive vehicle controls, and machine learning that can handle the big bad trucks even here in the Kailas range.

In a recent development, “Autonomous haulage offers one way to address this challenge,” continues the Econ report. “Rather than requiring a driver for each truck, autonomous systems allow fleets to be managed through centralized supervision, with personnel overseeing operations and intervening when required. This reduces the need for people to spend entire shifts operating equipment at elevation, while changing how workforce resources are allocated across the mine … depending on the system configuration, some operations can manage autonomous fleets from remote Integrated Operations Centers located away from the mine site, (allowing) personnel to supervise haulage activities from lower-altitude locations, further reducing the need for workers to remain in extreme-altitude environments.”.

The working partnership between the two companies combines SANY’s battery-powered truck platform with Eacon’s full technology stack to create dependable, driverless haul trucks with logic and behaviors that are ideally suited to China’s open-pit mining environments.

Eacon technology is currently operating more than 3,100 autonomous trucks cross more than 40 large-scale mines, including Zijin Mining’s Zijinshan Gold-Copper Mine and at the Norton Gold Fields project in Australia.

While specifications for this specific deployment weren’t disclosed, the SANY SKT105E trucks (the “D” is, presumably, the wide-body variant) the company has deployed elsewhere are powered by a dual-motor electric drivetrain, pairing two permanent-magnet synchronous motors with a dual three-speed automated manual transmission. The system delivers 570 kW (~765 hp) of continuous power and up to 820 kW (~1,100 hp) at peak output, with each motor producing some 2,430 Nm (~18,00 lb-ft) of peak torque.

Those motors get their electrons from an absolute whopper of a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack in capacities ranging from 423 to 642 kWh, depending on configuration. The big trucks also offer regenerative braking to recover energy on downhill runs, while their fast-charging system can reportedly charge the battery from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that tesla drivers can now seamlessly charge their electric cars at Ioona Rechargeries using a feature called Autocharge, as reported by State of Charge. With Autocharge, EVs can simply be plugged in, and the session will start automatically, without the driver having to do anything. Billing is also handled automatically, but a one-time setup needs to be completed to enable the functionality to work in the background.

Recent findings suggest that in Tesla and Ionna’s case, a third-party smartphone application is needed to get started, as the charging network doesn’t have its own app. Drivers need to download and set up the Presto Charging app, which bundles over 190,000 chargers across the United States.

The setup involves creating an account with Presto Charging, scanning the car’s VIN for validation, and manually starting the first charging session in the app. While the initial charging session is active, an “Enable Autocharge” option will appear on the screen, which needs to be confirmed by the driver.

After this initial learning session, charging at Ionna locations will start automatically, and the driver’s payment method will be used to pay for the dispensed energy automatically.

Recent findings suggest that to be clear, Presto Charging’s Autocharge function is not the same as Plug & Charge, even though it works in a similar way. With Plug & Charge, the EV communicates directly with the charger using a digital certificate, while Autocharge uses the car’s charging port network address to identify the vehicle and authorize it with a specific charger. In this case, the Presto Charging app takes the car’s information, checks it, and passes it to the charger, which starts the charging session.

Ionna Rechargeries feature CCS and NACS connectors.

Plug & Charge is generally regarded as being a more secure option, but Presto Charging claims it constantly monitors sessions to prevent any complications. For instance, if the same vehicle appears as charging in a different location than the charger, the platform can flag it and fix it. Presto Charging handles all of the charging history and user data, which could be useful, considering Ionna doesn’t offer a way of keeping track of charging stops at its stations.

To make the feature more appealing to Tesla owners, the first session using Autocharge at Ionna is free. After that, pricing will be similar to Ionna’s regular offering, though it’s important to note that Presto Charging will get a small share to keep the lights on and squash any potential bugs. Other automakers have enabled Plug & Charge at Ionna, and drivers can use the card terminals at all stations to pay for charging.

According to recent reports, it’s an important step for Ionna, which is still small compared to Tesla’s own Supercharger network, but has made significant progress when it comes to the quality of charging sessions. According to J.D. Power’s latest driver satisfaction survey, Ionna ranked first, and it’s hardly surprising, given how we’ve always had great experiences with the tech giant’s chargers. They always work, they’re fast, and there are clean amenities nearby.

According to recent reports, last month, Ionna opened its 200th station, marking a huge milestone for the up-and-coming organization. In total, the network now has over 1,600 ports across the country—double compared to seven months ago—and it’s not slowing down. No fewer than 80 fresh locations are under construction, and more are planned.

Elon Musk once promised the fully autonomous, steering-wheel- and pedal-free Tesla Cybercab would arrive before the year 2027, and start at less than $30,000.
