#17381. Tesla Model X on Autopilot/FSD hit a pole and flipped, killing passenger

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1177 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla Model X on Autopilot/FSD hit a pole and flipped, killing passenger

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1177 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A Tesla Model X veered off Golden Gate Parkway in Naples, Florida, hit a traffic signal pole and overturned in September, killing a 50-year-old woman riding as a passenger.
  • According to recent reports, tesla flagged this crash itself, through its telematics, and says it has the car’s event data recorder and video.
  • on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, a 2025 Tesla Model X was heading east on Golden Gate Parkway in Collier County, approaching the Estuary Boulevard intersection, according to a Florida Highway Patrol press release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A Tesla Model X veered off Golden Gate Parkway in Naples, Florida, hit a traffic signal pole and overturned in September, killing a 50-year-old woman riding as a passenger. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators says Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged.

According to recent reports, tesla flagged this crash itself, through its telematics, and says it has the car’s event data recorder and video. The public was told a car “veered off the road.” It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data.

At 11:43 p.m. on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, a 2025 Tesla Model X was heading east on Golden Gate Parkway in Collier County, approaching the Estuary Boulevard intersection, according to a Florida Highway Patrol press release.

The SUV left the road, hit a traffic signal pole on the corner of the intersection, and rolled over. Its passenger, a 50-year-old woman from Fort Myers, was pronounced dead at the scene. The 48-year-old driver, also from Fort Myers, went to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

Industry observers note that FHP said the crash remains under investigation. It hasn’t released the woman’s name, a cause, or anything about speed or impairment. And nothing about a driver-assist system.

Sources indicate that under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone is killed or hurt. Tesla filed a report on this one.

It has been revealed that it identifies a 2025 Model X and marks the “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged,” meaning Tesla confirmed through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 39 mph, a collision with a pole or tree, airbag deployment, and damage to the front and the top of the car, which fits FHP’s account of the rollover.

This record is unusually complete on what Tesla has. It checks the event data recorder, telematics, video, and “other.” And it claims Tesla learned of the crash through its own telematics, not just from the media.

Then it redacts the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was inside the system’s operating domain, all as “confidential business information,” the same treatment Tesla gives 99.9% of its reports.

Industry observers note that how we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 03:41 UTC on October 1, which is 11:41 p.m. in Florida on September 30, two minutes off FHP’s 11:43 p.m. The city, the 2025 Model X, the pole, and the fatal outcome all line up. Because the UTC timestamp crosses midnight, Tesla’s record lists the crash in October, so anyone checking Tesla’s data against September crashes would miss it. It’s the same crash.

Most of the crashes we’ve matched leave real gaps in what Tesla holds. Not this one. Tesla has the video, the EDR, and the telematics, and it knew about the crash on its own.

Sources indicate that so Tesla can see what the car did on the approach to that intersection. It knows whether the system steered the SUV off the road or the driver did, whether the car warned him, and how fast it was going when it hit the pole. It filed all of that under a redaction.

According to recent reports, autopilot/FSD might not have caused the crash, but it was active within 30 seconds of the crash, so it’s vital to understand what happened. Was the driver distracted? Did Autopilot/FSD make a run move?

According to recent reports, there’s also a living witness here. The driver survived with non-life-threatening injuries, which means FHP can ask him whether he had Autopilot or FSD on and what the car was doing. We don’t know if anyone has. Troopers may not even know Tesla verified the system was engaged.

According to recent reports, this is the second fatal Tesla driver-assist crash in Naples in this NHTSA release. In May, a Model 3 with the system engaged at 71 mph hit an overturned box truck on I-75 at Pine Ridge Road, killing three people. FHP investigated both, and neither crash was ever publicly tied to Autopilot or FSD.

The same release set a fresh record: 264 Tesla driver-assist crashes in September 2026, beating July’s 236.

This is the cleanest example yet of how much Tesla knows and how little it shares. It detected the crash on its own. It has the video. It has the EDR. A woman riding as a passenger died in a Model X that, according to Tesla, had its driver-assist engaged. And the public account is one sentence: the car veered off the road.

In a recent development, tesla certainly benefits by keeping the information hidden. Most are willing to look past these things and not be suspicious, but ultimately the question is why hide. something if you dont have something to hide.

Industry observers note that we’re not saying the system caused this crash. We don’t know, and that’s the point. Tesla does know, and it decided the account of what its car did in a fatal crash is a trade secret.

If FSD or Autopilot did nothing wrong here, Tesla has the footage to prove it. It was happy to share data in the Katy crash when it helped its case. When Tesla keeps the video sealed, people are going to assume the worst, and Tesla only has itself to blame.

Recent findings suggest that we’re asking the Florida Highway Patrol whether its investigators knew the system was engaged and whether they got Tesla’s video and raw data, or only Tesla’s interpretation of them. Same questions we asked about Vineland. How many more fatal crashes will troopers close without knowing what Tesla knows?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bentley’s first electric car, the Torcal SUV, looks like a hit already.
  • In a recent development, the British luxury automaker noted that all available production slots for next year have already been allocated and that the tech giant is now taking orders that will be delivered in 2028.
  • “Needless to say, we’re very pleased with the response and position we’re in,” a company spokesperson told Automotive News.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bentley’s first electric car, the Torcal SUV, looks like a hit already. Even though production hasn’t started yet, the $220,000+ EV is sold out for 2027, according to Frank-Steffen Wallier, the tech giant’s head honcho, quoted by Automotive News.

In a recent development, the British luxury automaker noted that all available production slots for next year have already been allocated and that the tech giant is now taking orders that will be delivered in 2028. Bentley didn’t say how many EVs it will build in 2027, but the initial customer response has made the marque quite happy with the outcome.

“Needless to say, we’re very pleased with the response and position we’re in,” a company spokesperson told Automotive News.

That’s great news for Bentley, which isn’t doing great in terms of sales and profit. From January through September, it sold 5,970 cars globally, 17% fewer compared to the same period last year. Meanwhile, the profit dropped by more than half to $54.1 million through the first nine months of the year.

Industry observers note that the Torcal, which is smaller than the Bentayga SUV, is the brand’s cheapest model, though it still costs a pretty penny. The base Torcal starts at $222,495, followed by the more powerful Torcal S at $262,695, and the Torcal First Edition at $300,995. All things considered, Walliser remarked that the smaller size and relatively lower price compared to the Bentayga have attracted new and younger customers to the brand.

By comparison, the Bentayga starts at $231,150, the Flying Spur sedan starts at $254,850, and the Continental GT two-door starts at $288,750.

According to recent reports, so far, the Torcal S has proved to be the most popular version of the latest EV, but when it comes to personalization, the sky’s the limit. “We see cars spec’d north of 300,000 pounds ($397,086),” said Walliser. “Individual content does not stop in case of an electric car. There have been some assumptions, and some people have been critical if people would be ready to do so.”.

Industry observers note that based on the same underpinnings as the electric Porsche Cayenne, the Bentley Torcal is powered by a 113-kilowatt-hour battery that can be charged at up to 400 kilowatts. It can go from 10% to 80% in less than 20 minutes, and the estimated EPA range is expected to be over 300 miles.

It has been revealed that built on the Premium Platform Electric (PPE) architecture, it has two electric motors that make 810 horsepower and 881 pound-feet of torque in the standard Torcal and a whopping 876 hp and 996 lb-ft of torque in the Torcal S. When the model debuted in September, Bentley stated it was the most powerful and quietest model to come out of the factory in Crewe.

To make the Torcal a reality, Bentley invested $463 million to upgrade its factory in England, plus at least the same amount for supply chain preparations and research and development, Walliser mentioned.

Despite the electric SUV’s initial success, the British automaker is still heavily invested in gas and plug-in hybrid models, and the Bentayga isn’t going anywhere. “We have a very good combination with Torcal and Bentayga,” Walliser remarked. “The segment definitely has space for two cars.”.

In fact, some of these games can be completed in less than 10 hours.

For players who are wanting a one-and-done experience with an open world game, being able to beat it within the same day or two days maximum, these games scratch that itch. You’re able to hop in and complete the game practically quicker than you can download it, and it’s just the right amount of content to tide you over until the next game.

While others are diving into open world games to sink hundreds upon hundreds of hours into them, you can rest assured that these games won’t eat up your schedule.

The thing about Outer Wilds is that the world itself is the final boss, with players only having a limited amount of time in order to save the universe – but it’s not done on its own. The game’s DLC, Echoes of the Eye, is about 10 and half hours long, obviously shorter for faster players.

It has been revealed that the DLC doesn’t replace anything in the game, but it’s rather a separate and self-contained location, more than ready for players to dive in and unravel its secrets. This way, if players are wanting a taste of Outer Wilds without going through the whole game, they can easily do so.

This is especially the case if you’ve already beaten the game/solved the mystery of the main story. Since there isn’t really any replayability, the DLC offers a whole new mystery altogether – in a way, it’s like you’re playing the game for the first time all over again, and it can be solved pretty promptly.

Thankfully, there are also even more DLCs if you want more mystery, but they aren’t anywhere near as condensed as Echoes of the Eye.

There’s something particularly special about Shadow of the Colossus: the game is labelled as an open world, but many players would walk away from it thinking that it’s a semi-open world due to just how empty the world itself is.

In a recent development, of course, that’s typically a bad thing for open worlds, but the unique thing about Shadow of the Colossus is that it would not work without that emptiness. Combine this with a linear order for the bosses themselves (which are platforming puzzles as well), a vague yet compelling story and a genuinely cool premise, and you’ve got a game that’s as fun as it is challenging.

It has been revealed that one of my students refers to the game as “Rated T for Teen Mario,” and I'm bound to agree, if that helps get the idea across. And just like Mario, the game can be beaten pretty promptly: about 7 hours, in fact.

With that in mind, if this is a game that interests you, be prepared to spend most of those 7 hours climbing rather than fighting; you’re going to love it regardless.

Right now, The Legend of Zelda once again has the gaming community in a complete buzz thanks to the fantastic reception to the Ocarina of Time Remake.

The series is continuously revolutionary, constantly evolving and redefining the open world genre as we know it. However, many tend to forget that open world Zelda didn’t start with Breath of the Wild, it started with the very first entry in the entire franchise.

Sources indicate that the nice part about the game is that it’s not long at all (especially when compared to its sequels that will come over the next few decades) – averaging only at about 8 hours to beat the game. Players who want a traditional Zelda experience in a short amount of time can’t find any other game that would be a better fit.

And as the game comes up on its 40th anniversary, it’s all the more reason to dive into where it all began.

In a recent development, obviously, both Red Dead Redemption games are massive, telling all kinds of stories jam-packed in a rich world of historical fiction, so it would take a while to beat either entry. However, the first game’s DLC, Undead Nightmare, is a fantastic stand-alone story that only takes about 6 and a half hours to complete.

Undead Nightmare takes everything you love about the classic Red Dead Redemption, but with a twist: suddenly, everyone is trying to survive a zombie apocalypse that came about practically overnight. The world and everything you can do within it, naturally, is related to this instead of your standard robberies and bounties.

Recent findings suggest that since the world is so condensed, the DLC goes by much quicker than most, but it’s an absolute blast from start to finish. In fact, it’s widely considered to be one of the greatest DLCs of all time, simply for how refreshingly unique and fun it is.

With that in mind, the fact that this game can be completed quicker than a standard work shift just makes it all the better.

Of all the Assassin's Creed games, the shortest mainline entry (non-DLC game) is easily Assassin's Creed: Rogue, clocking in at about 11 hours to be beaten (again, it’s much quicker than that for veteran AC fans and seasoned gamers as a whole).

Surprisingly, the game has one of the more unique stories that the series has seen, focusing on an Assassin named Shay Patrick Cormac literally going rogue, slaughtering the brotherhood he knows and siding with the Templars.

And the best part of the story is the fact that the modern-day segments are thankfully incredibly short – the segments that drag and feel like a chore in all the other titles in the franchise don’t bog down this game.

Sources indicate that overall, it’s the perfect bite-sized game for Assassin’s Creed content, regardless of if you’re a fan or even brand latest to the series. It’s truly one of a kind, especially for a series like AC.

Recent findings suggest that if you were given 10 hours to simply explore Fresh York City and soak it all in, you wouldn’t even be an eighth of the way through your journey before you reach that time. The fact that Marvel's Spider-Man brought in NYC on a similar (still scaled down) scale cemented the game’s timeframe as you continue to whip around as The Friendly Neighborhood himself.

Yet, you don’t have anywhere near as many superhero duties in Spider-Man: Miles Morales, so obviously, it will take you a lot less time. It would take about 8 hours, in fact.

In a recent development, since you’re playing the game as Miles Morales (duh) while Peter Parker is still around and kicking, you’re basically a superhero in training. This training will have you busy constantly taking down bad guys and saving the day, serving as the sole Spider-Man in NYC for several hours until Peter comes back from vacation with MJ.

Or you could just swing around Fresh York City doing whatever you want for that timeframe, you’d get the same amount of enjoyment.

Just because a game is a horror game doesn’t mean it can’t also be open world, and in DREDGE, our open world is a vast, dangerous ocean. Even then, it’s nowhere near as dangerous as it will be once your sanity drains due to the Lovecraftian terrors you’ll encounter.

Recent findings suggest that it sounds horrifying, but it’s actually the coziest fishing game you’d ever imagine. You fish, fill out your encyclopedia, discover aberrations with the marine life and upgrade your ship, but the real fun comes from the simplest mechanic: sorting the fish into your boat. Seriously, the inventory management is the most addictive part of the whole game.

It has been revealed that the nice part is that it’s wrapped up quickly, too, taking only about 9 and a half hours to complete – but trust me, you’re going to willingly sink far more hours into the game (and your ship). And if that doesn’t sound like enough content in the game for how much I sing its praises, it also has two equally dense and fun DLCs.

When it comes to short, yet full open world games, you cannot get any better of an experience than with DREDGE.

The lovely thing about Eastshade isn’t just how stunning of a game it is, but also the fact that it can be beaten pretty quickly and pretty easily – just around 9 hours.

Sources indicate that the whole game is about finding the most beautiful spots in the game to paint them (using a photography mechanic), so those entire 9 hours are filled with genuine beauty. Of course, since it’s open world, there are side quests (artwork commissions) and other things to do, but you’re going to be far more caught up in how pretty the world is.

And for those who love subtle, environmental storytelling, this world is full of it. You can learn more while you’re out and about exploring in it, or from the various other characters that you can talk to.

It’s one of the few open world games that keeps you busy without actively stressing you out; since, after all, the point of the game is to relax you, you’re going to find yourself in a comfortable state of bliss while playing.

If you’ve ever wanted to feel like you’re driving a pod around Tatooine (like any Star Wars fan would), you would have a fantastic time with Sable.

It has been revealed that the game seems pretty surface-level and simple: just ride around on your sand-speeder and enjoy the game’s lovely art style, but once you start playing, you’ll see it’s a lot deeper than you’d expect. It’s supposed to be about the protagonist’s self-discovery on their home planet, but by the end of your adventure, you’re going to feel like you’ve gone on a self-discovery of your own.

Recent findings suggest that while the game can be completed in about 7 and a half hours, it’s actually better if you take your time with the exploration – that’s the game’s strongest component, after all. Why not take the time to enjoy a world as pretty and interesting as this one?

In a recent development, it’s not perfectly polished; it’s actually pretty janky of a game at times, but if anything, it makes you love the game and all the charm it has even more. At the same time, if some of the previously mentioned jank (charm) is a little too much, then rest assured that you can get through this game very, very promptly.

It has been revealed that A Short Hike is just that: short. It’s not the kind of short where it’s on the shorter end of a long game, no, the game is only about an hour and a half long. If you try to complete every single element within it to 100% the game, you’re looking at about 4 hours, an incredibly tiny open world game.

The premise of the game is simple: you’re hiking up a mountain. If you run into anyone or anything on the way there, you’re more than welcome to interact with them, but it’s optional if you’re wanting to just get to the top. Considering how short the game is, I’d recommend not skipping anything if you can help it, just to get the richest experience you can.

According to recent reports, don’t rush through this hike, either. The game is already short enough, and there is so much enjoyable content that you don’t want to miss out on while on the way to the top.

But as we’ve learned with games like these: it’s not about the destination, it’s about the journey, so don’t be afraid to go on that journey.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article was updated in November 2026 with latest products and information.
  • According to recent reports, there’s a particular satisfaction in picking up a tool or piece of gear and knowing where it was made.
  • Industry observers note that buying American-made products helps support the craftspeople, businesses, and communities that keep making things here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article was updated in November 2026 with latest products and information.

According to recent reports, there’s a particular satisfaction in picking up a tool or piece of gear and knowing where it was made. It’s more than patriotism: a pair of boots stitched in Michigan or a kitchen tool forged in Ohio carries a connection to the people and skills behind it.

Industry observers note that buying American-made products helps support the craftspeople, businesses, and communities that keep making things here. And finding those products doesn’t have to be a treasure hunt. We’ve rounded up standout U.S.-made picks for weekend wrenchers, road-trip warriors, and everyone in between.

Sources indicate that the brass bolsters and wood handle give the iconic Buck Knives 110 Folding Hunter Knife a significant heft that exudes quality. Made in Post Falls, Idaho, it locks open with a satisfying click and holds an edge through serious cutting tasks. It is not the most high-tech blade on the market, but it is a timeless tool that feels great in the hand.

Most carry-on bags feel flimsy, but the Pelican ATX 22 feels like you could drag it behind the car on the highway and it would survive. Hell, I'm not even sure a particularly grumpy baggage handler could destroy this thing.

Industry observers note that the layout is simple, but the injection-molded construction is undeniably Pelican. This particular model is sized just right to fit in the overhead bin without a fight, and you can rest assured clothes and gear will be protected from the elements better than standard fabric luggage ever could manage.

Built just down the road from me in Rockford, Michigan, these Wolverine 1000 Mile Boots are no joke. While they do require a significant break-in period, the payoff is worth the blister or two.

Once the Horween leather molds to your foot, these boots feel like a second skin that look as good as they feel and are tough enough for daily wear. The Goodyear welt construction also means you can resole them in a few years rather than tossing them in the trash when the tread wears down.

As you'd expect from a brand as synonymous with quality as Channellock, this Tool Roll-5 is the kind of pliers kit that just works, day in and day out. The cutters bite cleanly, the tongue-and-groove jaws actually meet, and the pivots don't wobble after a season of real use.

The included roll keeps everything from clanking around in the trunk or bottoming out in a drawer and is great for keeping forgetful DIYers such as myself from losing them in the middle of projects. As all products on this list, these tools are made in the USA and tough enough to hand to a neighbor without worrying about getting them back bent.

Manufactured in the US, the Smithey 5.5-quart dutch oven skips the fragile enamel coatings found on expensive European imports in favor of bare, heavily seasoned cast iron. You can drag it across steel grill grates or bury it directly in glowing campfire coals without worrying about chipping a delicate finish. And it works equally well atop gas, electric, and induction stovetops.

In a recent development, the sheer mass of the walls and dome lid acts like a thermal battery, locking in steady, even heat for hours to properly break down tough cuts of meat and soften even the most stubborn carrots. It’s a heavy-duty, straightforward piece of American hardware that handles campfire stews and kitchen braises with equal capability.

According to recent reports, if you're looking to pair the Dutch oven with a skillet, or simply don't need the massive capacity of a 5.5-quart pot, the Smithey No. 10 is the logical alternative. Like the rest of their South Carolina-forged lineup, it features a machined, glass-smooth interior that eliminates the stubborn break-in period typical of modern cast iron. It cooks with the non-stick capability of a well-worn vintage piece right out of the box.

According to recent reports, the 10-inch diameter hits the sweet spot for daily duty, whether you're searing a pair of ribeyes over an open fire or frying eggs on a kitchen stove, although there are plenty of other sizes available on Smithey's website if you're hoping to go smaller or larger. I'd also recommend picking up a chainmail scrubber to get out the more stubborn food remnants, and Smithey's salt keeper is an adorable accessory to boot.

Having a heavy-duty piece of American metal that takes high heat without warping, wipes clean in seconds, and feels substantial enough to outlast your vehicle fundamentally changes how you operate in the kitchen.

Industry observers note that the GoRuck GR1 is overkill for a commute, which is exactly why you will like it. Made in America by a veteran-owned company, this bag has straps that are padded perfectly to handle heavy loads, and the laptop compartment is suspended to protect your tech from drops. It opens flat for easy packing and shrugs off rain and abrasions like they are nothing.

According to recent reports, I've personally owned one of these for more than 15 years now, and it's been everything from a daily backpack in college to a tool bag that's been used and abused during car repairs. While the 1000D Cordura is certainly faded and the zipper pulls have been replaced a few times, it still performs just as it did on day one.

Recent findings suggest that finding quality local products oftentimes requires giving up a Saturday morning. You have to navigate a farmer's market, walk the stalls, and sift through the inventory to find something worthwhile. The Farmers Finds outsources that legwork by scouring regional markets across the country, buying small-batch goods from independent makers, and packing them into a single box. It’s a straightforward logistical solution akin to a regional community supported agriculture (CSA) box. Instead of driving across state lines to find a specific local preserve or hot sauce, it arrives directly on your porch.You can order a single box, though the subscription model is how the service is really meant to be used. The monthly tier delivers two to four items from a single brand, while the quarterly option scales up to seven to ten products sourced from five different makers. It's a practical gift for someone who appreciates regional goods, but doesn't have the bandwidth to track down the vendors themselves. You get quality American-made products, and the makers get the business.

What more can I say about Duck Tape Duct Tape that hasn't already been remarked? Sure, it's never a long-term solution to automotive or home problems, but it'll get the job done until you find a more permanent solution. Hopefully you'll never have to use it, but for 10 bucks or so, it's nice insurance to throw in the trunk for the inevitable emergency.

The Wave is one of Leatherman's most iconic tools, and while it takes on a newly introduced shape with the Wave Alpha, it's still the answer when you want one thing that handles 10 small jobs and you don't feel like going back to the toolbox.

This all-in-one tool features one-hand blades, real pliers, actual drivers, a large scissor tool, and more. Leatherman backs it with a no-drama warranty, and their stuff is easy to service if you get it gritty (I've sent in my original Wave for service twice and had it back within a week with little more than the shipping cost to send it out).

Odds are this tool will outlast whoever you give it to, so consider it a long-term investment made right here in the United States.

If you want deep color and gloss for a weekend cruiser, this Griot's Garage Best of Show Wax gets the job done. Formulated just west of Indianapolis, Indiana, it goes on smooth and buffs off without leaving stubborn white dust in the panel gaps.

According to recent reports, while it's easy enough to use with a hand buff, it works equally well with an electric buffer if you want to expedite the process. It's affordable, it works well, and overall it delivers a robust shine with a little bit of elbow grease.

It has been revealed that duke Cannon's Big Ass Brick of Soap is comically big at first, but then you realize it outlasts three normal ones and doesn't turn into goo in the shower. I've purchased and used a dozen of these over the last decade, and every time I go through a single bar, my spouse has already gone through a three-pack of normal ones.

The scent of this particular bar (they have dozens of scents/formulations to choose from) is more warm "vanilla/wood" than "spill at the distillery," but it does have that signature bourbon smell you'd expect from a little Buffalo Trace.

This Rite in the Rain notepad lets you write down torque values, weird part numbers, or your "What's that noise?" notes, all without having to worry about whether the pages will smear if your hands are greasy or it's misting outside.

It has been revealed that the covers hold up in a pocket, and the wire doesn't explode into a tangle like some other cheap pads I've used over the years. It's a bit pricey for a small notepad, but when you need a reliable notepad that can take on the elements and solvents, you won't find a better option.

As a Michigander, I'm a bit biased, but Carhartt Beanies are just a way of life (second only to Stormy Kromers). While not all versions are made in America, there are Woodside Beanies made right here in the States. Just be sure to check the product listing to confirm before making your purchase.

Sources indicate that this American-made bag takes a beating and looks all the better for it. The rugged twill of the Filson Original Briefcase resists water and wear, while the bridle leather handles soften up nicely over time. It is heavy for what it holds, but it protects a laptop and documents with a style that works as well in a truck as it does in an office.

LED technology revived the classic Maglite form factor you remember from your childhood. Built in Ontario, California, it still has the heft that feels reassuring in your hand, but now it throws a beam that properly lights up the road ahead (or engine beneath you). You get a simple focus twist mechanism, as well as the convenience of D-cell batteries that are easy enough to find at any gas station.

It has been revealed that smell like you upgraded to a nicer car. Drift infuses a magnetized wood block with clean-ingredient essential oils—teak, amber, and cedar—then snaps it to a low-profile metal visor clip. It's made in the U.S., looks grown-up, and takes quick monthly refill blocks when the scent fades. No dangling trees, no headaches.

Pouring fluids into a cramped engine bay usually results in a mess, but this FlexAll Flexible Funnel by TEC Products solves that geometry problem.

In a recent development, the nitrile rubber handles oil and gas without degrading, and you can mold it around hoses and wires to create a leak-free path. Sure, it might be a bit more of a hassle to clean when you're done, but the convenience of the gooseneck makes all the difference when trying to get fluids into all the nooks and crannies of modern vehicles.

According to recent reports, the lifetime warranty is real, but the comfort is why you will keep buying them. Knit in Northfield, Vermont, these Darn Tough Micro Crew Socks breathe well inside a driving shoe or a heavy boot, and the merino wool blend doesn't stink after a long day on the road.

Sources indicate that you will have a hard time wearing a hole in a pair, which makes the higher price tag feel like a bargain over the long haul. I've had probably a dozen pair of Darn Tough socks over the years, and I only managed to wear a hole in one, which was only thanks to a little nail sticking out of my home's mid-century wood floors. And, of course, Darn Tough promptly replaced it with a brand-latest pair.

According to recent reports, you usually buy emergency kits hoping you wasted your money, because nobody wants to have to use one. But when you get stranded on a dark shoulder, this Pelican SRVL2 2-Person Emergency Kit is exactly what you want to have in the cargo area.

Sources indicate that made and assembled in Torrance, California, this kit organizes the chaos of emergency prep (water pouches, food rations, and first-aid gear) into a distinct, bombproof case that protects the contents from moisture or being crushed. You can toss it in the trunk and forget about it until the moment you really need it.

The integrated handles and wheels are great for easy transfer between cars or garages and the neatly organized bags, and instructions inside all but ensure you'll be better prepared than anyone in the neighborhood if you ever do end up needing it.

Industry observers note that according to the FTC, a product must be “all or virtually all” made in the United States. That means final assembly and significant processing happen in the USA, and nearly all components are made and sourced in the USA.

According to recent reports, no. “Assembled in the USA” means the product was put together in the USA, but some parts may come from other countries.

Look for the product’s country-of-origin information and check the manufacturer’s website for details about where it is made, assembled, and sourced.

There are a lot of reasons why, but mainly because shopping U.S.-made goods means you are supporting domestic manufacturers, workers, supply chains.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase.
  • The enhancement, of course, also adds latest content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.
  • Recent findings suggest that we’ve known about the new content side of today’s patch for quite some time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase. The game received a major enhancement earlier today, version 1.1.2.0, which delivers a host of changes to the game, many of which have been expected.

The enhancement, of course, also adds latest content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve known about the new content side of today’s patch for quite some time. The update kicks off the California Resistance stage of Season 1, which is the second of three. The new Eastwood map takes place in California, and it’s a map cut from the larger Battlefield Redsec battle royale map of Fort Lyndon.

There’s a upcoming limited-time mode called Sabotage - a tactical, 8v8 mode where two teams attempt to destroy as many bomb sites as possible. The other big new feature that arrives today is Battle Pickups.

According to recent reports, these are powerful weapons which can be found in specific game modes (and in Portal), scattered around the map for players to pick up and use. They have limited ammo that cannot be replenished, and deliver incredible firepower.

Industry observers note that redsec players have a latest Gauntlet mission to look forward to that joins the existing modes. It’s called Rodeo and it involves a lot of vehicular action. Finally, everyone gets to unlock two new weapons: the the DB-12 shotgun, and the M327 Trait revolver sidearm. There’s also a new angled grip attachment.

The fixes and tweaks side of the patch is arguably the more interesting. Controller aim assist has received a massive overhaul that essentially resets everything to open beta settings. The goal is to make infantry targeting more consistent.

In a recent development, controller players actually get the bulk of the changes in this update, which also improves input latency and stick response. Several complications that reset aim assist values, or make it behave erratically, have been addressed.

The conversation around weapon bloom/spread doesn’t look like it’s ever going to end, because Battlefield Studios is yet again tuning gunplay to fix unintended dispersion behaviour, and decrease its intensity across the board.

Certain Challenges have had their description rewritten so their requirements can be better understood. Beyond that, you can expect several deployables to behave much more consistently, including several bug fixes there, too.

Head to the official blog for the full rundown of patch 1.1.2.0.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated on November 17th, 2026 - Version: 2.1.20.

Sources indicate that want to know who you should deploy to protect your walking fortress? In our Fortress Saga tier list, we ranked all the available heroes so you can have a clear idea of who should be out on the field and who you shouldn't bother with (at all).

There are a lot of heroes in Fortress Saga. Many of them are good, but you do not have access to all of the best picks from the beginning. So, as is the case most of the time, you will probably end up upgrading some of the lower-rarity ones because you have no other choice.

Even if that is the case, the heroes that are ranked at the top of this Fortress Saga tier list are the ones you should try obtaining and upgrading ASAP. The second you get some of them, the rest is history. That's when the real game begins.

Since the game has been around for a while in Japan, this tier list is based on that, and I have adapted it to the Global server. I have also added explanations for some of the heroes underneath each tier, so if you're curious as to why some of the heroes rank the way they do, all you have to do is keep reading. Did you know we have the latest Fortress Saga codes? Go ahead and redeem them for some free goodies! Can you reroll in Fortress Saga? Some people might wonder about rerolling in this game, and that is just not worth your time. At the beginning, you don't have access to all the heroes anyway, so rerolling would just delete all your progress, account and everything else, while not getting any "good" heroes anyway. So, don't bother thinking about rerolling in Fortress Saga.

It has been revealed that now that we've got that out of the way, let's dive into the actual tier list so you can have a clear idea of which heroes to use on your team! S+ Tier  |  S tier  |  A Tier  |  B Tier  |  C Tier Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

Sources indicate that heroes at the top of the Fortress Saga tier list are a must-upgrade. I recommend you start with the first one you get (which is probably the only non-Legendary) and then upgrade the others as you get them.

Violet can summon Shadow Soldiers who fight battles for you. She is extremely good, especially since her passive can grant her summons a lot more damage and they can benefit from additional stats granted by other heroes. Malleus is a hero who works great against large clusters of enemies. He will jump to the area with the most enemies and deal a lot of damage, pulling them together. He can also buff allies with the Machina trait. Styria is a support, and she will recover allies' HP like no other. She can also shield allies, and just by being deployed, she will passively increase all allies' HP.

Winter is a beast in terms of AoE damage. This also knocks enemies back, and if the same enemy is hit by the skill four times, they become frozen. Zelos can deal some really good damage, but can also apply really good crowd control on enemies (Fear). He can stun bosses, so this hero works pretty well against them. He can passively absorb some HP based on the damage dealt, so he has a lot of sustain. Jibril is a burst damage dealer, and once her passive is unlocked, the flurry of projectiles can fly even further. She is great regardless of whether you face a single target or multiple enemies.

Soba amplifies allies' ATK with his passive, can deal quite high damage to enemies, and knocks them down. It's a decent hero if you don't have any better ones. Scarecrow is a Unique (blue) hero who is pretty good at all things. It can heal allies and then transform all the excess healing into a shield. Since it's a Unique hero, it can be upgraded fairly quickly, so that's why it lands in this tier. Ravia is a great AoE damage dealer and inflicts bleed on the opponent's hit. When they have low enough HP, she can execute them. It's great, especially against large waves of enemies, and when paired with more AoE heroes.

Sources indicate that bruce deals AoE damage based on his ATK. His passive amplifies all heroes' ATK, so that's great for a Unique hero. Loxia can apply crowd control on enemies hit. She is decent if you don't have any better damage dealers/passive buffers, preferably some from the higher-rated tiers. Bernhard comes with good AoE damage that shreds the enemies' DEF. He can also taunt them, and once you activate his passive, he will also become immune to crowd control. He could land in a higher tier if he has the right team (and versus the right enemies).

It has been revealed that as you can see, a lot of the other heroes land at the bottom of the Fortress Saga tier list. These are the heroes you should not bother with at all, regardless of their rank/upgrade status. There are plenty of Unique and Rare heroes in the higher tiers that you should focus on upgrading, so in my opinion, don't bother with these at all.

If you need to use some of them until you get an upgrade, that's fine, but otherwise, just try not to invest anything more than necessary into them because it's a waste of resources.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that in terms of current games, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is getting a long-requested New Game Plus thanks to a new revision coming on November 5.
  • This news comes a few days after Fresh Game Plus arrived in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has released a fall update on the Assassin’s Creed franchise, providing news big and small on its flagship series. The news includes updates for existing games and smaller but significant insights on the various upcoming Assassin’s Creed games previously announced.

Sources indicate that in terms of current games, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is getting a long-requested New Game Plus thanks to a new revision coming on November 5. This means you can start a fresh game while bringing over your progression items/level from your previous playthrough. This update will also introduce the following features:.

This news comes a few days after Fresh Game Plus arrived in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

Codname Invictis, a PvP multiplayer game, remains in development as Ubisoft shares it has incorporated feedback from players who, according to Ubisoft, “saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed.” To this end, Ubisoft has spent months reworking Invictis to reflect this vague feedback and say the game is “now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions.”.

Sources indicate that as for the next single-player Assassin’s Creed, Codename Hexe, Ubisoft says it will share the next major update on this game in 2027. First unveiled in 2022, Codename Hexe is set during the 17th-century reign of the Holy Roman Empire, and the era's witch hunts will play a significant role.

With the release of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this year, Ubisoft has given fans what they'll likely see as a disappointing upgrade on potential future remakes: “One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we right now have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development. Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring upcoming settings and stories.”.

However, Ubisoft adds that this door isn’t closed for good. “Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back,” says Ubisoft.

Ubisoft’s next update concerns the live-action Assassin's Creed series in production for Netflix. They say the show is “nearing completion” in Rome and that award-winning composer Hannah Peel (Insomnia, Rogue Agent, Game of Thrones: The Last Watch) is composing the score.

Lastly, Ubisoft teases substantial celebrations are planned for 2027, which marks the 20th anniversary of the Assassin's Creed franchise. It's keeping details to itself for now, but states it's "preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and community moments. ".

For more on Assassin's Creed, check out our review of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

BYD Is Winning Over Japan With A Very Japanese Kind Of EV

💡 Key Takeaways
  • BYD’s latest milestone in Japan would barely register on its sales charts back home in China.
  • According to recent reports, the Chinese automaker unveiled that its cumulative Japanese passenger-car sales had passed 10,000.
  • It has been revealed that it was bold to challenge Japan’s homegrown manufacturers with something designed specifically for their market and to create the world’s first kei car from a non-Japanese automaker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD’s latest milestone in Japan would barely register on its sales charts back home in China. But selling 10,000 cars in a country dominated by domestic brands is progress, especially when part of that momentum comes from selling a vehicle tailored to what Japanese buyers actually want: a small, practical box on wheels, which also happens to be electric.

According to recent reports, the Chinese automaker unveiled that its cumulative Japanese passenger-car sales had passed 10,000. Its first 5,000 took roughly two and a half years after deliveries began in January 2023. The next 5,000 took about 15 months. That includes its entire lineup, rather than just its newest and arguably most interesting addition: the Racco electric kei car.

It has been revealed that it was bold to challenge Japan’s homegrown manufacturers with something designed specifically for their market and to create the world’s first kei car from a non-Japanese automaker. The Racco’s tall body, tiny footprint, and sliding rear doors follow the familiar Japanese formula for such vehicles. BYD didn’t need to reinvent anything, but its entry needed to be convincing.

Japanese buyers’ initial response to the Racco was encouraging. Launched on July 28, it attracted 1,002 orders in two weeks, the fastest order intake of any BYD model in Japan. By the end of August, that had grown to around 1,500. Roughly 80% of buyers chose the range-topping 300 Premium, clearly showing that the cheapest version was less attractive.

In a recent development, BYD credited the Racco with helping deliver record monthly orders across its Japanese lineup in August. Potential buyers who came to see the little EV ended up discovering its other models, too.

BYD offers six passenger-car models in Japan, and every one has a charging port. Five are fully electric: the Racco kei car, Dolphin hatchback, Seal sedan, Atto 3 crossover, and Sealion 7 SUV. The sixth, the Sealion 6 SUV, is a plug-in hybrid combining a gasoline engine with electric propulsion. That makes the entire lineup electrified, with no gasoline-only cars or conventional, non-plug-in hybrids on offer.

According to recent reports, what’s more interesting is comparing the Racco’s sales performance to its main rival, the Nissan Sakura EV, which is also Japan’s best-selling electric car. In October, the Sakura EV sold 878 units, while the Racco sold 607. That’s almost 70% of the volume, marking a 37% rise over September.

According to recent reports, the Nissan Sakura EV was Japan’s electric bestseller for a fourth consecutive year in 2025, but it could lose its crown to the Racco, which gives buyers more battery for less money, at least before subsidies. It starts at ¥2.145 million with a 22.4-kWh pack and 130 miles (210 kilometers) of WLTC range, while the Sakura starts at ¥2.449 million with a 20-kWh battery and 112 miles (180 km).

It has been revealed that even the longer-range Racco, with a 35.8-kWh pack capable of 199 miles (320 km), undercuts the entry-level Nissan at ¥2.398 million. The BYD also gets sliding rear doors instead of the Nissan’s conventional ones. What could help the Sakura stay ahead is the larger government subsidy it benefits from, which can make it cheaper to buy despite its higher sticker price.

It’s a tad early to call the Racco a Japanese sensation, but buyers are clearly interested. This newcomer is already selling roughly seven cars for every ten Sakuras in one month, so it definitely deserves attention.

#17370. Motorcycles are notoriously dangerous. Could electric motorcycles actually change that?

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1732 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Motorcycles are notoriously dangerous. Could electric motorcycles actually change that?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1732 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There’s no particularly comfortable way to talk about motorcycle safety.
  • According to recent reports, but that simple statement also hides something key.
  • Recent findings suggest that not because electricity is somehow safer than gasoline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s no particularly comfortable way to talk about motorcycle safety. Motorcycles are dangerous. All the statistics point to the fact that per mile, motorcycles are significantly more dangerous. And as someone who promotes them as a better alternative to large cars and trucks for many trips, it’s an uncomfortable reality that must be grappled with.

According to recent reports, but that simple statement also hides something key. Not all motorcycles, riders, or riding behaviors carry the same risk. And as a latest generation of smaller electric motorcycles begins to emerge, I think there’s an interesting question worth asking: Could electric motorcycles inadvertently make motorcycling safer?

Recent findings suggest that not because electricity is somehow safer than gasoline. It isn’t. Rather, because electrification may fundamentally change the type of motorcycle that hits the road.

In 2024, 6,228 motorcyclists were killed in the US, accounting for 16% of all traffic fatalities, according to the NHTSA.

Recent findings suggest that obviously, motorcycles have a fundamental disadvantage here. You don’t have a steel cage around you. There aren’t crumple zones separating your body from an oncoming SUV. There’s no seatbelt holding you in place or curtain airbag waiting to catch your head.

But there’s another component to motorcycle fatalities that is harder to ignore: rider behavior.

Industry observers note that around 35% of motorcyclist deaths in 2024 occurred in single-vehicle crashes, according to the IIHS. In other words, more than one-third of those deaths didn’t involve a rider being hit by another vehicle. At that point, whether or not a crash occurred was essentially in the hands of the rider.

Alcohol is another major factor. Among riders killed in single-vehicle crashes, the NHTSA reports that 40% were alcohol-impaired.

Then there are the bikes themselves.

Supersport motorcycles stand out for all the wrong reasons. Of the riders killed on supersports in 2024, 59% were under 30. Compare that to cruiser and standard motorcycles, where just 19% of killed riders were under 30, or touring motorcycles at only 7%.

That’s not proof that powerful motorcycles are causing those deaths, of course. There are all sorts of confounding factors, including the type of person attracted to different motorcycles and how those motorcycles tend to be ridden.

But it’s hard to ignore the broader picture.

Sources indicate that to put it more plainly, a huge portion of motorcycle deaths are caused by riders simply going too fast, doing something wrong (like drinking or taking turns too aggressively), or because they couldn’t handle the power of an insanely high-performance crotch rocket. So while figures such as “motorcycles are 27x more deadly than cars” might be true in a broad sense, that doesn’t mean you have a 27x higher chance of death – especially not if you aren’t a 25-year-old hooligan on a second-hand liter bike.

One of the strange things about motorcycling is just how cheaply you can buy extraordinary performance.

In a recent development, someone with relatively little riding experience can buy a used supersport capable of acceleration that would have required an exotic supercar not long ago. The motorcycle may weigh around 400 lb, produce well over 100 horsepower, and be capable of speeds approaching three times a typical US highway speed limit.

And unlike cars, there isn’t much protecting you when that performance gets away from you.

That’s why I find the current evolution of electric motorcycles so interesting.

In a recent development, for years, electric motorcycle companies largely chased gasoline motorcycles up the performance ladder. We got incredibly fast and powerful machines from companies like Energica and LiveWire.

Those bikes proved electric motorcycles could be fast.

But I’m increasingly interested in the opposite end of the spectrum.

Look at motorcycles such as LiveWire’s upcoming S4 Honcho.

This isn’t an electric superbike designed around insane acceleration or a 150 mph (240 km/h) top speed. It’s a smaller motorcycle intended to offer approachable performance at a more accessible price.

It adds to a growing market already populated by highly acclaimed modest-sized electric motorcycles like those from Ryvid, Land, and Maeving.

And we’re seeing more machines begin to occupy this previously neglected territory between an e-bike and a full-size motorcycle.

That could make a huge difference when it comes to overall safety, as crotch rockets get replaced by sensible electric motorbikes.

Battery technology actually creates an interesting incentive here. Making an electric motorcycle ridiculously powerful is easy. Giving it enough battery to sustain high speeds for long distances without becoming extremely heavy and expensive is much, much harder.

So the economics and physics of batteries naturally make smaller urban and suburban motorcycles fairly compelling right now.

Instead of asking how to build another 150 mph (240 km/h) electric motorcycle, manufacturers can build a lighter machine that goes 60 or 70 mph (95-120 km/h), has enough range for everyday riding, and costs considerably less.

Ironically, one of the limitations most commonly leveled against electric motorcycles could turn out to have a safety upside.

This is where I think things get even more interesting.

According to recent reports, for decades, the stereotypical progression into motorcycling might have involved learning on a dirt bike or small displacement motorcycle, then moving fairly quickly into larger machines. Often though, new riders simply took a licensing course and then bought their first 600cc sport bike to learn to ride.

But now we’re raising an entirely new generation on electric two-wheelers.

Sources indicate that kids and teenagers are increasingly growing up riding e-bikes and small electric motos. Eventually, many of them are going to want something faster than a 20 or 28 mph e-bike.

A 50 mph (80 km/h) electric motorcycle is a pretty logical next step for the e-moto kids of today. Eventually, perhaps that rider graduates to something capable of 70 or 80 mph (120-130 km/h) and comfortable highway travel.

That’s a much more gradual performance curve than jumping from essentially no powered two-wheeler experience to a screaming 600cc supersport.

There’s another advantage too: electric motorcycles are mechanically easier to operate. There’s generally no clutch, no gearbox, and no concern about stalling. Twist the throttle and go.

That doesn’t necessarily make them safer – instant electric torque can certainly get an inexperienced rider into trouble – but it does remove several tasks from the mental workload of learning to ride.

The rider can spend more attention on braking, cornering, traffic, positioning, and the thousand other things that actually keep you alive on a motorcycle. The reduction in cognitive load can mean more focus on control, if it’s used that way.

To be clear, I’m not arguing that electric motorcycles are inherently safe.

In a recent development, they’re still motorcycles and they still lack cages. Well, most of them.

If an inattentive driver turns left in front of you, the chemistry powering your rear wheel isn’t going to make much difference.

Recent findings suggest that and electric motorcycles can be outrageously powerful. In fact, the instantaneous torque of an electric motor can make poor throttle calibration especially unforgiving for inexperienced riders.

There also simply isn’t enough data yet to demonstrate that electric motorcycles have meaningfully lower fatality rates than comparable gasoline motorcycles.

But that’s not really my argument.

According to recent reports, my argument is that electrification may change what we consider a normal beginner motorcycle. And that could be much more important, helping to significantly reduce accidents and deaths.

Recent findings suggest that I’m never going to pretend motorcycles can become as safe as cars. The physics simply don’t work that way.

But the broad statistic of “motorcycles are dangerous” encompasses an enormous spectrum of machines and riders.

A sober, trained commuter wearing proper protective gear and riding a modestly powered motorcycle to work is doing something fundamentally different from an inexperienced 21-year-old seeing how fast his supersport can take an empty freeway ramp at 2 a.m.

Yet both contribute to the same broad motorcycle fatality statistics.

Sources indicate that what excites me about this emerging generation of electric motorcycles isn’t that swapping gasoline for batteries magically fixes motorcycle safety. It obviously doesn’t.

In a recent development, i appreciate your argument, but i highly doubt that Electric motorcycles will make things safer. A few key points.

Sources indicate that look at eBikes (from this point on i will refer to both eBike and electric motorcycles as eBikes for simplicity). Low speed low power tons of accidents since they are cheap to get.

You mentioned rider experience and skill. one of the biggest issues is not just speed but torque. thats why even low powered bikes are so dangerous to those who are inexperienced. eBikes (and cheap eBikes) have a lot of torque. This makes them harder to handle.

Many riders shy away from ebikes because they dont have the feel or the sound of a gas bike. Over time, just like cars, this will change. And these rides will relish the high power and torque of an ebike.

Its just a lot cheaper to make a lot of power from an electric motor.

It has been revealed that overall i totally fail to see eBikes making a long term play at safety. that remarked I have not see the statistics and time will tell.

It’s that electrification could help create a fresh category of desirable, affordable motorcycles that don’t need 120 horsepower and a 160 mph top speed to be cool.

If younger riders grow up progressing from e-bikes to small e-motos and then to highway-capable electric motorcycles, perhaps we’ll wind up with a generation that sees a lightweight 60 or 70 mph motorcycle as a perfectly legitimate machine rather than merely a stepping stone to something ridiculously powerful.

Maybe electrification’s biggest contribution to motorcycle safety won’t be traction control, ABS, or sophisticated electronics.

Maybe it’ll simply make sensible motorcycles fun and cool again.

Treyarch Lays Off Call of Duty Zombies Mastermind Craig Houston After 20 Years

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Craig Houston, the writer behind much of Call of Duty’s Zombies storyline, has been laid off by Treyarch after around 20 years at the studio.
  • He shared the news himself on Friday via X and LinkedIn, and I have to say, it’s a rather graceful message considering the circumstances.
  • He didn’t go into the reasons, but it appears to be part of the huge Xbox restructuring announced earlier this year, which is set to affect 3,200 jobs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Craig Houston, the writer behind much of Call of Duty’s Zombies storyline, has been laid off by Treyarch after around 20 years at the studio.

He shared the news himself on Friday via X and LinkedIn, and I have to say, it’s a rather graceful message considering the circumstances. Houston said he was proud and privileged to have worked alongside so many talented people, many of whom will remain friends for life, before thanking fans for their enthusiasm, support and kind words over the years. On X, he posted it alongside a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch, featuring footage from many of the games he worked on, which makes the whole thing feel a little more bittersweet.

He didn’t go into the reasons, but it appears to be part of the huge Xbox restructuring announced earlier this year, which is set to affect 3,200 jobs. Treyarch sits under Activision Blizzard, which in turn is owned by Xbox, so it isn’t a huge surprise that the cuts have reached the studio. Still, seeing a name like his on the list stings, especially if you’ve spent any amount of time shooting zombies with your friends at 2 in the morning.

For those who don’t know him by name, and I suspect that’s quite a few people, Houston has been at Treyarch since 2006. His first Call of Duty there was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor, which is a pretty humble start for someone who would go on to shape one of the series’ biggest modes. From World at War in 2008 onwards, he was the main writer for Zombies, whilst also writing for Treyarch’s campaigns.

It has been revealed that he is credited as a writer and designer on Black Ops 1 through 4, and later as part of the design and creative development teams on the likes of Cold War, Black Ops 6 and Black Ops 7. Interestingly, he isn’t credited on this year’s Modern Warfare 4.

Zombies obviously wasn’t a one-man show, with Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell and Kevin Drew all being a massive part of how the mode evolved. Houston’s writing is what a lot of fans point to when they talk about why they fell in love with the characters, though. He also wrote the jingles for the original perks introduced in Verrückt, which is one of my favourite details in all of this. If you’ve ever caught yourself singing along to a vending machine whilst a horde closes in on you, that one’s on him.

Recent findings suggest that the response since Friday has been lovely to see. Former Treyarch developer Tony Flame replied to Houston’s post calling him a legend and saying it was an honour to work with him, adding that he created a truly special experience that will live on for millions of fans. Over on Reddit, one fan described him as a great guy, noting that you can tell how much he loves the story and characters he writes simply by how excited he gets when talking about them in promo material.

Many fans argue that Houston never quite got the recognition he deserved. In the wake of this announcement, many people admitted they hadn’t really been aware of him until after Black Ops 3, despite him having been there since the very beginning, and I think that’s true for a lot of us players. We tend to know the directors and the faces from the trailers, whilst the people writing the lines we end up quoting for years stay in the background. Zombies a mode spawned out of passion, and it’s hard to see someone fundamentally involved with that leave.

Truth be told, this is the part of the Xbox restructuring that I find hardest to get my head around. Twenty years of knowing a story inside out, including every timeline, every character and every twist, isn’t something a studio can simply hire back in. Of course, I don’t know the reasoning behind this particular decision, and Houston himself hasn’t mentioned a bad word about Treyarch. It is, however, a reminder that these layoff numbers are made up of people, some of whom have been shaping the games we love for the last two decades.

Recent findings suggest that houston hasn’t said what he prepares to do next. Whatever it ends up being, I hope it involves writing, and ideally a jingle or two.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has announced that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.
  • Recent findings suggest that this is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play.
  • Sources indicate that the Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has announced that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.

Recent findings suggest that this is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play. Redsec, however, offers modes like battle royale and Gauntlet, which aren’t quite the traditional Battlefield experience.

Sources indicate that the Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25. It will run for one week, ending the following Tuesday, December 2. The trial will be available on all platforms, but won’t include all content from the full game.

Instead, players will have access to three of the game’s maps and five of its modes. Siege of Cairo will be there alongside Season 1’s two fresh maps: Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields. It’s not the strongest line-up of maps, considering Eastwood is already cut from the larger Fort Lyndon battle royale map that Redsec players should be quite familiar with, but it’s something.

As for modes, you can pick from Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch. Battlefield Studios didn’t say what the fifth mode is going to be, but a dedicated blog post with more information is set to arrive next week.

It has been revealed that beyond the trial's content itself, the timing is certainly great. Battlefield 6 just received one of its biggest patches, kicking off the second phase of its first season. So far this season, we’ve seen two new maps, several new weapons - but more importantly, solutions to problems the game’s had since launch, as well as fixes to longstanding bugs.

The miserable XP progression Battlefield 6 launched with is far more tolerable. Challenges and Assignments are much easier to understand and actually finish. The often maligned weapon dispersion has been toned down. Some of the wildest vehicle bugs have been fixed. And Portal has a host of experiences that go beyond just bot farms.

In essence, Battlefield 6 feels like its reached its 1.0 status, which makes this a great entry point for fresh players, even if the trial could've used more of the game's better maps.

With its simple gameplay at first glance, Garden Tower Defense doesn't exactly scream "challenging"; however, the moment you dive into your very first stage, you'll be convinced otherwise (not to mention totally get schooled and humbled).

With such difficult opponents, you'll soon wonder which units you should deploy to keep your defence intact - and that's where our Garden Tower Defense tier list comes into play. Industry observers note that so, are you eager to learn which plants give you the most bang for your buck? You'll find out on the following pages - or better yet, why not claim the latest Garden Tower Defense codes too, so you can really get a proper head start?

It has been revealed that right then - let's take a look at the complete Garden TD tier list! S+ Tier  |  S Tier  |  A Tier  |  B Tier  |  C Tier Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

Sources indicate that as you might have guessed, some of the strongest plants in our Garden Tower Defense tier list belong right here. Here you'll find powerful AoE damage dealers like all the Significant Mushroom varieties, which are simply fun to play!

We also have the Lucky Clover, which is a Support, and probably one of the best ones out there. As the name suggests, it boosts your Luck.

Hellroot is one absolutely amazing AoE, which also deals DoT (burn). It's definitely the best of both worlds for AoE and ST.

Corn is okay, but it is not as good as Juggercorn, which not only has higher flat stats, but also better range.

Doompetal is one of my personal favourites, and even though it is not in the S+ tier, it can still deal considerable damage, especially against single targets.

Recent findings suggest that the Laser Plant is lower-rarity than most of the others, but it works almost as well. It costs as much as the Confusion Plant to deploy (1500), but it deals good damage and has a pretty low cooldown.

It has been revealed that some of the plants in the A tier are pretty good, but despite some of them being rarer than others, they aren't quite as "wow". The Glass Sunflower is okay, but its damage is not that great.

As for the Pesticider, it could rank higher, but it has such a high deploy cost (3000) that it's simply not practical - there are better and cheaper options out there for sure.

The Venus Floortrap is a rare plant, and you shouldn't confuse it with the Venus Flytrap, which is a lot rarer. The Floortrap is a "Trap", and it does pretty high damage considering how common it is.

Many of these plants are viable early on, especially the Ghost Pepper - this one does really good damage for its rarity, and it's also super cheap (400).

Cherries might not seem that strong early on, but if you max them, they can deal significant damage to any opponent, especially bosses.

Durian is known for its signature "aroma" (a.k.a. insane smell), hence earning its place in our Garden Tower Defense tier list. It deals AoE damage, but it's ranked in the B tier because it has a pretty high cost for what it does.

The plants in this tier you won't use for very long. The Tomato is your starter plant, and although it's super cheap, it doesn't do much - it focuses on a single target, so you will swap them out as soon as you get something better.

As for the rest, it's pretty much the same story for all of them.

And there you have it - we've always known how beneficial plants are in real life, but our Garden Tower Defense tier list takes it a step further by ranking which ones are even more beneficial than others, doesn't it?

  • Industry observers note that stewart will always be a crucial voice and face in the legacy of sci-fi entertainment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to a report from The Hollywood Reporter, actor Sir Patrick Stewart has passed away at the age of 86. Stewart spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, shared that he died after “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.”.

Stewart was best known for his roles as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation (and its various spinoffs) and Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, but he did plenty of video game performing, too. Stewart played Emperor Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, one of the first characters you meet in the game, and Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. He also played Jean-Luc Picard in about 10 different Star Trek games and Charles Xavier in five different X-Men games.

Industry observers note that stewart will always be a crucial voice and face in the legacy of sci-fi entertainment. Jean-Luc Picard will undoubtedly be an enduring and notable character in the Star Trek franchise, and that's thanks to Stewart's portrayal of the starship captain. His portrayal of Charles Xavier also helped to legitimize the comic book movie, and he will appear again as the character in this year's upcoming Avengers: Doomsday.

Our thoughts are with his friends and family, and the millions of fans (of which I include myself) who are mourning his loss. Let's all drink some Earl Grey tea in his honor today.

According to recent reports, the most affordable Volkswagen ID. Polo Trend starts at just €24,995, or about $27,500, but you’ll have to wait close to two years to get one.

The new ID. Polo is “an affordable friend for everyday life,” as Volkswagen’s chief designer Andreas Mindt calls it.

After opening orders for the ID. Polo with the 52 kWh battery at the end of April, starting at 33,795 euros ($37,000), Volkswagen made good on its promise, launching the lower-priced, smaller-battery model in July.

Industry observers note that the VW ID. Polo Trend with the 37 kWh battery went on sale in Europe in July, starting at just 24,995 euros, or about $27,500, with a WLTP range of 207 miles (334 km).

By mid-September, reports claimed Volkswagen’s entry-level EV was already essentially sold out across actross all trims, with more than 30,000 orders and a 10-month waitlist.

According to recent reports, according to the latest patch from German automotive news outlet Edison Media, that number has doubled in about two months, and buyers now face delivery times of up to 21 months for the base ID. Polo Trend. Deliveries for the sporty GTI version are expected to be around seven months.

In a recent development, “We clearly planned too conservatively,” a VW manager told Edison during an interview. While VW expected about 90 to 95% to choose to lease, the leasing rate is only about 50%.

The larger 52 kWh battery version has also seen higher-than-expected demand, while 90% surprisingly opted to buy the optional €810 ($890) detachable towbar.

As a result, the organization is prioritizing higher-margin models, which is likely leading to longer delivery times for the base ID. Polo.

The entry-level variants “just clog up to the line,” Volkswagen’s manager mentioned during the recent interview.

Demand for the ID. Cross, the electric equivalent to Volkswagen’s T-Cross, is also already exceeding expectations.

How it could possibly take the makers of the Beetle and Golf (their two most successful products) to learn that small efficient relativity inexpensive cars would be popular (and their bloated ID4/5 things a bit of a flop) is hard to understand.

Of course all these cars too expensive to succeed out side the protectionist European market. Maybe they will work out how to be globally price competitive one day. I live in hope.

According to recent reports, volkswagen opened orders for the entry-level ID. Cross Trend last month, starting at €27,995 ($31,000) in Germany, including VAT. The 52 kWh battery version will go on sale in the UK this week, starting at £30,260 ($40,000). The ID. Cross Life with the 37 kWh battery will go on sale in January 2027, starting at £26,985 ($35,500).

Industry observers note that volkswagen’s new entry-level electric cars are off to a promising start. The electric urban car family, which includes the ID. Polo, ID. Cross, and the CUPRA Raval and Skoda Epiq, has received nearly 150,000 orders combined since production began in June.

However, the German automaker is still facing an uphill battle. The VW Group posted an operating loss of 5.9 billion euros ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its worst quarterly loss since the Dieselgate scandal.

In September, Volkswagen’s supervisory board approved its Future Initiative 2030, which calls for reducing its global workforce by up to 100,000, closing plants, and narrowing its vehicle lineup to cut costs.

In a recent development, not all commutes are created equal, and tackling a hard commute takes a lot more than a motor and a set of wheels. Ausom knows this better than most, with six highly capable, long-range electric scooters designed to handle your toughest trips. And this Black Friday, you can get the right tool for the job at the lowest prices of the year.
