#17345. 10 Games That Made Me Weirdly Passionate About Jobs I'd Never Want

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2165 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

10 Games That Made Me Weirdly Passionate About Jobs I'd Never Want

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2165 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some of my favourite games are, when you really think about it, just jobs.
  • The funny thing is that I wouldn't actually want any of these jobs.
  • Recent findings suggest that I had sunk many hours into both PowerWash Simulator games long before I ever held an actual pressure washer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some of my favourite games are, when you really think about it, just jobs. I have pressure-washed patios, stamped passports, hauled cargo across half of Europe and sold second-hand books out of a trailer, all of it voluntarily and in my free time. And boy, did I take every single one of them seriously!

The funny thing is that I wouldn't actually want any of these jobs. Some of them look like far too much hard work, others require a kind of patience I most definitely do not possess, and with one or two, I'm fairly certain I'd end up in prison. That is probably exactly what makes them so enjoyable from the safety of my sofa, so let's take a look at the ten games that made me weirdly passionate about jobs I'd never want.

Recent findings suggest that I had sunk many hours into both PowerWash Simulator games long before I ever held an actual pressure washer. That finally changed earlier this year, and I'm pleased to report that watching grime disappear is just as satisfying in real life as it is on screen. On a warm summer's day, it's even quite fun.

Industry observers note that still, there's a lot to be said for staying warm, dry and cozied up on the sofa whilst doing it. The game has an almost meditative quality that I couldn't quite find with a real hose in my hands, and that's no accident. Lead designer Nick McCarthy has said that the team left out certain real-world inconveniences on purpose, and I'm grateful for every single one of them.

Recent findings suggest that futurLab released the sequel on 23 October 2025, bringing 38 new jobs to Muckingham, online co-op for up to four players and new tools like an abseiling rig and a cherry picker. There are also two kittens named Bubbles and Squeak, which was frankly all the convincing I needed. As an actual career, though, it looks like an awful lot of work, so I'll stick to the version without the wet socks.

Papers, Please's premise is incredibly dark and difficult: you are manning a booth at the border of the fictional Eastern Bloc country of Arstotzka. It's 1982, and as a border inspector, it is your responsibility to check passports, permits and anything else that gets slid across your desk. Make a mistake and you get a wage deduction. Your family, meanwhile, desperately needs that money. The game is, however, also tense and brilliant, and it also taught me that I would be entirely unsuited for the job.

Quite frankly, I'm just not enough of a bootlicker for it. I'm far too nice, and my first instinct is to wave everybody through, which is not something Papers, Please looks kindly upon. Being generous with your stamp sooner or later gets you killed by your own government, and it's hard to build a career on that.

Note: Lucas Pope worked on the Uncharted series at Naughty Dog before making a game that's almost entirely about paperwork.

Sources indicate that by its tenth anniversary in 2023, the game had sold over five million copies, so there are clearly plenty of people out there who are much better at saying no than I am. I have a lot of respect for them. I'd just rather not meet them at passport control.

Running a late-night coffee shop in an alternative version of Seattle sounds like a dream. Even more so when you consider that your visitors will consist of elves, orcs and mermaids that are living alongside humans. Coffee is the great connector here, since the need for a warm drink and someone to talk to is universal across every race. Toge Productions chose Seattle because Starbucks first opened there, and also because the rain sets the mood so well. It's easily one of the coziest games I own.

Parts of this job would actually suit me extremely well: I enjoy good banter, I'm perfectly happy with small talk, and I seem to have the kind of approachable face that makes strangers trauma dump on me far more often than you'd expect. If being a barista was only about listening, I'd be employee of the month.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, you also have to make the coffee, and Coffee Talk is the game that revealed me just how hilariously bad I am at latte art. Nothing I produce looks like it was made on purpose. So as much as I love the idea, I could never run a coffee shop of my own.

Note: Creator Mohammad Fahmi sadly passed away in March 2022. He pitched the game as holding a warm cup of coffee by a window whilst it rains outside and lo-fi music plays in the background, which is exactly how it feels.

Industry observers note that stardew Valley is meant to be about running a cute little farm with cute little animals on it. The way I play it, with spreadsheets at the ready and more wiki tabs open than I'd like to admit, has very little to do with that. My approach is a lot closer to a general planning a war than a farmer enjoying the countryside.

The forensic intensity I bring to this game does scare me a little. Every day is planned, every crop has to earn its place, and my poor character hasn't had a quiet afternoon in years. If I ran a real farm like that, I'd work myself into a burnout before the first harvest.

Note: Eric Barone, better known as ConcernedApe, made Stardew Valley on his own over roughly four years.

Recent findings suggest that the game turned ten on 26 February 2026 and has sold around 50 million copies. I'd love to know how many of those players are peacefully watering their parsnips and enjoying the sunset, and how many are like me. I have my suspicions.

It has been revealed that something happens to me whenever I open Euro Truck Simulator 2. Within minutes, I turn into a 60-year-old trucker who has been doing this for decades, completely locked in, with nothing on my mind except my cargo and the motorway ahead. I can't explain it, but it awakens something in me.

Recent findings suggest that there are two wolves inside of me: One is a sweet softie, and the other one is a fourth-generation trucker that graduated from the school of hard knocks, living and breathing 18-wheelers. Sadly for the second wolf, I'm really, really bad at parking, and truth be told, I'm no better at it in the game. That feels like a bit of a dealbreaker for a job that ends with reversing a trailer into a loading bay.

SCS Software first released the game at retail in autumn 2012, before it arrived on Steam on 16 January 2013. By its tenth birthday, it had sold over 13 million copies, and players had bought DLC more than 80 million times. Clearly, I'm not the only one with a trucker wolf, so at least I'm in good manufacturer.

Exterminauts is an upcoming co-op shooter from Behaviour Interactive, the studio behind Dead by Daylight, and it hands you several jobs at once. As part of a crew of three, you clock in, take on MegaCorp contracts, repair what's broken and exterminate alien pests along the way. It was revealed at gamescom Opening Night Live in August 2026 and is planned for 2027.

Anyone who has watched me deal with a woodlouse or a spider knows that pest control isn't my calling. I'm quite a caring person, so I had a lot of fun with the healing side of things. I've also discovered that I'm alarmingly quick to shoot my own teammates, sometimes because they were being annoying, and sometimes entirely by accident.

Note: Friendly fire is on in Exterminauts, and swinging one of the bigger weapons around carelessly is enough to take a teammate down.

A colleague who keeps taking out the rest of the crew isn't much use to anyone, no matter how good her healing is. I can't imagine it going down well in a performance review, either. It's better for everyone if I stay off the payroll.

Industry observers note that subnautica is one of my favourite games of all time, which means I approach the deep ocean with a healthy dose of suspicion. Dave the Diver has done nothing but confirm that this is the correct attitude. You spend your days diving into the Blue Hole to catch fish, and the further down you go, the more things would like to eat you instead.

Sources indicate that once the sun sets, the second job begins, and you help chef Bancho run the sushi restaurant, serving customers and keeping the drinks coming. All of that after a full day of nearly being eaten by sharks! I’d be a horrible sushi tester on the basis of not liking fish, and I could also never be the waiter on the basis of lacking a good sense of balance.

Note: The restaurant is the idea of Dave's friend Cobra, a former arms dealer who now handles the business side of things. Naturally.

By September 2026, Dave the Diver had sold more than 10 million copies across all platforms, and I completely understand why. It's a wonderful game. It's also the best argument I've ever seen for staying on dry land and ordering takeaway.

Recent findings suggest that kerbal Space Program puts you in charge of a space program run by the Kerbals, little green aliens who are far braver than they have any right to be. You build rockets, launch them and watch most of them explode. I was oddly passionate about all of it, right up until the moment I finally made it into orbit.

I'm very aware that the game doesn't end there. It had taken me so long to reach that one milestone, though, that my passion fizzled out on the spot, and I decided that my work here was done. That's quite unusual for me, as I'm normally someone who needs to tick off every last goal.

A real head of a space program with that attitude wouldn't bode well for anyone. NASA worked with developer Squad on an asteroid mission update in 2014, and ESA followed with missions of its own in 2020, so the people who do this for a living are clearly made of sterner stuff than I am. I have a lot of respect for them, and I'm more than happy to watch from the ground.

Sources indicate that barbie Rewind was developed by Digital Eclipse, published by Atari and released on 12 November 2026. It is unfathomably fun. You get to decorate the DreamHouse with over 250 pieces of furniture and decor inspired by real Barbie playsets, from a classic pink vanity to a '90s inflatable chair. There are also 16 classic Barbie games from 1991 to 2007 included, one of which, Barbie: Vacation Adventure, had never been released before.

Truth be told, I think I'd make a good interior designer, and I think I'd enjoy it, too. In Barbie Rewind, you get to design to your heart's content, and nobody questions your choices. Ken, Teresa and Christie do pop in to ask for help, but none of them will ever tell you that your sofa is ugly.

Recent findings suggest that real clients are a different story. Even when something looks questionable at best, you have to go with the flow and keep them happy, and whilst you'd hope they trust your design decisions, there's absolutely no guarantee that they will. I don't think I have the temperament for that, and I'm fairly sure someone would end up wounded.

Industry observers note that in Tiny Bookshop, you leave everything behind to sell second-hand books out of a little trailer in the seaside town of Bookstonbury-by-the-Sea. Each morning, you pick a spot, stock your shelves and wait for the locals to wander in. Many of the books are real ones, which I love.

According to recent reports, I've worked in retail before, I'm quite a good salesperson, and I enjoy helping people find what they're looking for. The customers in Tiny Bookshop put that to the test, because a fair few of them behave as if it's their very first day on Earth. Not all of them, mind you, but enough of them describe the book they want so vaguely that it borders on nonsensical.

On top of that, everyone in town seems to need a favour. Community is key, of course, but I'm trying to run a bookshop here, and I'd quite like to be left alone to do it! Over half a million players have fallen in love with Tiny Bookshop, and it won three German Developer Awards in 2025, so this one might just be a me problem. I'd still end up scaring all of my customers away.

#17344. Tech Report: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1598 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A major study involving more than 750,000 pregnancies has uncovered an vital difference in the potential pregnancy risks of popular weight loss medications such as Ozempic and Wegovy.
  • Among women taking the same medications for weight management, researchers found no significant association with premature birth or other pregnancy complications examined in the study.
  • The findings suggest that diabetes itself, rather than the medications, may be responsible for the increased risk of early delivery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A major study involving more than 750,000 pregnancies has uncovered an vital difference in the potential pregnancy risks of popular weight loss medications such as Ozempic and Wegovy. Women who unintentionally used these drugs shortly before or during early pregnancy were more likely to give birth prematurely, but only when the medications had been prescribed to treat existing diabetes.

Among women taking the same medications for weight management, researchers found no significant association with premature birth or other pregnancy complications examined in the study.

The findings suggest that diabetes itself, rather than the medications, may be responsible for the increased risk of early delivery. The research was published in Human Reproduction Open, a leading journal in reproductive medicine.

Recent findings suggest that the medications examined included semaglutide (brand names: Ozempic, Wegovy) and liraglutide (Saxenda). Both belong to a widely used group of drugs known as GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs). Originally developed to manage type 2 diabetes, these medications also suppress appetite, making them effective treatments for weight loss. However, their safety during pregnancy has not been established.

Why Ozempic and Similar Drugs Raise Pregnancy Concerns.

Professor Henriette Svarre Nielsen, who led the research at the Department of Gynecology and Obstetrics at Copenhagen University Hospital Hvidovre in Hvidovre, Denmark, explained that the rapid rise in GLP-1 prescriptions has created an urgent need for better information about pregnancy exposure.

Industry observers note that "GLP-1 RA treatment has, within the last few years, become the medication with the sharpest increase in prescriptions worldwide. Current guidance suggests the treatment should be stopped eight weeks prior to planning a pregnancy. However, this is based on early-phase model organism studies, and not real-world evidence. Nonetheless, because of its widespread adoption, inadvertent exposure in early pregnancy is inevitable, and there is hardly any evidence to guide clinical counseling when it happens.".

Sources indicate that to investigate these concerns, researchers examined whether accidental exposure to GLP-1 medications around conception was associated with complications during pregnancy. They focused on preterm birth (birth before 37 weeks), pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, delivering a baby that was unusually large for its gestational age, stillbirth, and placental problems.

Study Examines More Than 750,000 Pregnancies.

Sources indicate that the research team used Denmark's nationwide health registries to examine 756,636 pregnancies involving a single baby among 480,231 women. All pregnancies resulted in deliveries between October 1, 2009, and December 31, 2023.

The researchers classified a pregnancy as having possible accidental exposure to GLP-1 medications if the woman filled a prescription for semaglutide or liraglutide during the eight weeks before or after the first day of her last menstrual period.

This 16-week period included the time when a woman might not yet realize she was pregnant, as well as the early stages of fetal development when major organs begin to form.

Of the pregnancies included in the study, 529 involved prescription records indicating exposure to GLP-1 medications during this period.

To make the comparisons more reliable, the researchers accounted for several characteristics that could influence pregnancy outcomes. These included maternal age, body mass index (BMI), smoking habits, location, education, and whether the woman already had diabetes. They also considered the month and year of pregnancy to account for possible seasonal patterns and changes over time.

Diabetes May Be the Key to Premature Birth Risk.

The results revealed a striking distinction between women prescribed GLP-1 drugs for diabetes and those using them for weight loss.

In a recent development, dr. Kathrine Hviid, the study's first author and a PhD student in the same department, remarked the findings could help shape future research and improve medical guidance for women who unknowingly use these drugs during early pregnancy.

"We made some extremely vital findings that have implications for future studies, such as randomized controlled trials of GLP-1 RA usage in pregnancy, and for clinical counseling.

Recent findings suggest that "We found that these medications were associated with an increased risk of preterm birth, but the risk was only present when the medication was used for diabetes treatment, and not for weight management. This suggests that the underlying condition of diabetes, rather than the medication, may be driving this association.".

At first, women with GLP-1 prescriptions appeared to experience several pregnancy complications more frequently than those without exposure. However, most of these associations were no longer statistically significant once the researchers accounted for other factors that could affect pregnancy outcomes.

The remaining significant association involved premature birth among women who had been prescribed liraglutide or semaglutide to manage diabetes.

Compared with women who had not been exposed to these medications, the adjusted odds of premature delivery were 70% higher among women taking liraglutide for diabetes and 84% higher among those taking semaglutide for diabetes.

The researchers' accompanying announcement also reported estimated increases of approximately 11% for semaglutide and 9% for liraglutide among women with pre-existing diabetes.

Crucially, the same elevated risk of premature birth was not observed when the medications were prescribed specifically for weight management.

This difference suggests that the underlying medical condition may play a larger role in pregnancy outcomes than exposure to the medications themselves.

What the Findings Mean for Women Taking GLP-1 Drugs.

It has been revealed that according to Professor Nielsen, future investigations must distinguish between women taking GLP-1 medications for diabetes and those using them for weight control. Combining these groups could obscure important differences in their underlying health and pregnancy risks.

In a recent development, "Future studies must take account of the reason a woman has been prescribed these medications, as the risks differ between women using GLP-1 RAs for diabetes versus weight management. This is one of the first studies to examine GLP-1 RA exposure in early pregnancy according to the reason for prescription. As more evidence accumulates, these findings will guide clinical counseling for women inadvertently exposed to GLP-1 RAs in early pregnancy. In Denmark, about 70% of people who use weight loss medications are women and so it is inevitable that some may take it without realizing they are pregnant.".

Although the results provide useful new information, Nielsen emphasized that additional research is necessary before changing existing medical recommendations.

In particular, the findings do not justify abandoning current guidance to discontinue GLP-1 medications before a planned pregnancy. They also do not provide enough evidence to establish newly introduced clinical counseling recommendations based on why the drugs were prescribed.

Vital Limitations of the Pregnancy Study.

One of the investigation's greatest strengths was its size, with health records covering more than three-quarters of a million pregnancies.

Industry observers note that however, the study was observational, meaning it could identify associations but could not determine whether GLP-1 medications directly caused premature births. Other factors, including the effects of diabetes itself, may help explain the results.

Another limitation was that the researchers relied on prescription records. Although they could determine whether a woman had filled a prescription, they could not confirm whether she had actually taken the medication.

The researchers nevertheless believe that most women who purchased the drugs were likely to have used them because of their substantial cost.

In a recent development, in Denmark, patients generally contribute toward the cost of GLP-1 injections, although government subsidies are available for diabetes treatment. For example, a 1mg injection of Wegovy or Ozempic (semaglutide) costs approximately €180 and €114, respectively, with the diabetes subsidy reflected in the lower price.

Dr. Hviid mentioned: "Because of the high cost, we assume that compliance is very high among the women prescribed GLP-1 RAs.".

Experts Call for More Individualized Pregnancy Guidance.

The findings also attracted attention from researchers outside Denmark.

Recent findings suggest that in an invited commentary published alongside the study, Drs. Yeyi Zhu and Monique Hedderson of Kaiser Permanente Northern California and the Center for Upstream Prevention of Adiposity and Diabetes Mellitus in Pleasanton, California, described the results as important additions to the growing research on GLP-1 medications and reproductive health.

They wrote that the findings "complement and extend an emerging evidence base on the reproductive safety of GLP-1 RAs.".

The researchers also emphasized that the distinction between diabetes treatment and weight management could help doctors provide more personalized advice to women who accidentally used these medications around conception.

"For clinicians, the study by Hviid et al. (2026) may inform preconception and early pregnancy counseling. The observation that elevated preterm birth risk was confined to women treated for diabetes, and not to those using GLP-1 receptor agonists for weight management, supports more balanced, individualized discussions with patients who may have experienced inadvertent periconceptional exposure. For patients with diabetes, the study reinforces the importance of recognizing diabetes as an key risk factor for obstetric complications and prioritizing metabolic health and glycemic management before and during pregnancy.".

Recent findings suggest that ultimately, the study highlights why a woman's underlying health conditions matter when evaluating the potential pregnancy risks of GLP-1 medications. While the findings offer some reassurance regarding accidental exposure among women using these drugs for weight loss, they do not establish that the medications are safe during pregnancy.

Further research will be needed to clarify the risks and determine how best to counsel women who become pregnant while using these increasingly popular treatments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Recent findings suggest that coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

It has been revealed that the game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

According to recent reports, as it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

#17340. AI supercharges laser physics with a stunning 250x speed boost

AI supercharges laser physics with a stunning 250x speed boost

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Simulating the complex behavior of light inside powerful laser systems requires enormous computing resources, making it difficult for researchers to predict and adjust laser performance quickly.
  • The advance focuses on a branch of physics called second-order nonlinear optics, also known as χ2 processes.
  • In a recent development, at SLAC's upgraded Linac Coherent Light Source (LCLS-II), laser pulses undergo a series of transformations before they can help produce X-rays.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Simulating the complex behavior of light inside powerful laser systems requires enormous computing resources, making it difficult for researchers to predict and adjust laser performance quickly. Now, scientists at Stanford University, the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory have developed an artificial intelligence model that dramatically accelerates these calculations. Using deep learning, the upcoming approach reproduces the results of conventional simulations in a fraction of the time while maintaining high accuracy across a wide variety of laser pulse shapes.

The advance focuses on a branch of physics called second-order nonlinear optics, also known as χ2 processes. These interactions occur when light waves exchange energy while traveling through specially designed crystals, allowing scientists to change the frequency of light and precisely control the shape of laser pulses. Such capabilities are particularly key at large scientific facilities that use lasers to generate intense X-rays.

How Laser Light Helps Generate Powerful X-Rays.

In a recent development, at SLAC's upgraded Linac Coherent Light Source (LCLS-II), laser pulses undergo a series of transformations before they can help produce X-rays. Infrared light is first converted into green light and then into ultraviolet (UV) light. The resulting UV pulse strikes a cathode, releasing a cluster of electrons that is accelerated and manipulated to generate powerful X-ray pulses.

It has been revealed that the precise timing and shape of the UV pulse help determine the characteristics of the electron bunch. Those characteristics, in turn, influence the quality of the X-rays that researchers use in scientific experiments. Accurately predicting the conversion of light between different frequencies is therefore an key part of optimizing the system.

The newly introduced AI approach, described in the journal Advanced Photonics, was developed specifically to model the nonlinear χ2 interactions involved in this frequency conversion process.

AI Replaces Time-Consuming Laser Calculations.

It has been revealed that traditionally, scientists simulate these interactions by solving a complex mathematical equation known as the nonlinear Schrödinger equation. A widely used technique called the split-step Fourier method (SSFM) calculates how light changes as it travels through a material, repeatedly switching between representations of the pulse in time and frequency.

It has been revealed that although the method produces accurate results, it demands substantial computing power. In the complete laser simulation examined by the researchers, this calculation alone accounts for approximately 95 percent of the total processing time.

In a recent development, to overcome that bottleneck, the team developed an AI model based on a type of recurrent neural network called LSTM (long short-term memory). Building on earlier research that used similar networks to predict how laser pulses travel through optical fibers, the scientists adapted the approach to handle more complicated interactions involving multiple light waves.

In a recent development, they tested the model using a process called noncollinear sum frequency generation, or SFG, in which three interconnected light fields evolve together inside a crystal. The simulations covered a wide variety of laser pulse shapes, providing a demanding test of the model's ability to reproduce complex optical behavior.

Sources indicate that one important innovation was the way the AI handles information. Rather than repeatedly converting calculations between time and frequency, as conventional simulations do, the neural network works entirely with a compressed representation of the light's frequency characteristics. This eliminates much of the repetitive computation that makes traditional methods slow.

Complex Laser Simulations in Just Milliseconds.

The results highlighted that the AI model could accurately recreate how laser pulses change over time and across different frequencies, even under particularly challenging conditions. These included pulses with pronounced gaps in their frequency spectra and strong variations in optical phase.

When the researchers processed multiple simulations together using graphics processing units, the average calculation time for each simulation dropped to just a few milliseconds. That represents an improvement of orders of magnitude over conventional methods, making it possible to obtain predictions far more promptly without substantially compromising accuracy.

The system also demonstrated an notable ability to capture the interconnected behavior of the light waves. When the AI accurately predicted the main output of the SFG process, its predictions for the other interacting fields were generally accurate as well. This suggests that the network learned important features of the overall interaction rather than simply reproducing one output.

Toward Smarter Lasers and Real-Time Control.

Beyond faster simulations, the researchers envision connecting AI models directly to operating laser systems. Their approach uses a modular design in which individual physical processes can be represented by separate trained neural networks. Combining these models could make it possible to predict the behavior of an entire experimental system while it is running.

One potential application is the creation of digital twins, detailed virtual models that mirror the behavior of real laser equipment. With sufficiently fast and accurate predictions, these systems could help researchers monitor experiments, anticipate changes, and adjust laser settings in response to changing conditions.

The technology could also support adaptive laser control and closer integration with diagnostic instruments that measure the results of experiments. By removing a major computational obstacle, the research brings the possibility of more responsive, precisely controlled laser systems closer to reality, with potential benefits for a wide range of scientific facilities that rely on powerful lasers.

The ES350h epitomizes the quiet luxury experience that the Lexus brand is known for. Its standard 244-hp hybrid powertrain is fuel-efficient but not particularly exciting. The same can be noted of the ES’s handling, which is tuned for comfort rather than for driving joy.

The cabin's environs are premium and offer similar interior space and amenities to rivals from Audi and BMW, but the ES starts at a lower price point than those two sporty sedans. The Lexus has credible competition from inside the Toyota ecosystem, though: the uniquely styled Crown sedan, which shares its platform and powertrain with the Lexus but starts at an even more attractive price.

Expert Tip: While Lexus stopped selling the V-6-powered ES when the car was redesigned for 2026, it did add an electric variant. We review the ES EV separately.

Compare the 2027 Lexus ES with the top vehicles in this segment with our newly introduced compare tool.

Lexus redesigned the ES for the 2026 model year, so the mid-size luxury sedan slides into 2027 without any changes.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying newly introduced.

The ES is offered only in ES350h hybrid guise. Front-wheel-drive models are powered by a hybrid powertrain consisting of a 2.5-liter four-cylinder and two electric motors that combine for 244 horsepower. A continuously variable automatic transmission is standard. All-wheel drive models get a third electric motor that powers the rear axle, but combined horsepower remains the same at 244 horsepower.

The ES has always been a smooth operator, and this generation is no different. Lexus says this newly introduced model has more chassis rigidity than older models, and more attention has been spent on reducing body vibrations. When we drove the ES350h, we were impressed by its ride quality, but noted that it's no sports sedan, as its handling is still easy-going rather than sharp-edged.

A 10-speaker stereo is standard, and a 17-speaker Mark Levinson premium stereo system is available as an option.

A host of driver-assistance features comes standard, including adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, and automatic high-beam headlamps.

Recent findings suggest that the latest HoYoverse Special Program has brought us big Genshin Impact news. Version Luna 3 has been fully revealed, continuing the Nod-Krai story. The new chapter arrives December 3 across all platforms.

Industry observers note that the Moon-Prayer Night is the big in-world festival, marking Dameselette's final night before she sets off for the moon. The new patch, of course, introduces new playable characters, one with an interesting mechanic.

The events of this fresh chapter take place following Rarcher of Solnari’s defeat. The victory has given way to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations, which brings various stalls to the Nasha Town, alongside a new souvenir stamp book where you can record your memories.

Industry observers note that all is not fine, however, as Alice and Nicole Reeyn come bearing some bad news about phantoms appearing across the Nod-Krai region at Teyvat's borders. There’s a mystery to be uncovered here, and your journey to do so won’t be a lonely one.

Sources indicate that the highly-anticipated Durin is at last the newly introduced playable character. A 5-Star Pyro Sword wielder, Durin can switch between two different forms: one lets him deal damage, while the other is best suited to supporting the team.

It has been revealed that durin was once a dragon, you see, who was later given a human body. This is why he’s able to switch forms. The more powerful, Abyssal-infused form can launch major attacks on single targets to boost his own Vaporize and Melt damage, while his support form reduces enemies’ Elemental Resistance and deals AoE Pyro damage.

Durin’s Story Quest will shed more light on that aspect of his life, and completing it earns you a reward for him. Speaking of quests, completing the Archon Quest will grant you 500 Primogems. As a member of Hexenzirkel, Durin and other characters can gain fresh powers when you complete more quests in Moon-Prayer Night.

This is a big new addition, and will affect Venti, Klee, Albedo, Mona, Razor, Fischl, and Sucrose - all of whom can become Hexerei characters. This ties into the new Hexerei Secret Rite effect, which will trigger when two or more Hexerei characters are present. The effect boosts the entire party’s combat effectiveness.

It has been revealed that the other new character in Luna 3 is Jahoda, a 4-Star Anemo Bow wielder who’s great at healing teammates and absorbing Elements, which she can then use to deal damage. The first phase of Luna 3 will feature Durin and Jahoda, alongside the return of Venti. The second phase sees no new character debuts, but does feature the return of Varesa and Xilonen.

Industry observers note that there’s more to get excited about in Luna 3, even if you don’t feel like spending most of your time in Nod-Krai. The Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event will take you back to Dragonspine, where you’ll find winter-theme minigames appropriate to an update cycle spanning December to January. This is how you can earn the 4-Star Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow, too.

Recent findings suggest that beyond that, you can also look forward to the Miliastra Wonderland UGC module getting new updates. The Wonderland Resource Center is where creators can get and share resources through the editing tool.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This morning, Nintendo shared some updates related to the Pikmin franchise and has officially claimed November 1 as Pikmin Day, starting today and moving forward presumably forever.

It has been revealed that aside from the announcement of Pikmin Day as a general idea, Pikmin creator Shigeru Miyamoto appeared on camera to remind everyone that Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is coming November 12. A free demo for the game, which will include one standard level and two Dandori Academy levels, will be available on November 2.

The Switch 2 version of the game (you can read Game Informer’s Pikmin 4 review here) will have improved visuals and take advantage of the Switch 2’s mic to let you say things like “Rush” and “Go to work” to Oatchi. The Dandori Academy side of the game is essentially time trials you can practice, and then on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, you will have one chance to post your best time. You can read more about the Switch 2 version of the game here.

It has been revealed that miyamoto also shared that the mobile game, Pikmin Bloom, is also getting a fairly substantial upgrade soon with secret caves. In Bloom, players will be able to find maps that reveal caves that you can send your Pikmin into to battle and find treasure. You can also find maps for Bloom by playing Pikmin 4. Caves will be coming to Pikmin Bloom later this year.

According to recent reports, the Pikmin Day presentation also reminded viewers that every Pikmin game is available on Switch and Switch 2, though no announcements or hints were made implying that Pikmin 1 and 2 would be coming to the Nintendo Switch Online subscription service, which includes GameCube games on Switch 2. Those games can be purchased individually on the eShop.

#17336. Tesla needs wireless charging fast, or its $30,000 Cybercab can’t charge at home

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1391 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla needs wireless charging fast, or its $30,000 Cybercab can’t charge at home

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1391 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, tesla is now taking orders for the $29,990 Cybercab, with the first deliveries expected in Austin next month.
  • The Cybercab has no onboard charger, so it only takes DC fast charging.
  • Industry observers note that when Tesla unveiled the Cybercab in 2024, Elon Musk said it wouldn’t even have a plug.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, tesla is now taking orders for the $29,990 Cybercab, with the first deliveries expected in Austin next month. But there’s a problem buyers should know about: they won’t be able to charge it at home.

The Cybercab has no onboard charger, so it only takes DC fast charging. And the wireless home charging pad Tesla has been teasing since 2023 still isn’t something you can buy.

Industry observers note that when Tesla unveiled the Cybercab in 2024, Elon Musk said it wouldn’t even have a plug. “It just goes over the inductive charger and charges,” he said on stage.

Sources indicate that that initiative didn’t survive production, or at least the current version in production. Cybercabs have a NACS charge port behind a panel in the rear bumper, and Tesla has been plugging Cybercabs into regular Superchargers in Austin since they joined the fleet.

Sources indicate that the bigger matter is what sits behind that port. Tesla confirmed to attendees at Tesla’s Austin launch event in September that Cybercab has no onboard charger, the box that turns the AC power coming out of your wall into DC power the battery can store.

No onboard charger means no Wall Connector. No Mobile Connector on a 120V outlet, and no Level 2 station at the mall either. If it isn’t a DC fast charger, the Cybercab can’t use it.

Industry observers note that for a robotaxi, deleting the onboard charger makes sense. It’s one less part to buy, cool, and carry around, and a fleet car spends its downtime at a depot, not in someone’s garage. Those little things help make the car more economical and efficient.

But Tesla is now selling the Cybercab to individuals.

As we reported last week, Tesla’s Cybercab autonomy agreement requires a $299 monthly subscription for the car to move at all. The same document puts charging squarely on the buyer: “You are responsible for registration, insurance, parking, charging, general cleaning and all other costs.”.

It also tells owners to “keep the vehicle charged and connected so over-the-air updates can install.” Connected to what, it doesn’t say.

The Cybercab Order Agreement limits the car to NACS DC fast charging, Superchargers included. It also says only the registered owner can use the Cybercab, and only while physically present in it for the entire trip.

The subscription agreement carves out one exception: when service is due, the Cybercab “will travel autonomously, unoccupied to a Tesla service center.” Nothing similar exists for charging.

It has been revealed that so you can’t send your Cybercab to a Supercharger at 2 a.m. while you sleep, which is the one thing a self-driving car should be great at. You’d have to ride along, sit in a two-seater at a Supercharger while it charges, and ride back home.

The obvious answer is the wireless home charger Tesla keeps promising.

Recent findings suggest that tesla first indicated what looked like a wireless home charging station during its Investor Day in March 2023. Later that year, chief designer Franz von Holzhausen confirmed the project on Jay Leno’s Garage, saying owners would “just drive over the pad in your garage” to start charging.

Tesla then filed patents for the charging pad and, after the Cybercab unveiling, released a video of it charging the robotaxi at 25 kW, claiming efficiency “well above 90%.” In February, the FCC granted Tesla a waiver to use ultra-wideband radios to guide the Cybercab onto the pad.

And that’s where it stops. Tesla has never sold the pad, never priced it, and never given it a launch date. It even gave up on wireless charging for the Cybertruck last year, even though the truck shipped with the connectors for it.

With deliveries estimated for December, Tesla has about six weeks to launch a home pad if it wants the first owners to charge in their own garage.

Tesla’s own plans for Cybercab charging revolve around fleet depots. In Austin, it filed plans for a hub on St. Elmo Road with 48 V4 Supercharger stalls in a first phase and cabinets to support 80 wireless chargers in a second.

Tesla could, in theory, let private owners use it. But with the owner-presence rule, that means riding to a depot across town and waiting there. That’s a Supercharger visit with extra steps.

The other route is a home DC charger, and those exist. We covered Sigenergy’s 25 kW bidirectional DC charging module last year, which bypasses a car’s onboard charger the same way a Supercharger does. Lunar Energy also announced a 25 kW home DC charger this year, but it’s not expected until mid-2027.

Neither is a plug-and-play answer. Sigenergy’s module is built to sit inside its SigenStor home battery system, which isn’t cheap, and Tesla would have to support third-party DC charging on a car it controls this tightly. Tesla could also build its own small DC wall unit. It hasn’t announced one, but CEO Elon Musk talked about integrating one into the Powerwall for years.

This is what happens when you take a vehicle designed for a fleet and sell it to consumers to hit a deadline. And let’s be honest, charging is probably not even in the top 5 of problems with selling the Cybercab to personal owners in its current state.

Musk promised a Cybercab would be sold to a customer for under $30,000 before 2027. Technically, he’s going to make it. But on the Q3 earnings call, he also remarked “the vast majority” of Cybercabs will stay Tesla-owned and run as transport-as-a-service. The car was clearly engineered around that, and deleting the onboard charger is the best example.

That saved Tesla money on every unit. The cost now lands on the few people buying one.

The CyberCab is not a serious or well thought-out product, for any purpose besides inflating someone's ego and being able to tell people it looks like it came from a pre-2000's movie about a dystopian future.

If you live in Austin next to a Supercharger, you’ll manage. But think about what Tesla is actually selling here: a self-driving car that can’t drive itself to charge, can’t charge in your garage, and needs you sitting in it at a Supercharger. That’s worse than owning a Model 3 with a Wall Connector, and it costs $299 a month on top.

Industry observers note that the fix exists in Tesla’s labs. It has the pad, the patents, and the FCC approval. It needs to ship it as a product, ideally bundled with the car, or change the contract to let the Cybercab go charge on its own.

In a recent development, will the first Cybercab owners get a wireless pad in December, or will they spend their evenings at Superchargers? And if it introduces, how much will it cost? The rare few home wireless chargers that have been sold to date have been quite expensive, and the value proposition of the Cybercab, which is presently basically a $300 a month lease with a $30,000 down payment, is already pretty awful.

If you’re buying an EV, how you charge it at home matters as much as the car itself, and pairing it with rooftop solar can cut your fuel costs to nearly zero. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. Scientists discover a common sugar may help cancer cells break free and spread

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1402 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A common sugar found in many foods and sweetened drinks may play an unexpected role in helping aggressive ovarian cancer spread.
  • Recent findings suggest that the findings, published in Nature Aging, reveal a previously unknown way that cancer cells can continue influencing a tumor even after treatment has stopped them from multiplying.
  • Industry observers note that "Some cancer cells that survive chemotherapy aren't dividing anymore, but they're still biologically active," said Aidan Cole, Ph.D., a postdoctoral fellow in the lab of Katherine Aird, Ph.D., at The Wistar Institute and first author on the study.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A common sugar found in many foods and sweetened drinks may play an unexpected role in helping aggressive ovarian cancer spread. Researchers at The Wistar Institute have discovered that cancer cells surviving chemotherapy can release fructose, which acts as a signal that encourages nearby tumor cells to break free and spread.

Recent findings suggest that the findings, published in Nature Aging, reveal a previously unknown way that cancer cells can continue influencing a tumor even after treatment has stopped them from multiplying. The discovery also raises important questions about whether dietary sugar and commonly prescribed cholesterol medications could affect how cancer progresses.

Industry observers note that "Some cancer cells that survive chemotherapy aren't dividing anymore, but they're still biologically active," said Aidan Cole, Ph.D., a postdoctoral fellow in the lab of Katherine Aird, Ph.D., at The Wistar Institute and first author on the study. "Instead, they continue to release molecules that send signals to nearby cells. Our study is among the first to show that a nutrient -- in this case, fructose -- can act as one of those signals.".

Why Ovarian Cancer Often Returns After Chemotherapy.

Industry observers note that most patients with ovarian cancer receive platinum-based chemotherapy, a treatment that uses drugs containing platinum to damage the DNA of cancer cells and prevent them from reproducing. Although many patients initially respond well, the cancer eventually returns in most cases. It also frequently spreads throughout the abdominal cavity, the space inside the abdomen that contains organs such as the stomach, intestines, and liver.

This spread, known as metastasis, is responsible for approximately 90% of ovarian cancer deaths. Understanding what allows cancer cells to escape from their original location and establish newly introduced tumors is therefore a major priority for researchers.

Previous studies have suggested that cancer cells surviving chemotherapy may contribute to recurrence even when they are no longer actively dividing. These surviving cells can continue producing and releasing a mixture of substances that influence the behavior of surrounding cells.

To investigate this process, Cole and his colleagues developed an experiment that separated the surviving cancer cells from the molecules they released. They discovered that these released substances, even without the surviving cells themselves, were enough to significantly increase cancer spread in a preclinical model.

"As far as we know, this is the first time anyone has shown, in a preclinical model rather than just a dish, that it's the molecules these cells release -- not the cells themselves -- that drive the cancer's spread," stated Cole.

A Common Sugar Emerges as a Surprising Cancer Signal.

In a recent development, the next challenge was identifying which substances were responsible for encouraging cancer cells to spread. The researchers discovered an unexpected culprit: fructose.

Industry observers note that fructose is a naturally occurring sugar found in fruit, honey, and other foods. It is also a component of table sugar and high fructose corn syrup, a sweetener frequently used in soft drinks and processed foods.

The study revealed that cancer cells surviving chemotherapy could produce fructose and release it into their surroundings. Rather than simply serving as an energy source, the sugar acted as a chemical messenger that encouraged neighboring cancer cells to become more capable of spreading.

Industry observers note that the researchers also uncovered another concerning possibility. In their preclinical experiments, consuming high amounts of fructose comparable to those found in sugary drinks could promote signals associated with cancer spread even without chemotherapy treatment.

Recent findings suggest that this observation suggests that diet might influence cancer progression through a mechanism scientists had not previously recognized. Fructose consumption is particularly relevant in the United States, where high fructose corn syrup can account for approximately 8% to 20% of daily calorie intake in some individuals.

Industry observers note that unlike many factors that influence cancer risk and progression, dietary fructose intake can be changed. That raises the possibility that nutritional strategies might eventually become part of efforts to limit cancer spread.

According to recent reports, however, researchers have not yet tested whether reducing fructose consumption improves outcomes in patients with ovarian cancer. The findings do not establish that eating sugar causes cancer to spread in humans, and additional research is needed before specific dietary recommendations can be made based on this mechanism.

How Fructose Helps Cancer Cells Break Free.

To understand how fructose encourages cancer spread, the researchers examined what happens inside cancer cells exposed to the sugar.

They used several advanced methods to investigate the biological changes involved, including a CRISPR screen. This technique allows scientists to systematically examine genes and identify which ones influence a particular cellular process.

The experiments revealed that fructose suppresses cholesterol production in neighboring cancer cells.

Although cholesterol is often discussed in connection with heart disease, it also serves essential functions throughout the body. It is an notable component of cell membranes, the thin outer layers that surround cells and help regulate how they interact with their environment.

Recent findings suggest that in this case, cholesterol helps maintain the connections that hold neighboring cells together. These connections act somewhat like biological glue, making it harder for cancer cells to separate from one another.

Sources indicate that when fructose reduces cholesterol production, those connections weaken. As a result, cancer cells can detach more easily, potentially allowing them to escape and spread to other locations.

This discovery provides a possible explanation for how a common nutrient can influence one of the most dangerous aspects of cancer.

A Surprising Connection Between Statins and Cancer Spread.

The cholesterol finding also led researchers to investigate an unexpected question involving statins, medications widely prescribed to lower cholesterol.

Recent findings suggest that approximately 39 million people in the United States take statins. These drugs work by reducing the body's production of cholesterol and are commonly used to lower the risk of heart attacks and strokes.

Because fructose appeared to promote cancer spread by suppressing cholesterol production, the research team wanted to know whether statins might produce similar effects.

Their experiments demonstrated that statins alone could weaken the connections between cancer cells, making it easier for them to separate and escape.

In a recent development, the finding raises questions about whether cholesterol-lowering medications could influence the effectiveness of chemotherapy in certain situations. Researchers are now investigating that possibility, but they emphasize that the results have not been demonstrated in patients and are not a reason for anyone to discontinue prescribed statins.

"We haven't tested this effect in patients yet, but it raises questions about combining cholesterol-lowering drugs with chemotherapy, especially since ovarian cancer is most common in postmenopausal women who are often already on statins," remarked Katherine Aird, Ph.D., professor and co-leader of the Molecular and Cellular Oncogenesis Program in the Ellen and Ronald Caplan Cancer Center at The Wistar Institute, and senior author of the study.

Could Fructose Also Help Other Cancers Spread?

Although the research focused on ovarian cancer, the scientists suspect that the same biological process could occur in other forms of the disease.

Industry observers note that cancers affecting organs within the abdomen and torso can also spread to nearby tissues and organs. If fructose influences the connections between cancer cells in a similar way, the discovery could have implications beyond ovarian cancer.

"We think other cancers that spread within the torso -- pancreatic, colon, liver -- could behave similarly. We can't call it universal yet, but we think the effects are not just limited to ovarian cancer," stated Aird.

Aird and Cole have already begun designing additional experiments to determine whether their findings can be reproduced in pancreatic, colon, liver, and other cancers.

The research opens a latest avenue for understanding how cancer spreads, particularly after chemotherapy. It also suggests that the relationship between nutrients, cholesterol production, and cancer cell behavior may be more complicated than previously understood.

While the potential implications for diet and medication remain uncertain, identifying fructose as a signal that helps cancer cells break free could eventually point researchers toward fresh strategies for preventing metastasis and improving cancer treatment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now debuted, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

Recent findings suggest that the recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was announced last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy debuted, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

It has been revealed that the trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

Players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this concern before the trial officially kicks off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen will reveal the latest GTI hot hatch on Friday, promising it will be “something really spicy.”.

To celebrate the GTI’s 50th anniversary, Volkswagen is “starting a new chapter,” with its first all-electric model to bear the iconic performance badge.

Recent findings suggest that the ID. Polo GTI “brings the legendary GTI driving pleasure into the electric future,” VW mentioned after opening pre-orders last month.

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen previewed a mysterious upcoming hot hatch draped under a cloth that appears to be a souped-up version of the ID. Polo GTI. Despite its attempt to “hide” it, you can see the massive rear wing and wide wheel arches under the cloth.

The firm promised that “something really spicy” will be served this Friday, November 20, with the tags #Volkswagen, #GTI, and #GTI50.

Although no other details were revealed, the new hot hatch is thought to be the more powerful “Clubsport” variant.

A post shared by Volkswagen (@volkswagen).

Volkswagen’s head of driving dynamics, Florian Umbach, told Autocar earlier this year that the company is planning to launch the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, a more powerful variant that will deliver close to 300 hp, up from 223 hp in the standard model.

Umbach stated that Volkswagen is developing “a similar kind of paddleshift power delivery that the Hyundai N cars have” for the upcoming electric hot hatch.

Hyundai’s performance EVs, the IONIQ 5 N and IONIQ 6 N, feature a simulated gear-shifting system called N e-Shift that uses paddle shifters on the steering wheel to replicate the feel of an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission. It works with the N Active Sound+ system to make it feel like you’re in a traditional gas-powered sports car.

It has yet to be confirmed whether the hot hatch debuting on Friday is, in fact, the new ID. Polo Clubsport, but the design clues give us a good idea of what’s coming.

Check back on Friday for the full details.

Volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, starting at 39,995 euros (about $45,000).

Recent findings suggest that like the first Golf GTI from 1976, the electric ID. Polo GTI uses a front-wheel-drive powertrain. The front-mounted electric motor delivers 223 hp (166 kW) and 213 lb-ft (290 Nm) of instant torque, enabling it to sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 6.8 seconds.

In early 2027, Volkswagen will open orders for the ID.3 GTI, the second EV to wear the badge, and its first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.

#17329. Without this protein, damaged muscle fills with fat and scar tissue

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1369 w)

Without this protein, damaged muscle fills with fat and scar tissue

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1369 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when muscles are injured, the body normally activates specialized stem cells that help rebuild damaged tissue.
  • Researchers at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania have identified an unexpected role for a protein called TRF2, which was previously known primarily for protecting chromosomes.
  • In a recent development, the discovery, published in Science Advances, could provide new directions for muscular dystrophy treatments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when muscles are injured, the body normally activates specialized stem cells that help rebuild damaged tissue. But scientists have discovered that without one critical protein, this repair system can break down, leaving injured muscles filled with fat and scar tissue instead of healthy muscle.

Researchers at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania have identified an unexpected role for a protein called TRF2, which was previously known primarily for protecting chromosomes. Their findings suggest that TRF2 is also essential for maintaining the identity of muscle stem cells, allowing them to continue repairing and regenerating muscle throughout life.

In a recent development, the discovery, published in Science Advances, could provide new directions for muscular dystrophy treatments. It may also help scientists understand notable differences between muscle regeneration and cancer, including why skeletal muscle can repair itself so effectively while cancers originating in muscle are relatively uncommon.

"For years, TRF2 has been viewed as a protein whose primary job is protecting the ends of chromosomes from damage or corruption," stated senior author Foteini Mourkioti, PhD, an associate professor of Orthopedic Surgery at Penn Medicine. "But rather than simply protecting DNA, TRF2 seems to be key to regenerating muscle throughout life.".

A Hidden Protein With an Unexpected Role in Muscle Repair.

Industry observers note that for years, scientists have studied TRF2 because of its role in safeguarding telomeres, the protective structures found at the ends of chromosomes. Chromosomes carry our genetic information, and telomeres help keep their ends from deteriorating or being mistaken for damaged DNA.

The new research shows that TRF2 has another crucial responsibility. It helps muscle stem cells retain the genetic instructions that make them muscle stem cells in the first place. Maintaining that identity is essential because these specialized cells serve as the body's reserve supply for repairing injured muscle.

Recent findings suggest that under normal conditions, muscle stem cells spend much of their time inactive. When an injury occurs, they become active, multiply, and help replace damaged muscle tissue. Some then return to a resting state, preserving a population of stem cells that can respond to future injuries.

Through laboratory experiments, the researchers found that TRF2 levels change as muscle stem cells move between these different stages. The protein's activity rises and falls as the cells transition from dormancy to repair and then replenish themselves, suggesting that TRF2 helps regulate the entire regeneration process.

Without TRF2, Damaged Muscles Accumulate Fat and Scar Tissue.

To understand how notable TRF2 is, the scientists removed the protein from muscle stem cells in laboratory mice. At first, the animals' muscles appeared normal, suggesting that the loss of TRF2 did not immediately damage existing muscle tissue.

It has been revealed that over time, however, a serious problem emerged. The population of functional muscle stem cells began to decline, leaving the animals increasingly unable to repair damaged muscle.

It has been revealed that the researchers initially expected the cells to die, since losing TRF2 can produce that outcome in other tissues. Instead, they discovered something more surprising: the cells remained alive but lost the molecular identity that allowed them to function as muscle stem cells.

In effect, the cells no longer maintained the biological program needed to perform their specialized repair duties.

Sources indicate that the consequences became clear when the muscles were injured. Rather than rebuilding healthy muscle, the damaged tissue accumulated fat and scar tissue, a form of tissue replacement that cannot restore normal muscle function.

Industry observers note that "This completely changes how we think about TRF2's role in these cells," said Mourkioti. "The loss of identity has severe implications for whether recovery from injury is even possible.".

A Potential Breakthrough for Muscular Dystrophy Research.

Sources indicate that the team also investigated whether TRF2 plays a role in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, a serious inherited disorder that causes progressive muscle weakness and degeneration. The disease interferes with the body's ability to maintain healthy muscles, making effective repair especially vital.

Using a mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, the researchers removed TRF2 from muscle stem cells and observed a dramatic worsening of the disease.

Sources indicate that muscle degeneration progressed much faster, and the affected mice had shorter survival times. These findings indicate that TRF2 plays an vital role in preserving the regenerative capacity of muscles already struggling with a serious genetic disease.

In a recent development, the results do not yet establish a newly introduced treatment for muscular dystrophy. However, they identify a biological mechanism that researchers may eventually be able to target to help preserve muscle stem cell function and improve tissue repair.

How TRF2 Protects the Identity of Muscle Stem Cells.

Further experiments revealed how TRF2 performs this unexpected function.

Although the protein is best known for working at the ends of chromosomes, the researchers found that it also attaches to regulatory regions throughout the genome. These regions help control which genes are active or inactive, determining how cells behave and what specialized functions they perform.

For muscle stem cells, this regulation is particularly vital. Their ability to repair muscle depends on maintaining a specific pattern of gene activity that preserves their identity and regenerative potential.

The scientists discovered that many of the DNA regions associated with TRF2 contain unusual structures known as G-quadruplexes. These structures form when sections of DNA rich in the building block guanine fold into distinctive arrangements involving four interacting strands or segments.

Sources indicate that G-quadruplexes have attracted considerable scientific interest because they can influence how genes function. They are also being investigated as possible targets for cancer treatments.

The Penn researchers found that TRF2 interacts with these specialized DNA structures to help maintain the genetic program that keeps muscle stem cells functioning properly.

In a recent development, "We found that TRF2 works through these secondary DNA structures to preserve the identity of muscle stem cells and keep them capable of repairing damaged muscle," Mourkioti stated. "That was completely unexpected.".

What Muscle Regeneration Could Reveal About Cancer.

Beyond muscular dystrophy, the discovery may help researchers investigate a longstanding mystery about muscle biology.

In a recent development, skeletal muscle, the type of muscle that allows the body to move, has an impressive ability to regenerate after injury. Yet cancers that originate in skeletal muscle are relatively rare, even though other tissues with substantial regenerative activity can be more vulnerable to cancer.

This raises an notable question: how can muscle maintain such a powerful repair system without frequently developing cancer?

The researchers believe that TRF2's unusual role in muscle stem cells could offer clues. By examining how the protein regulates gene activity in muscle compared with other tissues, scientists may gain a better understanding of the mechanisms that support regeneration while limiting the risk of uncontrolled cell growth.

In a recent development, that distinction matters because cancer develops when cells acquire changes that allow them to grow and divide without the normal biological restraints. Finding ways to strengthen muscle repair without encouraging abnormal growth would be an important goal for future therapies.

Mourkioti and her colleagues are now investigating whether the way muscle stem cells use TRF2 could lead to latest treatment strategies for muscular dystrophy. They also hope to determine what this mechanism can reveal about cancer biology in tissues that are more susceptible to the disease.

Industry observers note that although additional research is needed to determine whether these findings can be translated into treatments for people, the discovery reveals an key part of the body's muscle repair system. It also demonstrates that a protein long associated with protecting DNA has a much broader role in keeping muscles capable of healing.

The research was supported by grants from the National Institutes of Health/ National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (R01 DK123356, R01s CA174904, GM101149, and FDN-143330).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that infinity Nikki has officially evolved into a bigger, more feature-rich game. After months of waiting, version 2.0 has arrived to bring massive overhauls - and plenty of new content - to the dress-up RPG.

According to recent reports, the update, available now on all platforms, is dubbed Terra’s Call. It adds a new region, Itzaland, to the game’s world. It also reshapes the rest of Miraland.

Itzaland is only the tip of the iceberg. Elderwood Forest and Spira are the region's two new areas, with more to be unlocked down the line. This patch also upgrades several core mechanics, including combat and exploration. There’s a suite of new traversal abilities, too, like grappling, low-gravity and even gigantification.

It has been revealed that archery is a newly introduced addition to combat, and you’ll spot new combat companions as part of the adaptive energy mechanics. Terra’s Call clearly has a focus on interactivity with the game’s world, to make it feel more alive and lived-in.

There’s a host of new interactions you can have with cute creatures like singing mushrooms, and wall-climbing snails. Version 2.0 also makes for a great starting point for new players as both main and side stories are now available for free.

It has been revealed that it wouldn’t be a dress-up game without a host of latest fashion sets, and outfits, of course - and there's plenty here, both free and paid. The launch of the new patch also kicks off several in-game events, including some that celebrate the game’s second anniversary, and Nikki’s birthday.

Infold also recently announced that Idina Menzel — the actor who originated the roles of Elphaba in Wicked and Elsa in Frozen — will be singing the brand-fresh theme song for Version 2.0. You can listen to that on the official Infinity Nikki YouTube channel, where you can also watch a behind-the-scenes interview with Ms Menzel.

AO3 is Back Online After Two Long Weeks Without Clerith Fanfics
