💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the internet has spent the past two and a half weeks deprived of many important things, including easy access to stories in which Cloud Strife and Aerith Gainsborough get the ending their readers wanted.
  • The volunteer-run fanfiction archive returned on Sunday, November 15, after going offline on October 29.
  • For anyone who hasn’t spent much time on AO3, it’s a huge collection of fan-written stories covering games, movies, books, television, and just about any other fictional universe you can name.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the internet has spent the past two and a half weeks deprived of many important things, including easy access to stories in which Cloud Strife and Aerith Gainsborough get the ending their readers wanted. Fortunately for Clerith fans, Archive of Our Own (AO3) is finally back online.

The volunteer-run fanfiction archive returned on Sunday, November 15, after going offline on October 29. Its operator, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), says a security incident prompted the extended shutdown. AO3 is usable again, although it hasn’t quite returned to normal.

For anyone who hasn’t spent much time on AO3, it’s a huge collection of fan-written stories covering games, movies, books, television, and just about any other fictional universe you can name.

According to recent reports, some stories fill gaps in the original work; others toss canon aside altogether. In Final Fantasy 7’s case, the apparently immortal debate about Cloud’s love life is practically built for it. Even Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth director Naoki Hamaguchi refuses to settle the Aerith-or-Tifa question.

OTW says it was able to reopen the archive before the far end of its four-week recovery estimate by switching off a handful of features. User and collection icons right now don’t appear, importing works from other websites is unavailable, and the only download option is HTML. No icons were deleted; they just aren’t being shown yet.

In a recent development, traffic is another problem. AO3 has warned that some owners will see slow loading times or even the maintenance page as it manages demand. Refreshing and trying again is the recommendation, although it may take a little patience to get in.

Initially, the October 29 outage looked like ordinary maintenance. The situation changed when OTW disclosed evidence of a security incident and warned that recovery could take between two and four weeks. It has brought in a security firm to review the incident, but isn’t detailing its fixes while that work is underway.

The return also comes just after AO3’s seventeenth anniversary. Not a particularly fun way to celebrate, but at least readers can now get back to their bookmarks.

According to recent reports, that pause will remain in place until November 29. The catch is that dates shown on existing drafts may still reflect their original deadlines, not the extension. Writers are being asked to review unfinished work and save or publish it before automatic deletion resumes.

Recent findings suggest that OTW also says published works, bookmarks, kudos, and other archive data remain intact. That’s the good news. The security side is less settled, though. The organization says it has no reason to think its user database was compromised, but it can’t be ruled out.

Recent findings suggest that it recommends an AO3 password change, as well as on other sites if you’ve reused your AO3 credentials there. You can follow further updates on the official AO3 status page.

Sources indicate that look, you don’t need to have read a single fanfic to understand the appeal. Games ask you to spend dozens, sometimes hundreds, of hours with fictional people. Once the credits roll, it’s hardly surprising that some players want to spend more time with them, or imagine things going differently.

Industry observers note that the Final Fantasy 7 fandom is an obvious example. We have covered how central Tifa and Aerith are to Rebirth’s story, while a separate guide to Aerith’s relationship options shows how much attention players can pay to Cloud’s relationships. The official story gives players scenes and choices to dissect. Fanfiction lets them carry the argument somewhere else, without waiting for Square Enix to settle anything.

Fanfiction lets them carry the argument somewhere else, without waiting for Square Enix to settle anything.

In a recent development, beyond the romance, fans have been reimagining Final Fantasy 7’s cast in entirely different art styles for years. Writing an alternate ending or inventing a crossover isn’t so different in spirit. AO3 simply gives that kind of work a home, a tag system, and readers who actually go looking for it.

Industry observers note that after 17 days of an error page, that home is accessible again. If you left a story half-read on October 28, there’s finally a chance to find your place. Just don’t be surprised if everyone else had the same idea.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has launched an investigation into Honda’s automatic engine start-stop system. The inquiry comes after NHTSA received hundreds of complaints, with owners stating that their engines were failing to automatically restart after coming to a full stop at a traffic light.

Industry observers note that the investigation was declared on Friday, November 13, and covers 1,033,632 total vehicles. The affected models are the Honda Passport, Odyssey, Pilot, and Ridgeline, along with the Acura MDX, all from between the 2024 and 2026 model years.

See all results for new 2026 Honda Passport for sale near ?

In total, NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation has been sent 701 complaints about the automatic start-stop feature. The system is supposed to automatically turn off the engine when the vehicle comes to a complete stop, and it’s supposed to automatically restart the engine when the driver takes their foot off the brake pedal. However, “the complaints allege that the engines are failing to restart once they have been shut off by this system.” NHTSA says that there have been no injuries related to the stop-start system problems.

This isn’t the first time that this issue has arisen with Honda’s automatic start-stop system, which is meant to improve fuel economy by limiting idle time. In 2025, the federal government investigated the system, looking at 2.2 million units of the Pilot, Odyssey, Passport, Ridgeline, MDX, and Acura TLX. The previous investigation covered all of the vehicles in the current investigation, except for the 2026 model year.

Although the system failure is similar in both populations, “the vehicles in this current investigation appear to have different root causes and respond differently to repairs,” NHTSA states. More information should continue to emerge as NHTSA continues its investigation.

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1061 w)

Breaking: Common forever chemicals linked to nearly double the rate of aggressive breast cancer

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1061 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women with higher blood levels of two common "forever chemicals" may face an increased risk of developing a particularly aggressive form of breast cancer, according to upcoming research from the National Institutes of Health (NIH), part of the U.S.
  • The study identified a connection between estrogen receptor-negative, or ER-negative, breast cancer and two widely encountered chemicals: perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS).
  • Recent findings suggest that both substances belong to a large family of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly called PFAS.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women with higher blood levels of two common "forever chemicals" may face an increased risk of developing a particularly aggressive form of breast cancer, according to upcoming research from the National Institutes of Health (NIH), part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).

The study identified a connection between estrogen receptor-negative, or ER-negative, breast cancer and two widely encountered chemicals: perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS). Women with greater concentrations of these substances in their blood were more likely to develop this type of cancer. However, researchers found no clear link between either chemical and breast cancer risk overall.

Recent findings suggest that both substances belong to a large family of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly called PFAS. These chemicals have been used in numerous everyday consumer products and are often described as "forever chemicals" because they resist breaking down in the environment. They can also accumulate in the human body and remain there for years.

"Women deserve clear answers about how chemicals in their environment may affect their health," noted HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. "This NIH study links two forever chemicals to a higher risk of ER-negative breast cancer and demands further investigation. Under President Trump's leadership, we will pursue the evidence, confront environmental health risks, and give women the information they need to protect their health.".

Why This Aggressive Breast Cancer Is Concerning.

Industry observers note that ER-negative breast cancer differs from more common forms of the disease because its tumor cells lack the receptors that allow estrogen to stimulate cancer growth. These cancers are often more aggressive and generally have poorer outcomes than tumors that respond to estrogen.

Sources indicate that despite their severity, researchers still have relatively little information about what makes someone more likely to develop ER-negative breast cancer. The new findings suggest that exposure to certain persistent environmental chemicals could be one contributing factor.

"Our findings, which we confirmed using a meta-analysis of prior research, indicate that certain legacy PFAS, including PFOA and PFOS, are associated with a higher risk of ER-negative breast cancer, a more aggressive tumor type with few known risk factors," explained NIH Stadtman Investigator Alexandra White, Ph.D., who led the study.

The findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology.

Higher Forever Chemical Levels Linked to Greater Cancer Risk.

Sources indicate that to investigate the possible connection, NIH scientists and their collaborators examined blood samples that had been collected years before participants received a cancer diagnosis. The researchers measured concentrations of 17 different PFAS chemicals, allowing them to compare earlier exposure levels with subsequent breast cancer outcomes.

Recent findings suggest that the results revealed substantial differences for two chemicals. Women in the highest PFOA exposure group had a 67% higher rate of ER-negative breast cancer than women in the lowest group. The association was even stronger for PFOS, with the highest exposure group showing a 93% higher rate, nearly twice that of the lowest group.

In a recent development, these percentages represent relative differences between groups rather than the absolute probability that an individual woman will develop breast cancer. The findings also establish an association, not proof that the chemicals directly cause the disease.

Recent findings suggest that the analysis used data from the Sister Study, a major research project conducted by NIH's National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS). Between 2003 and 2009, the study enrolled 50,884 women ages 35-74 from across the United States and Puerto Rico.

It has been revealed that all participants were free of breast cancer when they enrolled, although each had a full or half-sister who had already been diagnosed with the disease. For the PFAS investigation, researchers analyzed information from 1,609 women who subsequently developed breast cancer and a comparison group of 2,269 women.

Could Reducing PFAS Exposure Lower Cancer Risk?

Although PFAS can remain in the environment and the body for long periods, researchers emphasize that exposure is not necessarily unavoidable. The findings could eventually help identify fresh ways to reduce the risk of aggressive breast cancer.

Sources indicate that "These findings matter for women's health broadly," stated first author, Che-Jung Chang, Ph.D., who previously worked as an NIH research fellow and is now a researcher at DLH, a scientific research organization. "Although PFAS are persistent in the environment and in our bodies, exposure to them is still potentially modifiable, meaning people can take steps to reduce their exposure, and these findings could open upcoming avenues for prevention.".

It has been revealed that the researchers are also interested in understanding how these chemicals might influence cancer development. Because the strongest associations appeared in tumors that lack estrogen receptors, the findings suggest that PFAS could act through biological processes unrelated to hormonal signaling.

Potential explanations include changes in gene activity or alterations in the immune system. However, the study did not directly investigate these mechanisms, so their involvement remains uncertain.

Newer Forever Chemicals Raise Unanswered Questions.

Sources indicate that although PFOA and PFOS have largely been phased out and replaced with other PFAS compounds, measurable amounts of both substances are still present in most people's bodies. Their persistence means that exposure to these older chemicals remains a potential public health concern.

It has been revealed that the researchers say additional investigations should focus on populations with greater PFAS exposure, as well as groups that experience higher rates of ER-negative breast cancer. Such research could help clarify the strength of the observed associations and identify whether certain populations face greater risks.

Scientists also need to determine whether the newer chemicals introduced as replacements for PFOA and PFOS carry similar health concerns.

"More research is needed, particularly evaluating the risk of breast cancer associated with newer replacement PFAS chemicals," White said.

The findings add to growing questions about the long-term health effects of forever chemicals and highlight the importance of understanding how environmental exposures may contribute to aggressive forms of breast cancer.

The research received support from NIEHS grants Z01ES044005; Z1AES103332; and R01ES032831.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh Arc Raiders patch has arrived, bringing a host of newly introduced fixes to several exploits players have recently been relying on to do things they’re not supposed to, and bypass certain mechanics to get into areas without having to go through proper channels.

The patch is fairly small, and surprisingly doesn’t include any buffs or nerfs to anything in particular.

Sources indicate that the list of notes for update 1.4.0 is compact, with a clear focus on addressing several exploits. The biggest one, of course, is the addition of “exploit mitigation mechanisms” to stop players from glitching through locked doors.

In a recent development, this fix applies to all maps, and it’s intended to address an issue whereby players would not bring the required keys to access those areas of the various maps. Locked rooms, if they can be unlocked, often hide a wealth of high-tier and rare loot.

But players have also been using similar exploits to clip through walls and access areas outside the playspace, allowing them to ambush enemy players and set up traps that would be impossible for others to detect.

Industry observers note that the game’s recent patch, which was released exactly one week ago, mainly consisted of balance tweaks to some of the more popular weapons and mines. However, it also introduced a few fixes to prevent players from clipping through walls by using barricades.

While on the subject of being in places where you’re not supposed to, the patch blocked exterior access to the locked room inside Spaceport's Control Tower, making it only accessible from inside the tower.

1.4.0 also fixes an especially nasty exploit that allowed players to bring up their weapons much faster than normal by rapidly swapping to the quick use menu. There’s a range of smaller fixes for lighting and texture bugs here, too, and you can read all about it in the full change log below:.

#17320. M3 Goes EV! We Drive a Prototype as the M Car Undergoes a Monumental Change

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1492 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Caranddriver ↗ Open Full Page

M3 Goes EV! We Drive a Prototype as the M Car Undergoes a Monumental Change

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1492 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, most BMW fans cannot help falling all over themselves when a new M3 is debuted, but this time they might get well and truly tripped up.
  • After driving a camouflaged prototype and hearing all the dirty details at BMW’s Miramas test center in southern France, we most certainly do.
  • This machine has four electrically excited synchronous motors, one for each wheel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, most BMW fans cannot help falling all over themselves when a new M3 is debuted, but this time they might get well and truly tripped up. That’s because what BMW is calling “the fastest and most powerful BMW M3 of all time” is 100 percent electric. There’s no mention of a gasoline version and no special EV designation tagged onto the name, just “here’s the new 2027 BMW M3, and we hope you like it,” or words to that effect.

After driving a camouflaged prototype and hearing all the dirty details at BMW’s Miramas test center in southern France, we most certainly do.

This machine has four electrically excited synchronous motors, one for each wheel. The pair at each axle is not quite what you expect, with one motor situated ahead of the other and a reduction gear for one of them on each side of the shared housing. The front-axle motors make approximately 644 horsepower and 398 pound-feet of torque, while the pair on the rear axle is good for about 751 horsepower and 738 pound-feet. Combined output is likewise still subject to an asterisk at this pre-production stage, but total power is at least 838 horsepower, and torque is an axle-twisting 885 pound-feet. If you’re thinking the sum total is less than the two axles, you are absolutely correct. The surplus is there to allow for serious torque vectoring, both front to rear and side to side. In normal driving, the car operates strictly in rear-wheel drive, with the front axle brought in whenever there’s acceleration, if the situation demands front-axle recuperation, or if you have the drivetrain set to Sport mode.

See all results for new 2028 BMW M3 EV for sale near 29651.

Industry observers note that four motors require precise and rapid control during acceleration and braking, but they also play an outsize role in cornering. It all operates much more smoothly and immediately than any electronically controlled differential or transfer case ever could, so you absolutely get what you request. The so-called Heart of Joy (essentially another name for the M Dynamic Performance Control module) is the single ECU that oversees everything in the powertrain and driving dynamics arena. It’s the brain that seamlessly decides what motor is required for whatever demands you place on the car by looking at steering position, accelerator input, and braking demands, with a nod toward the basic settings that you have dialed in.

The battery that powers all of this is specific to the M3, even though it fits in a similarly sized case as the one in the i3. It’s designed to give higher peak and sustained power output and is capable of higher energy recuperation (up to 540 kilowatts) and faster charging (420 kilowatts), which means it has a higher level of cooling. The battery capacity is slightly lower for all this, currently sitting at about 100 kWh. Estimated EPA range is currently 300 miles or so, but all of these numbers are subject to change. As for the difference between how this battery pack is installed versus the i3’s, the M3 gains a direct connection to the front and rear axle subframes for enhanced torsional rigidity for more precise handling.

See all results for fresh 2028 BMW M3 EV for sale near 29651.

Whatever the underlying mumbo jumbo, we can say that it really works, and the result is simply epic. We first went out in the default mode, with the drivetrain, chassis, steering, and brakes set to Comfort and energy recovery set to Mid, just to get a feel of the track. Once we knew where we were going, we let fly with the M1 button, and that brought everything to Sport mode but left the energy recovery in Mid and, crucially, left the DSC stability control setting in On. We pressed the car hard, and the M3 absolutely responded, and our pace built immensely. But that eventually resulted in a bit too much understeer as speeds climbed, which led to a brief off-track excursion, as they say in the business. We kept on going, but the car was imposing a limit on our fun.

Recent findings suggest that we did what you would do at that point and duly selected the M2 button. That setting was programmed by our hosts to bring the drivetrain and chassis up to Sport+ and raised the recuperation to Max. It also put the DSC in a more permissive state, otherwise known as MDM, and all of that was the magic bullet. The car now dived toward apexes and slithered nicely out of corners. The front end was quite pointy, and the rear now had permission to loosen up. Our lap times fell, and our grin widened. This car felt alive. It really did feel like an M3, just like no other before it. Through it all, the braking response felt entirely natural, probably because on the track there was a strong base level of recuperation, overlaid with a thin veneer of friction braking for a precise feel of what is happening underfoot.

Interestingly, there is a sound accompanying all of this, although BMW indicates it’s not modeled on any particular car. We drove it with the eDrive set to Auto, which delivers the augmented sound of six gears known as “stages.” You don’t have to shift in this mode, and there’s no real interruption of power, but the interior sound level rises and falls as the car progresses up and down through each stage. There’s extra emphasis on powertrain load and aggression, too, so when you’re driving the M3 hard, it really does give you the auditory cues that you miss when you drive an otherwise-quiet EV. If you want a manual-like experience, you can set the eDrive accordingly, and then you’ll get shift lights, and it’ll even cut power if you don’t upshift at the right time. In the time we had, this setting was not particularly fun. We’ll table this issue for now, probably until we can get our own M3 to soak in. You can also turn the eDrive to Off, in which setting the car will just quietly amble along like any other EV, but what’s the fun in that?

Industry observers note that the prototype’s camouflage didn’t do much to cover up the exterior of the new M3, as it was formfitting. That noted, you couldn’t really get a sense of the exterior look of the car, although it was still clear that every panel below the greenhouse was different from the i3. The body is distinctly pulled out to cover the wide Michelin Pilot Sport S 6 tires. Also clear to see were the M Yellow DRLs and the track lights below them, as well as many of the carbon-fiber bits, such as the hood vents, the rockers, and the mirror housings.

According to recent reports, it was even more difficult to see what was going on inside, as much of the interior was obscured. But you could still see some things, such as the steering wheel and its extra buttons. The top of the “wings” (because the spokes are lower down in typical Neue Klasse parlance) has two extra red buttons per side. There are the M1 and M2 buttons, but there’s also the M Setup button you use in conjunction with the touchscreen to program each one. The fourth button is interesting; press it twice to deactivate the ADAS active-safety minders. For track work, it’s nice to have one button that will do all that. The 17.9-inch central screen was obvious, but BMW had it covered much of the time, except to show the newly introduced screens that had to do with setting up the M buttons. The Panoramic Vision screen at the base of the windshield was mostly visible and mostly the same apart from fonts and the like, but for some reason the central section was blocked off.

Industry observers note that as for what it’s called, the car’s official name is just 2027 BMW M3. Like we said, there’s no EV or Electric nomenclature tagged onto the end. As for the unofficial model code that you may be wondering about, that is ZA0. More will be divulged as we get closer to its summer 2027 launch date, including the price. We have a $90,000 placeholder, but that is subject to change. As for an ICE version, there is no official word from BMW. Stay tuned.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alongside its completely revamped visuals and modernized gameplay designed around the Joy-Cons, one of the things I was most excited about when I finally got my hands on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was facing its bosses all over again.

I've played the original countless times, and there are so many incredible boss fights throughout this adventure that the mere thought of experiencing them again with all these changes was almost too exciting to handle. Thankfully, despite my ridiculously high expectations, it managed to exceed them. Congratulations, Nintendo, all my childhood nightmares have officially been upgraded!

Jokes aside, the remake does an incredible job of staying faithful to the original bosses while giving them enough visual and gameplay improvements to make these encounters feel fresh. And honestly, the excitement I felt when entering these arenas was just as strong as it was the first time around. And picking a favorite Ocarina of Time boss is still as difficult as picking just one Zelda game to call your favorite: there are simply too many amazing ones to choose from!

So, I decided to put together a ranking of the ten best boss fights in the new Ocarina of Time, including a few mini-bosses to make things even more interesting. Let's see which encounters managed to steal the spotlight. Naturally, there are lots of spoilers here if you haven't completed the remake or the original, so beware!

Fighting Gohma is actually pretty easy, I must say, but there's no denying that she makes a fantastic first impression as Ocarina of Time's opening boss. This is basically the first real test of your skills, giving you a taste of what's waiting for you throughout the rest of the adventure – and there's something incredibly satisfying about finally defeating your first major enemy.

Besides, her introduction is absolutely fantastic! You enter what appears to be an empty room, already anticipating the boss encounter because you know something is waiting for you. But there's nothing there. So, naturally, you look up... and surprise! Gohma is crawling across the ceiling, ready to ruin your day.

Sources indicate that her imposing size makes the encounter even more memorable, especially when you realize she's trying to give birth to a bunch of smaller spiders just to make your life miserable. Lovely! The remake takes all these elements and makes them even more impressive with its updated visuals, giving Gohma a much more intimidating presence. Not bad for our first massive fight.

Industry observers note that what's not to love about fighting a giant blob of goo? I'll admit that I never found Morpha particularly exciting in the original game, but the remake completely changed my mind.

One of my favorite things about this encounter is how rapidly it goes from zero to one hundred. After surviving the Water Temple, you're probably expecting some terrifying aquatic monster, perhaps a giant shark or a creature covered in tentacles. Instead, you walk into the boss arena and find... a blob.

However, things get considerably more interesting once the battle begins. Morpha uses its gelatinous body to create enormous tentacles that can grab Link and take a surprisingly painful chunk out of his health. And believe me, they're considerably faster this time around, so you'll want to keep moving.

According to recent reports, falling into the water is also something you should avoid at all costs, since the rest of Morpha's body is lurking beneath the surface. It's a surprisingly stressful encounter, but also fun, especially because you have to use the Hookshot to pull Morpha's inner nucleus out of its tentacles and attack it. It's the only boss that requires you to use what is the coolest equipment in the game!

Industry observers note that my first encounter with the Iron Knuckle in the remake was just as terrifying as I remembered it being in the original. This heavily armored enemy hits like a truck, and every successful attack can take a ridiculous amount of Link's health away. Even worse, its powerful strikes can send you flying across the arena, making it incredibly difficult to regain control of the situation.

Sources indicate that A big part of what makes this encounter so intimidating is that you're facing the Iron Knuckle as Child Link. You're considerably weaker than Adult Link, and you don't have access to the powerful equipment and abilities you've grown accustomed to using throughout your adventure. So suddenly, you're reminded that you're still a pretty vulnerable little kid, and this walking tank is more than happy to prove it!

Industry observers note that the remake's improved visuals make the encounter even more impressive, giving the Iron Knuckle an intimidating presence that makes every swing of its enormous axe feel dangerous. It's a little like eating your grandmother's homemade food after worrying that something might have gone wrong with the recipe. Somehow, it turns out even better than you remembered.

Industry observers note that king Dodongo is an enormous creature that spends most of the fight rolling around its circular arena, trying to crush Link before eventually opening its mouth to unleash a fiery attack. What I love most about this boss is how clever its main weakness is. Since the creature seems so eager to swallow Link, let’s give it something else to eat, of course!

So all you need to do is avoid its rolling attacks and throw a Bomb into its mouth whenever it opens it, and watching this enormous beast swallow an explosive and immediately regret its life choices never gets old.

It's also a fantastic early boss because it makes you realize just how much bigger and more dangerous Hyrule is compared to the relatively cozy Kokiri Forest. Nothing states “your adventure is officially getting more challenging” quite like fighting a creature thirty times your size over a pool of lava.

Dead Hand has always been one of the most nightmare-inducing enemies in the entire Zelda franchise, and apparently, Nintendo knows exactly how much we fear this thing. Because if there's one boss that the remake refuses to make less terrifying, it's this horrifying creature!

Just like with the Iron Knuckle, your first encounter with Dead Hand happens while playing as Child Link. Veteran players already know what's coming as soon as they enter the room and spot those creepy hands emerging from the ground. And you can feel the tension building before it actually appears. Once it finally reveals itself, things get considerably worse.

Sources indicate that its updated design makes its face even more disturbing, and watching it attempt to bite Link with its enormous mouth is enough to make you question whether you accidentally launched a survival horror game instead of Ocarina of Time. I honestly don't know how Nintendo managed to make this thing even creepier, but I certainly won't be looking under my bed tonight.

Industry observers note that fighting an invisible enemy is already challenging enough. Fighting an invisible enemy while standing on top of a giant bongo drum that it's constantly playing? Now that's a completely different story.

Sources indicate that bongo Bongo is easily one of the most creative boss encounters in Ocarina of Time, and its updated appearance takes the entire experience to another level. The idea of fighting this enormous, headless creature while trying to keep your balance on a drum is already wonderfully bizarre, but the atmosphere surrounding the encounter makes it even better.

According to recent reports, the remake also makes some of its attacks noticeably faster, meaning you'll have even less time to react while trying to keep up with the rhythm of the fight. And since Bongo Bongo is literally drumming throughout the entire encounter, you can bet that things get pretty intense! It's such an unusual boss concept, and I love how the remake manages to preserve its original identity while making the entire battle feel even more chaotic.

Recent findings suggest that facing Dark Link is one of the most memorable moments in the original Ocarina of Time, and the remake manages to make this encounter just as special. As you progress through the Water Temple, you'll find yourself fighting Dark Link (accompanied by a rather creepy-looking Dark Navi, by the way), which ends up being an unforgettable battle.

The symbolism behind this encounter is already fantastic, since what better way to challenge the Hero of Time than by forcing him to face a darker version of himself? But the remake takes things even further by giving Dark Link a new move that might just be the coolest animation I've seen in the entire game.

In a recent development, whenever you try to attack him with the tip of the Master Sword, he can actually dodge your strike by jumping onto the blade and standing on it – yes, he literally uses your own sword as a platform to avoid being hit, and it's ridiculously stylish! I also swear the controller gives you a little vibration when he pulls off this move, which makes the moment even more satisfying. Or maybe I'm imagining things because I'm still trying to process how cool it looks. Either way, Dark Link remains one of the best highlights of this remake.

According to recent reports, I'll admit that Phantom Ganon has always been my favorite boss in the original Ocarina of Time, and a reason for that is the incredible atmosphere surrounding the Forest Temple. By the time you reach this dungeon, you've already seen what Ganondorf has done to Hyrule during his seven-year reign of terror, and there's a constant sense of dread surrounding his presence.

Sources indicate that so, when you finally reach the boss room and see what appears to be Ganondorf himself, it's a pretty intimidating moment! Even if is a phantom version of him. What I love about it is that it uses a painting mechanic, where Phantom Ganon hides inside the painting and you must pay attention to spot him before he strikes you! Visually, it is a truly striking moment, and when he gets off the painting to face you off is amazing.

Industry observers note that also, the remake makes this encounter even more memorable by extending Ganondorf's dialogue after the battle. Once the boss is defeated, the real villain appears and calls him a useless puppet, warning that he knows Link’s intentions and won’t let him accomplish them so easily.

Twinrova just hits differently in the remake. The combination of their updated designs, new animations, and fully voiced cutscenes makes this battle feel considerably more special than it already was in the original. Gameplay-wise, the fight remains faithful to its original mechanics. You'll need to use the Mirror Shield to absorb the correct elemental attacks from Koume and Kotake before redirecting that energy toward the opposite witch. It's a clever mechanic that forces you to pay attention to both enemies while carefully timing your movements.

Industry observers note that however, what really makes this encounter shine is how expressive the two witches have become! Their personalities come through much more clearly now, especially when you're managing to land a successful attack. Watching them react to your moves, get increasingly frustrated, and argue with each other is genuinely hilarious.

Industry observers note that things get considerably more serious once they fuse into Twinrova, turning the encounter into an even more intense battle involving both fire and ice. But the fun doesn't stop when the fight ends. The final interactions between the two witches are fantastic, and their newly voiced dialogue gives the entire sequence so much personality. Honestly, I could watch these two argue for hours.

There was no way I could finish this list without giving the final boss encounter the top spot. Facing Ganondorf and, eventually, Ganon is the culmination of everything you've experienced throughout Ocarina of Time, and the remake manages to make this already iconic confrontation even more impressive.

In a recent development, his updated animations, additional moves, and much more expressive character model make every moment feel considerably more dramatic. You can really feel that you're facing the main villain who has been threatening Hyrule throughout your entire adventure, rather than just another boss waiting at the end of a dungeon.

And then, just when you think the battle is over, Ganondorf transforms into Ganon, giving you one final confrontation against an enormous beast that looks terrifying in the remake's updated visuals. It's the perfect way to bring the adventure to its conclusion and also to deliver the best-looking sequences of the entire game. Now, if you'll excuse me, I think I need to replay the entire game again.

Stopping statins after 70 may be safer than expected, but there's a catch

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1145 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A major new study suggests that many adults age 70 and older who have never experienced a heart attack or stroke may be able to stop taking statins without substantially increasing their short-term cardiovascular risks.
  • Recent findings suggest that the independent, preliminary research was presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, held November 6 through 9 in Chicago.
  • Sources indicate that an estimated 25% of American adults have elevated levels of low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C), commonly called "bad cholesterol." When too much LDL cholesterol accumulates in the arteries, it can restrict blood flow and contribute to heart attacks and strokes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A major new study suggests that many adults age 70 and older who have never experienced a heart attack or stroke may be able to stop taking statins without substantially increasing their short-term cardiovascular risks. However, the findings also point to a possible increase in risk over a longer period, making the decision more complicated than it initially appears.

Recent findings suggest that the independent, preliminary research was presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, held November 6 through 9 in Chicago. The annual conference brings together cardiovascular researchers and healthcare professionals from around the world to share scientific discoveries, emerging evidence, and advances in clinical care.

Sources indicate that an estimated 25% of American adults have elevated levels of low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C), commonly called "bad cholesterol." When too much LDL cholesterol accumulates in the arteries, it can restrict blood flow and contribute to heart attacks and strokes. Statins are widely prescribed to lower cholesterol and reduce these risks, including in people who have never experienced a cardiovascular event. This preventive approach remains a central part of the American Heart Association's 2026 joint guideline on dyslipidemia.

Do Older Adults Need to Keep Taking Statins?

Although statins are an established treatment for reducing cardiovascular risk, questions remain about how much benefit they provide when people reach their 70s and beyond, particularly if they have never had a heart attack or stroke.

"While the Association's recent joint guideline recommends lifestyle and potentially medication for people with high LDL-C at younger ages to reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke, recent studies question the health benefits of continuing statins in the later decades of life," said study author Rita F. Redberg, M.D., M.Sc., FAHA, professor of cardiology and the Araxe Vilensky Endowed Chair in Cardiology at the University of California, San Francisco School of Medicine. "A few previous studies assessed the safety of discontinuing statins for primary prevention at age 70 and later, and they found no difference in mortality. One study suggested quality of life improvements after stopping statins. Whether it is safe to discontinue statins to prevent a first CVD event in the elderly remained unclear and the question we explored in our study.".

To investigate, researchers enrolled nearly 1,900 adults aged 70 and older who were taking statins specifically to prevent a first cardiovascular event. Every participant also had at least two chronic medical conditions, such as a history of cancer or lung disease.

Recent findings suggest that participants were divided into two groups. One group stopped taking statins, while the other continued their prescribed treatment. Researchers tracked their health for approximately two years, with additional follow-up extending as long as four years. They examined rates of heart attack, stroke, and death, along with changes in quality of life, muscle pain, falls, and muscle wasting (known as sarcopenia).

What Happened When Older Adults Stopped Statins?

The initial findings were largely reassuring. After approximately two years, participants who stopped taking statins did not experience a statistically significant increase in heart attacks, strokes, or deaths compared with those who remained on the medications.

In a recent development, stopping treatment also did not produce measurable improvements in the other outcomes researchers examined. Quality of life, muscle discomfort, falls, and muscle wasting were similar in both groups.

Industry observers note that there was, however, a small difference in cardiovascular outcomes. Over the first two years, the results indicated approximately one additional cardiovascular event for every 40 people who discontinued statins compared with those who continued treatment.

Sources indicate that the longer follow-up revealed a more concerning pattern. Over a period of up to four years, 12.7% of participants who stopped statins experienced a heart attack, stroke, or death, compared with 9.2% of those who kept taking the medications.

Longer Follow-Up Reveals a Potential Risk.

Recent findings suggest that redberg explained that the higher rate of serious outcomes during the four-year follow-up represents a new finding in research on statin discontinuation among older adults. She suggested that the difference may have emerged because this trial included more participants and tracked them for a longer period than earlier studies.

Recent findings suggest that these results complicate the question of whether older adults should continue cholesterol treatment indefinitely. While the findings suggest that stopping statins may be a reasonable option for many people in this age group, they also indicate that remaining on treatment could offer some protection over time.

Industry observers note that "This small, increased risk of cardiovascular events means that one cannot make a general recommendation about stopping statins in this patient population," she noted. "There should be shared decision-making between the patient and the healthcare professional to know if it is appropriate for an individual to discontinue the medication. In general, however, discontinuation is safe for most people who are in this age group and without a previous CVD event.".

Study Design and Important Limitations.

Recent findings suggest that the trial involved 1,880 participants aged 70 and older (average age of 77; 53% men, and 47% women), all of whom had at least two chronic health conditions. Individuals with established cardiovascular disease or a previous cardiovascular event were not eligible to participate.

Researchers conducted the study between November 2021 and April 2026 across 24 medical centers in Switzerland, France, and the Netherlands. Of the participants, 938 were assigned to discontinue statins, while 942 were assigned to continue taking their medications.

Throughout the trial and subsequent follow-up, researchers recorded heart attacks, acute ischemic strokes, and deaths from any cause. Participants also completed surveys assessing their overall quality of life, muscle pain, falls, and sarcopenia.

According to recent reports, one limitation was that some participants did not remain in their originally assigned groups. Some people instructed to stop statins eventually resumed treatment, while others assigned to continue taking statins stopped using them. Altogether, approximately 14% of participants switched from their assigned treatment approach during the study.

According to recent reports, to determine whether these changes affected the findings, the researchers performed several additional statistical analyses. The results remained unchanged.

Taken together, the findings suggest that discontinuing statins may be an option for many adults over 70 who have not previously experienced cardiovascular disease, especially when considering outcomes over the first two years. However, the higher rate of heart attacks, strokes, and deaths during longer follow-up underscores why stopping treatment should be an individualized decision made with a healthcare professional rather than a general recommendation for all older adults.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season patch not intended to change the game significantly.
  • However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.
  • The December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the latest year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season patch not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

The December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the latest year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

Battlefield Studios revealed a host of new changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

The focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an glitch that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

The patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios notes should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

Going forward, Battlefield Studios said to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

In a recent development, some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect new maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • HoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major upgrade.
  • Alongside showing everything coming with this next patch, the developer also declared that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six.
  • The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major upgrade. Version 3.8 was the big highlight, of course, with the latest release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

Alongside showing everything coming with this next patch, the developer also declared that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

Industry observers note that this final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

The fresh playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

Industry observers note that the Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

In a recent development, while The Dahlia is the only latest character appearing in this final Amphoreus update, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the newly introduced patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

Afterwords – Marvel’s Wolverine

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1831 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We interviewed game director Mike Daly after the launch of Insomniac’s recent Wolverine game to get his take on what makes Wolverine and Spidey different to work on, his thoughts on breadcrumb trails, and why Logan can’t ever seem to get the girl.
  • It has been revealed that insomniac had extensive experience working on well-known superhero characters before starting on Wolverine.
  • Sources indicate that from a story perspective, we wanted Logan to be a man with centuries of experiences that he can’t remember, creating a mix of being worn, wizened, and cynical.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We interviewed game director Mike Daly after the launch of Insomniac’s recent Wolverine game to get his take on what makes Wolverine and Spidey different to work on, his thoughts on breadcrumb trails, and why Logan can’t ever seem to get the girl.

It has been revealed that insomniac had extensive experience working on well-known superhero characters before starting on Wolverine. Early on, what traits or qualities of Logan as a story character and playable avatar did you know you wanted to focus on, distinct from the Spider-Man games and character?

Sources indicate that from a story perspective, we wanted Logan to be a man with centuries of experiences that he can’t remember, creating a mix of being worn, wizened, and cynical. His resilience makes him fearless, which comes through in his candid manner, and he can’t ignore his sense of justice, as much as he would like to.

For gameplay, it was crucial that players felt the difference made by his healing factor, claws, berserker rage, animalistic strength, enhanced senses, his adamantium skeleton, and corresponding weight.

Recent findings suggest that in both story and gameplay, emotionally and physically, Wolverine is a hero who gets hurt and feels that pain deeply but always gets back up again and presses on. This dogged resilience was really crucial to us and a central theme of story and gameplay.

In a recent development, wolverine is more of a linear adventure than the open-world exploration of a big city seen in Spidey. In my playthrough, that added to the sense of relentless pacing that characterizes Wolverine as a fictional lead. Was that part of the thinking behind why the game was built that way, or was the more linear path there for other reasons?

Ultimately, we made a game suited for a Wolverine story that had comic book pacing – action and meaningful story development on every page.

We experimented with different structures and stories, evaluating from the perspective of: “Is this the best way to do Wolverine justice?” As the various things we tried didn’t feel right, we had to challenge our assumptions and look to our favorite Wolverine stories for inspiration, which led us to where we ended up – a story with momentum in which every beat felt authentic to the character.

Scenes and gameplay sequences that might have been fine in other games but didn’t strongly evoke Wolverine undermined the consistency of the fantasy we were trying to create, so we tried to keep things very focused.

It has been revealed that after the game’s release, there was an active online conversation about some of the breadcrumb-trail guidance the game offers to lead you to pickups, or to mark the continued golden path of progression. What was the thinking internally about that design decision, and your take on the debate after the game introduced?

Our thinking was that it was essential to make the player feel like they were empowered by Logan’s enhanced senses, a canonical mutant ability, enabling players to do things they could not with other characters. We wanted to weave that power into as many parts of the game as we could, so that if Logan could smell or hear something relevant, the player could see it too.

For collectibles, we wanted players to enjoy seeking out and spotting senses cues, enabling you to find things that would have been obscure to other characters. Using the cues, players can cover a lot of ground without feeling the need to scour, maintaining story and action momentum.

Industry observers note that after the game debuted, we saw feedback from players that interpreted senses as abstract designer guidance, along with a desire for options in how they approached exploration and discovery. Fortunately, we have been able to incorporate this feedback from players in our post-launch patches. One aspect we’ve improved is the scent trail’s organic presentation, so they give a stronger impression that they belong in the world rather than being an abstraction. For players that want to do more manual exploration, we’ve added options to remove the sense cues for optional collectibles, and one to make scent trails dimmer until the player requests a hint.

Ultimately, enhanced senses are still essential to creating an authentic Wolverine, and that’s still reflected in the cinematic and environmental storytelling of the game. I think it’s great that on top of that, players now have more flexibility in how they experience them.

In a recent development, as a longtime comics fan, I found Logan’s combat system especially exciting, particularly for the relentless forward momentum it provided. What do you think were some of the keys to nailing that dynamic, as distinct from other high-quality third-person action games?

There were a few key elements we wanted to get right - Logan’s resilience, rage, claw feel, and overall lethality.

Recent findings suggest that for resilience, Logan’s healing factor needed to feel vital for survival - a prominent element of the system. A natural starting point there was to try continual regeneration so you could outlast enemies, but that rapidly fell apart as it incentivized the player to slow the pace of combat or even retreat for maximum advantage. Even though it was incredibly effective at enabling survival, it was also hard to notice by the player so it didn’t feel prominent.

According to recent reports, the key to solving this problem was making a connection between rage and healing factor. The Last Stand mechanic is a healing surge that can happen when you lose all your health, themed as using adrenaline to keep Logan’s heart beating. This incentivized aggression and made a space for an up-close look at visceral healing.

According to recent reports, speaking of rage, it’s the backbone of the combat system where being an indicator of momentum is key. At the low end of rage, you don’t have the safety net of Last Stand, so your decision-making naturally biases towards survival; ensuring you prioritize threat assessment and defense. As you climb into the middle tier, you have the leeway to push your luck for longer combos or barrages that let you build up rage and get kills faster. Finally, you get to rage tier 3, where the quick decay of rage makes your rate of kills the top priority, so you might prefer to attack groups over ranged stragglers just for the improved kill density. Beyond the mechanics, we change the presentation of combat, especially through Logan’s animations and exertion to reflect his state of mind. The presentation and systemic incentives drive the player into a frenzy, just like Wolverine.

We invested a lot in the details of claw feel to make sure it was distinct from general game attacks. Claws shred, so we added locational body damage to our enemies to reflect that, along with a dynamic blood system where it globs together as it is spilled, splatters on contact with characters or the environment, drips down the walls, diffuses in the water, and other details. Many kills throughout combat are punctuated with custom animations with cinematic camera work that pushes in and frames the puncturing of claws into the body for a strong impression of the connection and weight of the puncture. Severing limbs on these attacks is an occasional reminder of how sharp Logan’s adamantium claws are. Reinforcing this is top-notch sound and haptics design, so each hit registers.

Industry observers note that the last aspect I’ll touch on is lethality, the rate at which Wolverine is able to dispatch enemies and vice versa. We found that fights where enemies were more technical and could survive a lot undermined what players expected to experience as Wolverine, which was aggressively and lethally tearing through a lot of enemies. On the other hand, combat was less exciting if the enemies didn’t feel like a serious and deadly threat, and you didn’t feel like Wolverine if a little bit of caution could enable you to defend perfectly and avoid all damage.

These aspects led us towards encounters where you confronted large groups of enemies that were highly aggressive, to the point of feeling unfair. Enemies can’t believably go toe-to-toe with Wolverine alone, even world-class mercenaries, so their strategy is in group coordination, which creates a counterweight to Wolverine’s own rage-based momentum.

According to recent reports, marvel’s Wolverine draws in a number of characters from across the X-Men comic mythology, but notably makes no mention of some foundational figures of that fiction – Professor Xavier and Magneto. That, in turn, leads to dramatically different lives for characters like Jean Grey or Logan. Is the narrative you crafted an intentional exploration of a world where those figures weren’t present in the early days of mutant emergence?

I would say it was more of an exploration of the character than the world. We wanted a story where Logan is pulled into conflict not because he’s a crusader, but because there’s no other option. There are no X-Men to help. His growth as a person should be a challenging journey, which could go unearned if he was surrounded by wise, supportive, heroic characters pushing him in the right direction. In contrast, his dynamic with the members of Team X evokes his struggle. The adversity to personal growth is what makes it interesting.

Jean does end up being the person that pushes him in the right direction, and that works because they can relate to each other, having had similar struggles.

In a recent development, in several versions of Marvel storytelling, Jean and Logan share a special bond, but Jean ultimately chooses Scott Summers as a partner. But even without that barrier in your story, Logan still hits some roadblocks to love. Is Wolverine fundamentally a better character when he just can’t get the girl?

The way I would put it is that a Wolverine story is fundamentally better when you empathize with Logan’s pain and admire him for pressing on despite it. That goes for his emotional pain as much as physical. He’s a tragic character in this regard – all he wants is to be at peace but can never find it for long.

In a recent development, wolverine gets to take on a lot of the “heavy hitters” of his comic mythology in different boss fights throughout the game. When you began development, do you recall who the very first character was that you decided he simply had to fight in your game?

Sources indicate that sabretooth. No character is a better foil for Logan. His inner turmoil and chaotic behavior helps illustrate Logan’s own inner beast and his struggle to resist it. Sabretooth’s strength and mutant powers also provide a mirror to Logan in combat, and his savagery creates shocking moments that leave an impression. We knew an epic confrontation with Sabretooth was going to be a thing from the start.

#17310. Forcing yourself to smile can actually make you miserable

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (988 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Forcing yourself to smile can actually make you miserable

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A smile might brighten your mood, but fresh research suggests that forcing yourself to smile over and over can have the opposite effect.
  • For years, psychologist Nicholas Coles, Ph.D., studied evidence suggesting that even an artificial smile could make someone feel a little happier.
  • "I used to work in customer service.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A smile might brighten your mood, but fresh research suggests that forcing yourself to smile over and over can have the opposite effect. When smiling becomes an obligation, especially one tied to financial pressure, it may actually leave people feeling less happy and more irritated.

For years, psychologist Nicholas Coles, Ph.D., studied evidence suggesting that even an artificial smile could make someone feel a little happier. Yet those findings never quite matched his own experiences.

"I used to work in customer service. I actually got written up for my inability to keep smiling at work at an unnamed theme park in Florida," laughed Coles, a professor of psychology at the University of Florida. "So I'm looking at all this evidence I had accrued so far that smiling boosts happiness and realizing it flies in the face of my own experiences in the world.".

According to recent reports, that contradiction inspired Coles and his colleagues to investigate what happens when people must keep smiling, rather than simply trying it once. Their findings suggest an important distinction: A brief, intentional smile can provide a small emotional lift, but repeatedly putting on a smile under pressure can undermine happiness.

Testing How Forced Smiling Affects Happiness.

To explore this difference, Coles worked with researchers Annabel Dang and Joao Francisco Goes Braga Takayanagi to design an experiment that more closely resembled the demands of customer service jobs. Their findings were published on October 1 in the Journal of Experimental Social Psychology.

According to recent reports, "We tried to combine the classic way of studying it in a lab with some extra ingredients that we might see in the real world. We told participants that we would pay them less if they weren't successfully smiling," Coles mentioned. "We also controlled the number of times they have to do it, because in customer service, every interaction is another faked smile.".

The online experiment initially enrolled 1,201 people, with data from 1,174 included in the final analysis. Participants were shown images designed to produce different emotional reactions. Some depicted appealing subjects, such as kittens and flowers, while others showed disturbing situations, including theft and mistreatment of animals.

During the experiment, participants either deliberately formed a smile or allowed their facial expressions to develop naturally. Depending on their assigned group, they completed the exercise once or repeated it 10 times.

To introduce an element of pressure, researchers warned half the participants that failing to follow the smiling instructions could cost them $2 from their $6 payment. However, nobody actually lost any money, and every participant received the full amount.

When Fake Smiles Start to Backfire.

In a recent development, after completing each task, participants reported how happy they felt. The results showed that the emotional effects of smiling depended on how often people had to do it and whether they felt pressured.

Industry observers note that when participants viewed unpleasant images, producing a single smile gave their mood a modest boost. This benefit appeared even among those who had been warned about a possible financial penalty. However, the positive effect weakened when smiling was repeated, and it disappeared when repeated smiles were combined with the threat of losing money.

The pattern was even more revealing when people looked at pleasant pictures. Smiling just once offered little additional happiness compared with allowing their faces to respond naturally. But when participants had to smile repeatedly or felt pressure to do so, their happiness ratings actually fell below those of people who responded naturally.

Industry observers note that further analysis revealed another unexpected consequence. In the pleasant picture conditions, forced smiling was also associated with increased irritation and anger.

"If you only force a smile once without any financial penalties, you can see the improvement in happiness. So what psychologists were seeing in their lab is right," he mentioned. "But when you make it a little bit more like the real world, where you have to keep repeating it, and if you don't do it well, you get financial penalties, you see it completely reverse.".

The Hidden Emotional Cost of Smiling at Work.

These findings may help explain why expectations to appear cheerful throughout the workday can become frustrating rather than uplifting.

In a recent development, the issue has already sparked controversy in the workplace. In recent years, Target faced widespread criticism over a policy requiring employees to smile when customers came within a specified distance. Although the policy was intended to encourage friendly interactions, Coles argues that such requirements can interfere with people's ability to express their emotions naturally.

Sources indicate that the problem may extend beyond employees. Customers can also feel obligated to respond positively to friendliness that is being imposed rather than offered spontaneously. According to Coles, these expectations limit the emotional freedom of both sides of the interaction.

Could Trying Less to Be Happy Make Us Happier?

Recent findings suggest that after spending years investigating how people can improve their emotional well-being, Coles has begun considering a broader question. Rather than constantly searching for ways to increase happiness, might people be better off placing greater value on simply being content?

His research suggests that efforts to manufacture positive emotions do not always produce the intended results. Sometimes, trying too hard to appear happy can make the experience less pleasant.

"As a society, we have placed such an immense amount of emphasis on trying to make ourselves feel happier than we at the moment are," he said, "much less emphasis on just being content with what we have.".

Materials provided by University of Florida. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

8 Long JRPGs That Are Best Played in Switch 2 Handheld Mode
