💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that many JRPGs are long by nature, whether because of seamless exploration, a narrative packed with colorful dialogue, or a post-game that increases our playtime considerably.
  • Sources indicate that one way to keep up with JRPGs is to buy a handheld console, which is becoming increasingly common.
  • When Final Fantasy XIV was first confirmed for Switch 2, I was like: okay, neat!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that many JRPGs are long by nature, whether because of seamless exploration, a narrative packed with colorful dialogue, or a post-game that increases our playtime considerably. The more adulthood knocks at the door, the less time we have to dedicate to our favorite hobby, and well, if that hobby involves playing JRPGs as mine does, you know you are in a bind.

Sources indicate that one way to keep up with JRPGs is to buy a handheld console, which is becoming increasingly common. To ensure you have a packed catalog that gets newly introduced games every day, nothing beats having a Switch 2 at home. So, keeping portability, comfort, and time constraints in mind, I gathered some of the longest JRPGs best played in Switch 2 handheld mode.

When Final Fantasy XIV was first confirmed for Switch 2, I was like: okay, neat! More ways to play. As someone who has played the MMORPG for 13 years on PlayStation consoles, starting on PS3, I couldn't grasp the full potential of that announcement. Then, a friend of mine started the Free Trial, and it hit me after he shared his experience. MMORPGs are, almost by nature, a repetitive endeavor, with dailies, beast tribe quests, crafting, gathering, events, and whatnot. Doing all that in handheld mode? It is the Will of the Light.

In a recent development, FFXIV runs very well on Switch 2, so it's worth it even for veterans or those just starting out. Grinding was never this satisfying. The only caveat is that you have to buy the base game plus expansions again and pay a separate monthly subscription using a token made by Nintendo. But once you surpass these hurdles, portable Eorzea awaits.

Sources indicate that I did a reverse process that left me a bit spoiled: I played Persona 5 before playing Persona 3, the portable version. That left me a bit tired of Tartarus, which felt too repetitive, even though I understood it was a product of its era. Persona 3 Reload improved the Tartarus dungeon crawling by removing random encounters and adding gimmicks like changing dungeon rules and even Shuffle Time.

Before each full moon in Persona 3, there is a bunch of downtime, just evolving Social Links, doing daily chores, and increasing your protagonist's stats. They are all a joy to watch, but since they are less heavy-loaded than the main story, you can easily enjoy them wherever you want to take your Switch 2 and just enjoy handheld mode.

I remember perfectly when I started playing Dragon Quest XI and assumed I liked the slime franchise more than Final Fantasy. After advancing a bit further, I realized I still like Final Fantasy more. Still, Dragon Quest XI is so spectacular and such a stunning evolution of the Dragon Quest formula that I fell in love immediately. DQXI mixes the simplicity and classic feel of its predecessors while modernizing and expanding all features and mechanics, making it the most ambitious title ever made in the series.

Like every Dragon Quest, the JRPG features many, many side objectives, exploration, collectibles, and of course, a robust post-game. To this day, I don't know if Act 3 is canonical or post-game, but either way, expect hundreds of hours simply to complete the main campaign and much more if you want to do everything. And there is nothing better than doing all of that on Switch 2.

Normally, I'd recommend Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter and 2nd Chapter, because they are flawless JRPGs remakes that will guarantee you hundreds of hours of playtime. However, considering I have already recommended them countless times, and in the hope that some of you heeded my call, the next step would be to go to the next arc, Crossbell, featured in the duology Trails from Zero and Trails to Azure.

According to recent reports, coincidentally, both recently received a Switch 2 version, adding more quality-of-life features and visual upgrades. I recognize that the whiplash of coming from a full-fledged remake like the Trails in the Sky versions to the graphical style of Zero and Azure can be a bit shocking, but hear me out: if you don't mind that and manage to finish both, reaching the ending of Trails to Azure, your mind will be blown away, trust me. Plus, there is never a wrong time to meet the members of the Special Support Section.

In a recent development, one of the biggest criticisms I read about Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave was its runtime. Players are loving Nintendo's tactical JRPG, but constantly complain that even after 100 hours, it still doesn't feel close to the end. Honestly, it seems to me that this protest is not because they are not having fun or are tired of the game, but because Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave came out in a period packed with other games, and well, you want to play it all.

But forget about that. There is no time limit on your fun, so just grab your weapons, choose your route, and enjoy your protagonist's story. Fortune's Weave introduces emblematic gameplay changes, freshening up the whole loop while still keeping elements Fire Emblem fans have learned to love and appreciate.

Honestly, I could put any Xenoblade Chronicles here, and it would fit. All of the games received, or will receive in the case of Xenoblade Chronicles 3, an enhanced version for the Nintendo Switch 2 that even added new content. And while all of them feature an immense open world you can explore from the get-go, if you want to play more leisurely in handheld mode, Xenoblade Chronicles X is the way to go.

According to recent reports, xenoblade Chronicles X also has plenty of story and characters to get to know, but director Tetsuya Takahashi said his goal in creating the game was to test the Wii U's technological capabilities with a gigantic world. And the madman did it. You will certainly spend much, much more time doing side content, installing probes, facing Nemeses, and flying around with your Skells than on the main story. And do you know the best way to do so? Yes, Switch 2 full-armed handheld mode.

It has been revealed that metaphor: ReFantazio, just like many Atlus games, is an effortlessly long JRPG. With its calendar system, every day brings a fresh activity, keeping the experience fresh and engaging us without us even noticing. Then, whenever I got tired of roaming around a new city, I could go hunt some monsters, tackle a new dungeon, or watch some impressive story beats unfold in this political race.

Industry observers note that the entire design of Metaphor: ReFantazio is highly gripping, and I was completely consumed by the JRPG without even seeing the hours go by. Come to think of it, maybe suggesting playing Metaphor in handheld mode is a bit dangerous, because if I lost track of hours sitting in an uncomfortable chair, imagine if I could play it on my Switch 2 lying in bed with the air conditioning on. Okay, scratch that, too fun, too dangerous.

In its most recent fiscal report, Square Enix showed great profits and dedicated much of that success to the performance of Final Fantasy VII Rebirth on Switch 2. I understand that in terms of visual quality and performance the JRPG leaves a bit to be desired on Switch 2 compared to other platforms, but in overall experience, gameplay, and comfort, it certainly triumphs. The sprawling open world of Rebirth becomes much more practical when played in handheld mode, especially if you are hunting down minigame trophies.

In a recent development, what took me the longest for the Final Fantasy VII Rebirth platinum was getting high scores in a bunch of Chocobo minigames, Cactuar Crush with Aerith, and of course, Chadley's challenges. That was because I had to stay glued to my TV on my PS5, whereas if I had done it on the couch, all leisurely while watching my son play or my wife watch another K-Drama, the experience would certainly have been much more pleasant. Mind you, story-related moments and cutscenes should have your full attention, especially during the Gold Saucer!

  • Thew latest content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, battlefield 6 is about to receive a newly introduced upgrade. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Thew latest content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only fresh weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Easily the most interesting change in this update is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a significant pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this patch is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

According to recent reports, speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Sources indicate that something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an update. BF Studios indicates there are still some instances where that might happen, but the issue should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, with the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day. And if you’re the gamer in the family, we always encourage you to circle relevant items in the coming pages and leave your magazine open in hard-to-miss locations around the house. We’ve scoured dozens of tech products, tabletop games, collectibles, and more to select and highlight some of the coolest items we found this year.

We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap. This family-friendly platform features original games that sit comfortably between the digital and physical divide. The horizontally placed screen reveals the backdrop of one of the several included games, or the sold-separately add-on games that have popped in since launch. Each game has its own real physical play pieces that interact with the action onscreen, often in innovative and charming ways. Think of it as the best of both worlds between board games and video games, and you’ll get what they’re shooting for here. $399.

Sources indicate that few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this new expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions. New subclasses, spells, creatures, magical items, and factions add thoughtful, intriguing options for both players looking to play someone new and DMs hunting for new story hooks and challenges. $50.

In a recent development, if you’re as excited as we are about this month’s celebration of the Tomb Raider legacy (see p. 40), this centerpiece statue is an ideal fit for your collection. Standing roughly nine inches in height, Lara is poised for exploration in her original classic garb. The sculpt strikes a perfect balance between crisp detail and stylistic presentation, in line with that early version of the character; the metallic blue motorcycle paint is especially striking. $250.

Industry observers note that for players longing for the glory days of stand-up arcade games, it’s hard to beat Arcade 1Up’s approach. The team’s sturdy cabinets look and sound great as a marquee feature of your game room. The fresh Outrun machine features much of the original display art, a bright 19-inch screen, and responsive gas and brake pedals as you steer around those tight corners. Sega has packed in OutRun, Turbo OutRun, OutRunners, and Power Drift. If old-school racing isn’t your thing, look for cabinets that run the gamut from Pac-Man to Joust to Claw Machines. $629.99.

The long-running Nendoroid figures continue to be an attractive but still affordable choice for building collections across numerous fan-favorite series. There are somewhere around 2000 characters at this point! Latest entries like the Genshin Impact collection make a strong case for the line. The look is chibi, the quality is excellent, poseability is high, and customizable face and accessory parts let you change up your display over time. $46.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve previously sung the praises of Libernovo’s versatile approach to an ergonomic gaming chair, which includes a lumbar stretch functionality, a steady recline option for comfortable pushback without sudden shifts, and dynamically adjusting parts as you move through your day. The Maxis line does all that, but addresses one of the fundamental problems for at least some people with the original – it wasn’t big enough. With features like a wider base and longer headrest reach, the Maxis aims to provide the same comfort to the players who are tall or wide enough to need the extra breathing room. $1119.

According to recent reports, privacy around smart glasses has been a major point of contention as wearable tech continues to expand. Even G2s have a clear answer to that issue by consciously leaving out a camera. Instead, these glasses focus on productivity and specific tasks, like real-time translation into 35 languages, in-lens teleprompters for presentations, and calendar notifications – all presented in a readable display that is largely invisible from the outside. $600.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re the player on your team who likes to have easy access to soundboards and real-time voice changing, the Key Pocket could be just the ticket. This small device straps onto your phone for mobile play, but it’s also compatible with consoles, Discord, Twitch, or just about any place you want to tweak audio on the fly. A free tier gives you access to some voice-changing and sounds, while a separate subscription opens up hundreds of thousands of additional options. But be warned: we can’t help you after your friends abandon you for that baby voice you won’t stop using. $99.

Sources indicate that the question of the best bang for your buck in modern consoles has become extraordinarily complicated, especially as tech prices have soared in recent years. There’s no right answer, but Sony’s high-end machine walks the line of offering extremely high-tier performance without escalating to even higher-priced gaming PCs. Higher and more consistent frame rates than on standard PS5, advanced ray tracing, and an increasing number of games that feature enhanced PSSR image options all add up to a better gaming experience, if you’re ready to make the significant price jump. $900.

If the gamer in your life is looking for a stylish, understated way to express their love of the hobby, Anicorn’s designer watch collaboration with PlayStation could be a standout option. Available in black and a slick silver/white combo, the minimalist timepiece includes the familiar face buttons of Sony’s controller encased in an oil-injection display so they slowly and freely float across the watch as you move. $250.

It’s a safe bet you’ve at least seen the popular Shashibo puzzle cubes by this point. We’ve been fans of their brain-teasing, fidgety fun for some time. Battle Shapes takes the core concept – reshaping the box into various distinct magnetically-locked shapes – and extends it into a timed game experience, playable solo or head-to-head. By targeting specific shapes, you significantly improve your speed with the toy, and scannable QR codes on the cards offer clear tutorials for each shape so you can prep for competition. $50.

Sources indicate that while the vast majority of gamers looking for good personal audio are going to be okay with a larger set of cans over their ears, We know more than a few players for whom that’s a definite no – for comfort, awareness of surrounding sounds, or other reasons. The Arc 5 earbuds aim to solve for that, with an over-ear design that feels extremely comfortable. And because they sit on the ear, you can still hear what’s going on around you. While that limits some aspects of the final sound quality, the inclusion of THX certification, Dolby Atmos optimization, and Dynamic Bass Enhancement helps to ensure audio is still very strong. $230.

Sources indicate that across Lego’s many recent themes, Tolkien’s legendarium has offered some stellar sets. The largest yet is the capital of Gondor, with an astonishing 8,278 pieces and a height of roughly two feet. The castle/city build is impressive, featuring tons of interesting angles and turns. The finished product aims to offer the best of both worlds in presentation – a microscale representation of the front façade and a reverse minifigure-scale Hall of Kings. We especially like the inclusion of Denethor’s cherry tomatoes. $650.

The original Azul is often cited as a foundational entry in modern board gaming. The “Kids” versions of celebrated titles aren’t always a sure bet, but this one holds up to scrutiny. Azul Kids lowers the complexity threshold but keeps the foundational strategic thinking. Players lay out uniquely shaped tiles into mosaic frameworks in colorful, appealing patterns; the basic concept of the original inspiration is clear, and kids as young as five can grasp and enjoy the fun. $25.

In a recent development, many corners of the collecting world have embraced the fun (and frequent despair) of blind boxes, where you never know exactly who you’ll get in a given series. Funism has a strong track record for quality, offering adorable smaller figures like their latest line of Evangelion collectibles. Each figure stands nearly four inches and features both human characters and mecha. You can buy singles and roll the dice, or purchase larger sets with a no-duplicates guarantee, which can save a lot of heartache if you’re trying to line your whole shelf. $21.

If you’re going to spring for a high-end keyboard for PC gaming, it’s key that you like the feel of the keys. The slightly smaller overall 75% size profile of this Blackwidow has no impact on the great feel of typing – a clear highlight for the unit. The customizable, colored backlights are also a big selling point, as is the side command dial and built-in OLED display, which can be tweaked to show PC performance, GIFs, lighting brightness, and more. It’s a strong contender in a crowded field, and justifies its price with both comfort and customizability. $300.

Beautiful, vibrant art and a refreshing take on the classic area-control board game genre are the two strongest reasons to take a close look at Wroth. Players control one of five races vying for supremacy across a conflict-ridden peninsula. Factions are asymmetric, so everyone has unique capabilities, and that adds significant replayability. Players roll and draft dice, allowing distinct actions that move the game forward. And move it does; unlike many games of this ilk, Wroth can be learned swiftly and played to completion in a little over an hour. $65.

It has been revealed that console and computer hardware prices are skyrocketing with no sign of slowing, and perhaps as a result, retro gaming handhelds are gaining popularity. Many quality devices are available, but what sets the Evercade Nexus apart is its officially licensed game cartridges. Imagine the nostalgic joy of a Game Boy, but with a cartridge that includes both Banjo-Kazooie and Tooie. The cartridge boxes even include manuals. For fans of physical media, Evercade Nexus is a great option. $199.

Sources indicate that this tiny USB-C plug-in (with included USB-A adapter) solves a bunch of audio challenges in one uniform device. It offers high-resolution Bluetooth transmission on iPhone, high-bitrate audio transmission to compatible LDAC headphones, enables high-quality Bluetooth output from your PC, and even low-latency Bluetooth audio on PS5 and Switch. In short, it takes a huge number of products with a USB port and ensures a dynamic Bluetooth audio connection with relative ease. $99.

Industry observers note that the original MV6 is a familiar sight on streams thanks to its clear voice reproduction and overall ease of use. Shure has built on that success with the Gen 2, offering an excellent standalone mic that doesn’t break the bank. Available in black or white, the Gen 2 features a handy auto-level mode that keeps volume even as you adjust your own amplitude, an adjustable denoiser for your space, a longer cable for out-of-the-box convenience, and three presets for plug-and-play use. In short, it’s an excellent choice if you want great performance without needing an audio engineering degree. $169.

XR Glasses are still fighting for awareness, but once you try them, it’s easy to see why the concept is on the rise. Viture’s Pro 2 makes an impressive case for adoption, with a competitive price point, comfortable wear, and a giant 146-inch screen that floats in front of your face for gaming or work on your PC or phone. The display is crisp, bright, and impressive, even as the glasses are light and easy to use. With a mobile dock mini (sold separately), you can even snap onto a Switch 2 with ease and start playing instantly. $299.

Role-playing gamers have several excellent universal systems to pick between when considering a story or campaign idea that might fall outside traditional genre staples. Among many good options, Cypher stands out as one of the very best. The system uses a rules-light, narrative-focused approach that prioritizes player-driven storytelling across everything from hard sci-fi to superheroes to intrigue- driven espionage. This is the corebook that’s needed to run and play the full system; additional books only add options. $50.

Industry observers note that as gamers have continually migrated toward personal audio that can rock amazing sound without disturbing the whole house, high-end premium headphones have become a dangerously competitive space. Turtle Beach meets that challenge head-on, with a robust option that sounds beautiful in use. The Stealth Pro II boasts the slick ability to wirelessly switch between different devices, which is awesome if you’re one of those players who regularly jumps between platforms to play your favorite titles. Like the whole category, it’s a lot to spend on a headset, but Dolby Atmos, active noise cancellation, and 60mm dual drivers all add up to a powerful argument. $300.

It has been revealed that with an increasing number of top-tier console and PC games like Resident Evil Village, No Man’s Sky, and Dead Cells now available on iOS, not to mention the consistent quality of Apple Arcade, Apple phones remain the best mobile platform for gaming. The 18 Pro Max phone has implemented a number of tweaks that strengthen the platform, including higher memory, much faster graphics processing, impressive HDR performance, and notably improved battery life, all adding up to a gaming experience that is working hard to justify your playtime when away from home. Starting at $1299.

SteelSeries is best known for its strong audio line-up, but its push into premium-tier controllers exhibits a similar flair for quality and usability. The latest Aeon Pro has a lot to recommend it as your go-to Xbox, PC, or mobile choice. The two included batteries (one of which can always be charging in the dock) ensure essentially unlimited playtime. The full-pull or hair triggers and buttons are clicky and satisfying, and the Hall Effect thumbsticks are built to minimize any drift. Textured handgrips and overall heft are ideal. And an onboard OLED lets you adjust profiles and button assignments, switch between platforms, and check battery at a glance. $260.

It has been revealed that valve’s pricey VR headset isn’t a revolution in the medium, but the firm has been invested in the technology since its inception. As a result, the Steam Frame is a very good, very comfortable headset. Like its competition, the Quest, its best use is playing games locally on the headset, and Steam’s library is vast and interesting. Wireless connected play to a powerful PC is also well done, but right now the included Wireless Adapter is not fully compatible with the Steam Machine – a baffling limitation we were shocked to confirm. VR is an expensive sub-hobby within video games, but Steam Frame is among the best ways to explore and enjoy it. $1059.

Industry observers note that many of the coolest “gaming lights” focus on the flexibility and fun of bright RGB customization. While we’re fans of that aesthetic, it leaves others out in the cold who might want something a bit more natural. The Elements hex panels feature a natural wood-inspired panel, customizable “scenes” like a campfire glow, and can react to both music and touch, with adjustable ambient white light to keep the vibe relaxed. $200.

Kyle Hilliard contributed to this article.

Exercise after ACL surgery may protect knees from early osteoarthritis

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A serious knee injury can cause problems that persist long after surgery, but fresh research suggests that the right exercise program could make a major difference.
  • Recovery from ACL surgery is often more difficult than expected.
  • Sources indicate that medical guidelines recommend combining exercise rehabilitation with patient education after ACL surgery, yet many people receive treatment that falls short of these recommendations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A serious knee injury can cause problems that persist long after surgery, but fresh research suggests that the right exercise program could make a major difference. A clinical trial led by researchers at La Trobe University found that supervised exercise and education can improve knee health, reduce pain, and enhance quality of life in young adults recovering from anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction. The findings also offer hope for addressing their elevated risk of developing knee osteoarthritis at an unusually young age.

Recovery from ACL surgery is often more difficult than expected. About half of patients are still dissatisfied with their knee health two years after the procedure. Even more concerning, roughly half develop signs of early-onset knee osteoarthritis within a decade, often before reaching age 40.

Sources indicate that medical guidelines recommend combining exercise rehabilitation with patient education after ACL surgery, yet many people receive treatment that falls short of these recommendations. One obstacle is the widespread concern, shared by some patients and healthcare professionals, that exercise could damage already vulnerable knee cartilage.

A Fresh Approach to Recovery After ACL Surgery.

In a recent development, to investigate whether additional rehabilitation could help, researchers at La Trobe University's Sport and Exercise Medicine Research Centre conducted the SUPER-Knee clinical trial. It was the first study to evaluate the benefits of combining exercise therapy and education more than nine months after ACL reconstruction, a time when patients are generally expected to have recovered even though many continue to experience problems.

It has been revealed that the researchers enrolled 184 adults between the ages of 18 and 40 who were still struggling with knee symptoms one to three years after their operations. Participants were assigned to either a progressive exercise therapy program or a comparison group that received a single educational session.

The findings, published in Annals of Internal Medicine, highlighted that participants who completed the four-month program under the guidance of a physical therapist experienced improvements in knee health and muscle strength, along with less pain and better quality of life.

It has been revealed that importantly, these benefits came without evidence that the exercises were damaging knee cartilage or worsening early osteoarthritis. The results challenge the belief that physical activity necessarily makes injured knees worse.

Exercise Offers Hope Against Early Knee Osteoarthritis.

Associate Professor Adam Culvenor, who led the research, said the findings provide much-needed evidence about how to help younger patients who remain at risk of knee osteoarthritis following ACL surgery.

According to recent reports, "Right now we don't have any high-quality evidence for what treatments should be offered to young people at risk of early-onset knee osteoarthritis. Our SUPER-Knee study changes this, and addresses a globally recognized research priority," Associate Professor Culvenor said.

"Our study showed physiotherapist-supervised exercise therapy and education is safe and should be recommended to improve the knee health of young people at high risk of early-onset osteoarthritis following ACL reconstruction.

"The evidence generated by the SUPER-Knee trial can be used to update international clinical practice guidelines for rehabilitation following ACL reconstruction and could be a lifeline for young people struggling after serious knee injuries.

"The intervention is ready to be used by local health professionals with minimal specialized equipment or staff training.".

The findings could influence how clinicians approach rehabilitation long after ACL surgery, particularly for patients whose symptoms continue beyond the usual recovery period. Although the trial did not establish whether the program prevents osteoarthritis over the long term, it demonstrated that supervised exercise can improve knee health without accelerating the cartilage damage or early osteoarthritis researchers were monitoring.

Years of Knee Pain After a Serious Sports Injury.

Recent findings suggest that for Ruby Cumming, the challenges of recovering from ACL surgery were deeply personal. In 2019, when she was 24, she tore her ACL while playing Australian rules football. Hoping to return to the sport as promptly as possible, she underwent reconstructive surgery within six weeks.

Recent findings suggest that but the operation did not lead to the recovery she had imagined. Her rehabilitation continued for years, and she ultimately decided not to return to football.

"I thought if I had the surgery and did the rehab I'd be able to get back to normal. After surgery impacted my entire life - not just footy - I changed my outlook and decided I wanted to avoid re-injuring my knee ever again so haven't played contact sport since," Ruby said.

"Experiencing regular pain, not being able to walk, getting public transport to work and living independently all became really challenging for me.".

Industry observers note that cumming remained committed to her rehabilitation, regularly attending physical therapy appointments and performing prescribed exercises. She initially exercised daily before moving to a weekly routine. Despite those efforts, she continued to experience varying degrees of knee pain every day for three to four years.

Her experience changed after she enrolled in the SUPER-Knee trial and began participating in weekly rehabilitation sessions supervised by a physical therapist.

"When I joined the SUPER-Knee program and did weekly physio-supervised rehab, this improved my pain significantly," Ruby said.

Sources indicate that the research suggests that people who continue to struggle after ACL reconstruction may benefit from additional structured rehabilitation, even years after their original injury. Because the program requires little specialized equipment or additional staff training, researchers say healthcare professionals could readily incorporate it into existing treatment services.

The SUPER-Knee clinical trial received funding through a Project Grant from Australia's National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the name Aston Martin conjures images of luxurious grand tourers flowing swiftly down curving mountain roads, perhaps with a certain British MI6 secret agent sitting suavely behind the wheel. In recent years, Aston Martin has also become increasingly involved in racing, from its Vantage-based GT3 car to Formula 1. Now, the British automaker is embarking on a new motorsports challenge, and it’s not one we were expecting: Aston Martin will compete in the 2027 Dakar Rally.

Recent findings suggest that dakar, for those unfamiliar, is one of the most grueling off-road rally races in the world. Starting in 1979, drivers originally raced from Paris, France, to Dakar, Senegal. More recently, the rally has been held in the desert of Saudi Arabia, departing its original location after violence in Mauritania. Now, the tension in the Middle East caused by the war between the United States and Iran has forced the Dakar Rally to move once again.

See all results for used Aston Martin for sale near 19805.

In a recent development, aston Martin’s first Dakar will see the fledgling outfit run from Loulé, Portugal, to Marrakesh, Morocco. Although this is Aston Martin’s first time entering the Dakar Rally, it has found a well-versed partner in Prodrive. The British racing and engineering organization developed the BRX Hunter, which ran from 2021 to 2024, managing a best finish of second, before partnering with Dacia to create the Sandrider, which ran in 2025 and 2026, triumphing at last year’s event.

Sources indicate that prodrive and Aston Martin already work together on endurance GT racing, so it’s not a shock that Aston Martin collaborated with Prodrive to develop and build the newly introduced Dreadnought rally raid car. This rally challenger borrows its name from an SUV designed by Aston Martin for the recently introduced Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 video game, and it shares some design elements with the virtual off-roader.

According to recent reports, the front end is characterized by a pair of octagonal lights that mirror the square pixel lighting from the video-game SUV. Like the Sandrider, the spare tires are tucked into the bodywork just behind the rear doors. Around back, the slatted roof, tall ducktail spoiler, and intricate LED lighting carry over from the Call of Duty Dreadnought. No technical details were revealed about the Dakar racer just yet, but we wouldn’t be surprised if the Aston Martin shares some components with the Sandrider, just as it was an evolution of the BRX Hunter. A fresh engine is likely—the Hunter used a Ford twin-turbo 3.5-liter V-6 and the Dacia used a Nissan twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6—but we don’t know what Aston Martin and Prodrive settled on, although a Mercedes-Benz V-6 seems likely.

See all results for used Aston Martin for sale near 19805.

Recent findings suggest that aston Martin has also amassed an incredible lineup of drivers for the race. Two-time Formula 1 World Champion and current Aston Martin F1 driver Fernando Alonso will take a break from driving on pavement to pilot one of the three Dreadnoughts. Alonso has competed in the Dakar Rally once before, taking a Toyota Hilux race truck to 13th place in 2020.

The second car will be driven by Sébastien Loeb, a nine-time World Rally champion who has finished second three times at the Dakar. Loeb is extremely familiar with Prodrive machinery, spending the last six years driving the BRX Hunter and the Dacia Sandrider. Last but not least, Aston Martin has signed Lucas Moraes, the 2025 World Rally Raid champion who has a best finish at Dakar of third, to drive the third Dreadnought.

In a recent development, the 2027 Dakar Rally kicks off on January 9 and runs over 12 stages until January 23. The competitors will cover a total of 4228 miles, with 2600 miles consisting of special stages, the timed portion of the event that occurs over the most challenging terrain. While Aston Martin will be a fresh face in the Dakar bivouac, a seasoned group of drivers and a successful partner in Prodrive give the upcoming team promise when the rally kicks off in two months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Where Winds Meet already has a staggering amount of content, but that’s not the end of what we can expect. Developer Everstone Studio just revealed a host of latest additions coming to the game this month.

It’s clear that the developer is committed to the free-to-play action RPG, and the game’s recent success on Steam, and PlayStation has more than likely solidified the team’s plans for the future of the game.

On the official Where Winds Meet account on Twitter, the developer shared a brief roadmap of some of what we can expect over the course of December. The roadmap is split into the four weeks of the month, covering everything from smaller quests to more larger additions.

The first week started off a little light, with two newly introduced Jianghu Legacy Quests: Twelve Years of Feuds, and An Unholy Prophecy. Both quests are currently available in the game.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it’ll come as no surprise to any gamer that pretty much every game has a way to cheat, whether it's approved by the developers or otherwise.
  • While a lot of the punishments for cheating in more recent years are typical things like warnings or outright bans, there are some that take a more creative approach.
  • This list consists of many games from all sorts of genres and ages, but they all have some interesting and hilarious punishments for what they perceive as cheating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’ll come as no surprise to any gamer that pretty much every game has a way to cheat, whether it's approved by the developers or otherwise. Over the years there have been some pretty creative and hilarious ways that developers have dealt with cheaters in all kinds of games from FPS games to the cozy ones.

While a lot of the punishments for cheating in more recent years are typical things like warnings or outright bans, there are some that take a more creative approach. Whether it’s a fun way to kill the player or an incredibly punishing turn of events for dark deeds, it’s always funny to see that happen.

This list consists of many games from all sorts of genres and ages, but they all have some interesting and hilarious punishments for what they perceive as cheating. It may not always be altering game files and could just be something players are able to abuse in game.

It has been revealed that way back in 1996 Crusader: No Regret came out following in the footsteps of its predecessor Crusader: No Remorse. The isometric gameplay combined with some great weapons and destructive environments made a very engaging combination.

Recent findings suggest that the only problem was if you played the previous game and attempted to use any cheats from the last game Crusader: No Regret would have something to say about it. Players would be greeted with a message and teleported into a room with eight copies of the final boss.

Heretic was created using the DOOM engine, but things were a bit mixed up and instead of the traditional DOOM world this one was steeped in fantasy elements. Everything revolved around the fantasy element as players could use magical weapons like the Elven Wand, and Phoenix Rod.

Unfortunately for players who were well educated in the ways of DOOM, the developers had a surprise for anyone hoping to use DOOM cheats. Inserting the cheat for God Mode would instantly kill players, and the all weapons cheat would instead reduce you to using just a wooden staff.

It has been revealed that with the recent remaster of Ocarina of Time there’s a lot of great details in the Legend of Zelda series coming to light. Some are just fun little tidbits or small things, but in Link’s Awakening the dev team decided to make things a little harder for anyone doing nefarious things with Link.

Link can steal some items from a shopkeeper by distracting him and then grabbing the items to take outside. Not only does doing this ruin Link’s reputation earning him the mark of thief by any other NPCs, that shopkeeper will also kill Link to settle the debt.

Traditional MMOs typically don’t play too well with cheaters, resulting in all kinds of punishments, but one MMO really stands out, EVE Online. This old school MMORPG is all about space battles and exploration in its entirely player driven world.

During a GM Week event there were public executions of cheaters who had been caught and the team opened up the destruction of these ships to any players who wanted to join. This turned it into an incredible spectacle that many will not soon forget.

According to recent reports, the Sims series is probably one of the most prolific gaming franchises on the planet, being enjoyed by a huge demographic of people. Even in these cute games people try to cheat and The Sims devs were not going to let that slide even on the DS.

According to recent reports, if you attempted to use the internal system clock to skip time forward the game would notice and spawn an alien invasion that would cause a lot of problems. They become a persistent problem in the game and could require players to restart the game.

CD Projekt Red are known for their storytelling and incredible game design, but they don’t just stop being amazing there. While the devs respect when players are able to find something they hadn’t accounted for they didn’t stop them from doing it, they just got a bit creative.

It has been revealed that when The Witcher 3 originally came out there was an exploit that would let you kill cows in the starter area indefinitely giving you crazy amounts of money. To fix that they simply spawned a giant late game monster, a Chort, that would likely kill players as a punishment.

Sources indicate that there’s nothing quite like finding out a classic game has punishments for attempted cheating, and Pokemon Ruby and Sapphire is no exception. Despite being a game for mostly young people they weren’t going to stand by and let someone cheat in their game.

According to recent reports, pokemon, of course, has a way to mess with players who were able to manipulate game code although it's a bit different from others on the list. Instead of anything dangerous the game would spawn a Bad Egg in a box that cannot be moved creating an matter with inventory for the rest of the game.

Cheat codes in games have been around for longer than most gamers, so a lot of early games allowed players to put them in. Now just like some other games, they want to encourage you to still play the regular way and have to get a bit more creative about punishments.

It has been revealed that banjo-Kazooie took this to an extreme and offered players the ability to put in forbidden codes doing all kinds of silly things. If you put in too many Gruntilda will threaten to erase your save file, making this a very dangerous gamble if you aren’t careful.

Edmund can’t ever do something in half measures and Mewgenics is more than proof of that in almost every aspect. The game took a lot of things to extremes and dealing with cheaters is no exception.

According to recent reports, if you tried to save-scum, quitting out of something quickly to reload a previous save, the game would know and you’d meet Steven. The first time you do this in a run he gives you a warning, but if you continue to do it you’ll no longer have control of the game and Steven will make all the choices.

Industry observers note that not many games have the sense of humor that The Stanley Parable has and this, of course, has to extend beyond the metaness of the game. This hilarious narrative game wants you to focus on the order of events and not have you screw that all up.

Recent findings suggest that if a player attempts to use console cheats the game takes notice and sends them to the Serious Room where the narrator has some choice words for them. Continuing to do it only makes the punishment longer and more ridiculous, much like everything in the game.

A surprising brain difference may explain why some kids struggle with math

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For some children, learning math is much more difficult than it is for their classmates.
  • Recent findings suggest that one possible explanation lies in differences in how the brain selects and manages strategies for solving problems.
  • The findings, published in JNeurosci, come from research led by Oliver Lasnick and colleagues at Stanford University.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For some children, learning math is much more difficult than it is for their classmates. Even when they practice and receive instruction, they may continue to struggle with problems that other children their age can solve more easily. Researchers are now uncovering clues about why these difficulties persist, and the answers may involve more than an understanding of numbers.

Recent findings suggest that one possible explanation lies in differences in how the brain selects and manages strategies for solving problems. A latest study from Stanford University suggests that children with persistent math difficulties may have trouble adjusting their approach when faced with different mathematical challenges. The researchers also identified distinctive patterns of brain activity associated with these struggles.

The findings, published in JNeurosci, come from research led by Oliver Lasnick and colleagues at Stanford University. Their work focused on children with a condition that causes ongoing difficulty with mathematical problem solving (developmental dyscalculia). Although the condition has been recognized for years, scientists are still working to understand the specific thinking processes and brain mechanisms that contribute to it.

Why Some Children Struggle With Math Strategies.

To investigate these challenges, the Stanford team studied 68 children between the ages of 8 and 10. They examined how the children approached math problems, how effectively they used different strategies, and how their brain activity related to their performance.

Solving a math problem often requires more than knowing numbers or remembering arithmetic facts. Children must also decide which approach will work best. For example, a child might count individual numbers to find an answer or use a more efficient method based on a familiar mathematical relationship. As problems become more difficult, the ability to recognize when a different strategy is needed can become increasingly important.

The researchers found that children with developmental dyscalculia were generally less effective at using different mathematical strategies than children without the condition. They took longer to shift from one method to another and were less responsive when the difficulty of a problem changed.

Another important difference involved learning to choose better strategies over time. While other children became more effective at selecting appropriate approaches, those with developmental dyscalculia did not show the same improvement. This suggests that their difficulties may involve not only performing calculations but also deciding how to approach a problem in the first place.

Brain Activity Reveals Latest Clues to Math Difficulties.

The researchers also examined patterns of brain activity to better understand what might be happening behind these behavioral differences.

They discovered that activity within a particular brain system differed between children with developmental dyscalculia and those who were more skilled at selecting and using math strategies. These neural patterns were not simply unrelated differences. They could also predict how effectively children counted and how well they switched between approaches when solving problems.

The findings highlight the possible importance of several mental abilities that extend beyond mathematics itself. These include attention, memory, and cognitive flexibility, which is the ability to adjust thinking or behavior when circumstances change.

According to recent reports, such abilities are part of what researchers often call executive functions. These mental processes help people organize information, stay focused on a task, hold relevant details in mind, and change plans when an approach is not working. In mathematics, they can help a child keep track of numbers, compare possible solutions, and recognize when to try a different method.

Recent findings suggest that the Stanford findings suggest that difficulties involving these processes may contribute to the development of dyscalculia. Differences in brain activity may also help explain why some children have persistent trouble choosing and changing problem-solving strategies.

Sources indicate that however, the observed connections do not establish that the brain activity differences directly cause the condition. They provide newly introduced evidence about the cognitive and neural processes associated with these mathematical difficulties.

Understanding Why Math Struggles Differ Between Children.

An important conclusion is that developmental dyscalculia does not appear to involve one simple problem shared by every affected child. Instead, different children may experience difficulties involving several interacting mental processes.

As Lasnick explains, "Importantly, this study also emphasizes the individual variability observed in dyscalculia, further demonstrating that the disorder reflects cognitive and neural dysfunction across multiple processes.".

By connecting children's mathematical behavior with measurable differences in brain activity, the research offers a more detailed picture of why math can be persistently challenging for some students.

It has been revealed that the findings also point toward the importance of looking beyond whether a child gets the correct answer. Understanding how children choose strategies, adapt to more difficult problems, and manage the mental demands of mathematics could ultimately help researchers develop better ways to identify and support those with developmental dyscalculia.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, there’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch.
  • Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.
  • Immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some new holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the revision’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.

Immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The concern is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios quickly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The issue remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer stated it’s working on a proper fix.

Perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

Recent findings suggest that ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to quickly jump into the latest content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the issue, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the patch.

Recent findings suggest that but Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an patch once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an problem that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the newly introduced Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

It has been revealed that this is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the new enhancement has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

It’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many issues at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst revision yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Blue Oval's most famous stallion has historically been a sports car for the masses, but the Ford Mustang GTD isn't for the faint of heart or pocket. For all intents and purposes, the GTD is an IMSA GT3 racecar for the road, but with far more power. Sandwiched between its flared-and- vented front fenders, a supercharged V-8 sends 815 racehorses sprinting through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. For reference, the Mustang GT3 race cars that compete in IMSA and at Le Mans only make around 550 horsepower.

Earth-quaking power is only one of the GTD's tricks, though, and with advanced active aerodynamics, a racing-derived pushrod rear suspension setup, and carbon-fiber bodywork, Ford's super pony can beat all production cars but Mercedes's AMG One hypercar around the Nürburgring Nordschleife. While the racetrack is undeniably the GTD's natural habitat, it's also surprisingly civilized on the road. That combination of traits, and an ultra-limited production run, makes the GTD a rare breed with a six-digit price tag to match.

Expert Tip: If you're after a lightning-fast palomino but can't quite justify the GTD's retirement-draining price tag, the Ford Mustang Darkhorse SC is well worth looking into. The SC might not have the GTD's trick suspension, but it features a virtually identical supercharged Predator 5.2-liter V-8 that churns out 795 horsepower.

Ford has a few minor changes in store for the GTD in 2028. After encountering manufacturing concerns earlier in the GTD's build cycle, magnesium wheels are finally available. The company claims that the new wheels save 50.3 pounds of unsprung mass, which should positively impact handling.

According to recent reports, in addition to the new wheels, the GTD's paddle shifters have been redesigned and are now 3D printed from titanium. An additional stripe design has also been added to the order sheet, and the Liquid Carbon special edition now comes with teal accenting.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

Sources indicate that with 815 horsepower from its supercharged Predator 5.2-liter V-8 engine, the roadgoing car has far more power than the Mustang GT3 race car it shares styling with. That track-only model instead uses a 5.4-liter V-8 with around 550 horsepower. Cog swaps for the GTD come courtesy of a rear-mounted eight-speed dual-clutch automated transaxle, similar to the type of gearbox used in the race car.

Recent findings suggest that A Mustang GTD we tested blew us away with its performance. Its shockingly civilized on-road ride quality surprised us as well. We would welcome more steering feedback, but the supremely balanced handling and staggering levels of grip make for a world-class driving experience.

In Comparison: The Mustang GTD is quick, but two other rear-drive rockets, the Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 and Porsche 911 GT3 RS, outran it to 60 mph in our testing, completing that task in 2.2 and 2.7 seconds, respectively.

Recent findings suggest that the Ford Mustang GTD prioritizes lap times over fuel economy, as the roar from its mighty supercharged V-8 swiftly reveals. As a result, the GTD only manages a pitiful 10 mpg in the city, 17 mpg on the highway, and 12 mpg combined, according to the EPA. For more information about the Mustang GTD's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

Sources indicate that first Row: Though it looks every bit like the Mustang GT3 purpose-built race car on the outside, the GTD's cabin looks a lot like any ol' Mustang's. Suede, leather, and carbon fiber are the main ingredients of the GTD's interior that upgrade it from its lesser kin—though not by much. Recaro bucket seats hug both driver and front passenger, but the GTD jettisons the rear seats of other Mustang models. The paddle shifters are 3D-printed from titanium, same for the rotary dial gear selector and serial placard. Ford claims it sourced the material for these components from retired Lockheed Martin F-22 fighter jets.

Cargo Capacity: The trunk is a treasure box of suspension and cooling components, but there is room for some small pieces of soft luggage where the rear seat used to be.

In a recent development, the Mustang GTD packs a 12.4-inch digital gauge cluster and a 13.2-inch touchscreen infotainment display. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard equipment. Though the system is largely the same as that of other Mustangs, it does include additional GTD-exclusive performance menus.

As you'd expect of a car like this, the GTD doesn't have many driver-assistance features, but it does have a lane-keep assist system and automatic emergency braking.

For information about the GTD's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

The Mustang GTD has a solid but average warranty. However, unlike rival Chevy, Ford doesn't provide a complimentary scheduled maintenance visit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Industry observers note that starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

According to recent reports, on Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

It has been revealed that the last change in this revision affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

According to recent reports, alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it introduced in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

In a recent development, but, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

#17294. Scientists discover a surprisingly simple way to turn coffee waste into fuel

Scientists discover a surprisingly simple way to turn coffee waste into fuel

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (950 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Used coffee grounds may be far more valuable than they appear.
  • Industry observers note that the findings, published in Biomass and Bioenergy, highlight the untapped potential of spent coffee grounds, a waste product generated in enormous quantities worldwide.
  • Finding a More Efficient Way to Extract Oil From Coffee Grounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Used coffee grounds may be far more valuable than they appear. Instead of ending up in the trash, this everyday waste could provide ingredients for renewable fuels and a variety of useful chemicals. Researchers at Universitat Rovira i Virgili (URV) have identified an efficient way to recover oil from discarded coffee grounds while keeping the remaining material suitable for other industrial applications.

Industry observers note that the findings, published in Biomass and Bioenergy, highlight the untapped potential of spent coffee grounds, a waste product generated in enormous quantities worldwide. Global coffee bean production reaches approximately 10 million metric tons annually, but only a small fraction of the beans' material makes its way into the brewed beverage. Much of the rest is discarded as solid waste. These leftover grounds contain roughly 15% lipids, or fats, which can serve as ingredients for producing biodiesel.

Finding a More Efficient Way to Extract Oil From Coffee Grounds.

Sources indicate that to determine how best to recover these valuable oils, researchers Jorge F. Romero, Alberto Tampieri, Daniel Montané, Magdalena Constantí, and Francesc Medina from URV's Department of Chemical Engineering examined three variables: extraction temperature, processing duration, and the amount of solvent used relative to the coffee grounds.

The team used n-hexane, a solvent widely employed to separate fats from other materials. Through a series of carefully designed experiments, they evaluated how changes in temperature, extraction time, and solvent quantity affected the results, both individually and in combination.

"We have found that the optimal conditions are at 45°C for 60 minutes with a ratio of 35 milliliters of hexane per gram of dry residue," explained Magdalena Constantí, one of the study's authors.

Industry observers note that under these conditions, the researchers recovered approximately 90% as much oil as could be extracted using Soxhlet, a standard laboratory method known for its high extraction yields. Although Soxhlet is effective, it generally takes longer, consumes more energy, and is less practical for large industrial operations.

Recent findings suggest that the newer approach also produced considerably cleaner oil. The optimized extraction yielded just 0.3% impurities, compared with 3.9% using Soxhlet. Chemical analysis revealed that the oil's fatty acid composition remained consistent across the different experimental conditions, with linoleic and palmitic acids making up the largest shares. This composition supports the oil's potential use as an ingredient in biodiesel production.

Coffee Waste Could Produce More Than Just Biodiesel.

Recovering oil is only one part of the opportunity. The scientists also wanted to ensure that extracting the fats would not destroy the remaining coffee material, which contains compounds that could be used to manufacture additional fuels and chemicals.

"In our study, we also demonstrate that extracting the oil does not mean that the rest of the material cannot be used for something else," pointed out Francesc Medina, a researcher at the Department of Chemical Engineering who participated in the research.

A central goal was to protect the structural components of the leftover coffee grounds, collectively known as the lignocellulosic matrix. This material contains cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin, substances that can be processed into products such as bioethanol, lactic acid, polyhydroxyalkanoates, phenolic compounds, and ingredients used to produce sustainable aviation fuels.

According to recent reports, removing the oil may actually make the remaining material easier to process. Fats can form a barrier that prevents solvents and catalysts from reaching other useful components within the plant matter. By extracting the oils without substantially changing the underlying structure, the researchers created a residue better suited for further processing.

In this way, the method serves two purposes. It recovers a potentially valuable source of biodiesel ingredients while preparing the leftover biomass for conversion into other products.

A Simpler Approach to Sustainable Biofuel Production.

It has been revealed that the team also investigated whether more advanced extraction methods could deliver better results. These included techniques that use ultrasound or microwaves to accelerate oil recovery.

According to recent reports, although both alternatives can speed up the early stages of extraction, neither offered a sufficiently compelling overall improvement. When the researchers considered oil purity, extraction efficiency, energy requirements, and the potential to expand production to an industrial scale, the conventional batch process using n-hexane under moderate conditions emerged as the more balanced option.

That combination of efficiency and practicality could make the method useful in biorefineries, facilities designed to convert biological materials into fuels, chemicals, and other products.

The research also supports the broader goal of creating a circular economy, in which materials that would otherwise be thrown away are reused to generate additional value. This approach is particularly relevant as industries search for renewable fuel alternatives in sectors that are difficult to electrify, including heavy transportation.

By finding ways to make use of both the extracted oils and the remaining coffee grounds, the scientists hope to reduce waste while expanding the range of materials available for sustainable fuel production.

As Daniel Montané, another researcher involved in the study, explained, the goal is "to transform a typically underused waste product into various energy vectors and bio-based chemical products, and to reduce the environmental impact associated with its accumulation.".

The findings suggest that discarded coffee grounds could eventually become an important feedstock for producing renewable fuels and other valuable materials, turning a familiar source of everyday waste into a resource with multiple industrial uses.

Void/Breaker Review – Chaos Is The Point

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1020 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that many games tout impressive destruction systems under the hood, but few implement it as well as Void/Breaker.
  • Void/Breaker wastes no time getting a gun in your hand.
  • Industry observers note that this narrative framework supports the game’s roguelite structure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that many games tout impressive destruction systems under the hood, but few implement it as well as Void/Breaker. The ruin is visually spectacular, sure – who doesn’t love to watch buildings crumble because of your grenade or gravity-thrown explosives? But importantly, it’s a critical aspect of Void/Breaker’s roguelite design. Enemies caught beneath falling rubble become instantly staggered, and that’s your moment to kill. Grenades do this too, as do most items you throw at the hostile AI machinery trying to end your run, creating a vortex of shifting priorities as you dash, jump, and shoot at sequential staggered enemies in your sightlines. Countless weapon mods and permutations make fewer than a dozen weapons feel like hundreds in your arsenal, adding even more blissful chaos to the mix. Though it can be difficult at times, if you can see through the literal remains of your destruction, one of the year’s most engaging shooters awaits.

Void/Breaker wastes no time getting a gun in your hand. An AI voice in your head wants your help escaping a simulation where thousands of runners attempt to reach the end of multi-arena stages to defeat a boss. He asks that you simply follow the simulation’s commands; meanwhile, he uses the data you collect along the way to find new exits for you and him. The storytelling style is very reminiscent of Valve’s Portal. Something much larger is at play here, but it’s worth discovering for yourself.

Industry observers note that this narrative framework supports the game’s roguelite structure. Mechanically, however, you enter various themed digital stages, from liminal spaces to beaches to snow-capped cliffs and more, and attempt to survive. Most arenas consist of a couple of starkly white structures that your grenades and thrown explosives can topple (ideally onto waves of enemies below). Learning the language of Void/Breaker means constantly scanning your field of view for explosives and structures practically begging to come down, and then eyeing neon-green bars above enemies that tell you they’re staggered and ready for a quick kill. Developer Stubby Games throws plenty of wrenches into this formula, like armored foes and electrostatic enemies you must melee first, and elite bots that will have you on the back foot, but for the most part, Void/Breaker’s formula is “Break stuff, then kill.”.

The game emphasizes explosives and bringing buildings down, but your guns do most of the killing; you can only select one weapon per run. You choose from a pistol, shotgun, machine gun, sniper, and more, and each has its perks (though once I unlocked the SMG, I rarely picked anything else). There’s no sense overthinking your weapon, though, because the dozens of mods you pick up each run determine its effectiveness. As you pick up more schematics, the pool of mods you find in chests or drop from enemies expands, and soon your gun fires corrosive acid, electricity, fire, projectile missiles, and more. Not to mention, mods change how the gun fires, how much damage certain bullets do, recoil, accuracy, and just about any other stat you associate with firing a video game gun. Wild combinations are easy to create, and a unique mod-stacking mechanic that can double or triple effectiveness adds a light touch of puzzle design to this otherwise straight shooter.

Sources indicate that stubby Games smartly emphasizes player expression, never getting in the way of the zanier combinations available to players. The SMG I used to beat the final boss featured mods that made each bullet electric, shot missiles with each shot, covered each bullet in a destructive orb, and featured a ricochet perk that made each bullet bounce off walls and split into even more bullets. I’m thankful for mid-run saves because this SMG permutation, paired with an ability mod that let me throw infinite grenades for a limited time, filled my screen with so much destruction that the entire game crashed. I’d usually bemoan such a thing, but I couldn’t help but laugh. I pushed my PC to its limit with my on-screen chaos.

In a recent development, boss fights leave a little to be desired – I rarely died because of their simple bullet-hell arenas. Instead, most runs ended because, after bringing down every structure around me, I’d get so lost in the chaos that I wouldn't realize I was stuck in debris while enemies swarmed my location. As stunning as it is to see so much happening on screen, it can be hard to understand what is going on during the most chaotic moments.

In a recent development, between enemy-filled arenas en route to a stage’s end boss, you might find a shop to buy more mods, ominous obelisks with risk-reward propositions (gain a lot of health or lose half your health, for example), optional trials, and strange phenomena that transport you to different locations. These moments are quick breaks in between bouts of adrenaline-fueled shooter action that I always welcomed – enemies can be relentless, especially as upcoming types are introduced in each stage.

Industry observers note that the rest of the Void/Breaker package offers few genre surprises. You can upgrade various traits between runs, research newly introduced mod schematics to add to the random pool, purchase new weapons, and discover fun secrets. You can unlock shortcuts, glean in-world information from computer terminals, and hear intriguing dialogue barks from the AI partner who needs your help. It’s all standard stuff for the rogue genre, but if anything, its simplicity pushes you back to the meat and potatoes of this shooter.

Void/Breaker’s shorter runtime – I rolled credits at 12 hours – ensures nothing gets too repetitive in its roguelite structure, but an expansive endgame promises even more to engage with, like different run modifications you can enable to make an already chaotic shooter even more anarchic. I’ll certainly be running it back (again and again) to see what other disruptions I can bring to this AI-simulated adventure. It’s hard not to when destruction feels this good.

Before we dive into the Infinity Kingdom tier list, though, let me give you a few tips about the immortals, so you'll know exactly why I've ranked them the way I did. You can invest in anything (pretty much), but it will be a lot easier to just stick to a few good ones Investing in any hero will never be a waste once you gain access to the lab because you can choose to reborn them when they have fulfilled their purpose. However, it will be easier if you just stick to the right heroes from the get-go. Try to think ahead about what teams you want to use and which heroes will fit best. Stick to one troop when you're at the beginning At the very start, you want to stick to one troop. Boost that troop in every way that you can, and use it for all content. Always summon 10x times, never do individual summons Whenever you collect nine Philosopher's Stones, you will be able to summon 10 times. This is the best option you have, so hold onto your Philosopher's Stones whenever you can, because it will guarantee you one Elite or Epic unit within the 10 units that you pull. Join an Alliance and don't use your speedups until you've received help from your Alliance mates This feature is super key for upgrading your kingdom quickly, for a number of reasons. 10 Great Games That Defined The Xbox 360
